chapters.title: Foreword by Prof. A.K. John, Alias Al - Dayrani
chapters.html:
Foreword by Prof. A.K. John, Alias Al-Dayrani

All Praise is due to God, and to Him alone, the Provider of the worlds. Perfect and complete communication with God and peace are achieved through the best of all creatures, our Prophet Mohammad (cpth ﴿1﴾

whom God sent as a great mercy to the worlds; and also through his family, his companions and anyone who follows his guidance till the Day of Resurrection.

Everything in this universe has a reality which can be recognised through constant and serious contemplation. The most important thing for you as a creature is to know your Creator, the Almighty God, and communicate with Him. The easiest way of approaching that is through His Envoy (cpth) and the Holy Qur’an which was sent down by Al’lah, and in which man can find the absolute truth. By applying the Word of Al’lah, mankind will reach a high rank of spiritual perfection, become overwhelmed with Godly Light and, through their personal efforts, they will acquire a third eye, known as the heart’s eye.

Through this they will come to know God’s Purpose beyond His bringing them to this worldly life: they will recognise the great wisdom behind the creation of the vast universe, and will certainly be able to discriminate between truth and falsehood, virtue and vice, and good and evil. In addition, they will come to know that this worldly life serves as a school for all human beings whereby they will be rewarded and elevated by making every effort to carry out good deeds during their lifetime, seeking only God’s Satisfaction. They should proceed in this way, sacrificing their wealth, prestige and rest in order to reach communication with God whereby they will receive integrity, wellbeing and spiritual health in return. They know that such behaviour will bring them happiness, Paradise and God’s Favour and Reward in this life and in the life to come. They will see, therefore, that all their deeds are full of goodness and altruism to all creatures, and all their words serve as guidance in order to lead people towards virtue, happiness and God’s Perfections.

Few human beings, even those who are fair and sound of mind, think deeply about this universe: its order, its produce (fruits), and the multitude of gifts that Al’lah causes to flow upon them through it. However they will observe and witness all the Supreme Godly Attributes: the Great Creator, the Wise Innovator, the Omnipotent Steering God, the Compassionate, and the Merciful… and will fully realise His Mercy and Sympathy for us and for all the worlds, and that He, the Great and the Almighty, has created us for no purpose except to enjoy happiness.

And just as the Almighty’s Creation and Steering of this universe are perfectly arranged so that everything bears fruit and provides more and ever more with no aim but the happiness of mankind, it is the same concerning His Legislation and His Orders in His Holy Book, for they too are quite perfect. They will finally realise God’s Justice in this universe. As long as the Creator is One, the Provider is Single and the Steering God is Unique and Genius, then as a result of your profound thinking and searching you will come to the conclusion that all things are in the Power of Al’lah alone. So, too, as He has duly arranged the heavens according to His Perfection He has similarly ordered the earth and the relationship between all creatures in accordance with His Good Names. Thus, the universe presents the perfect image: no chaos, no wrongful deviation and no failure. Everything within it, from the minutest atom to the greatest galaxy, are entirely organised within very strict discipline and under close and full control.

That was our pledge to Him the Almighty, that is, to be guided by His Legislation in this worldly life in order to achieve real happiness, and not to be unjust to ourselves or ignorant of the happiness that Al’lah has prepared for us in this life and in the life to come.

Dazzling fruits result from putting His Statute into action, for He is the Creator of mankind and He knows best about the law that will lead to happiness in this life and in the Afterlife, starting with the happiness of mankind and ending with that of all other creatures.

In this book we shall discuss some facts concerning spiritual knowledge, some rules which control the spirit and everything that is linked to it. In addition, we shall discuss certain issues which are the subject of much dispute: we shall clarify the truth concerning these and make the correct rules available to you.

We shall tackle the origin of the first Creation, where we were in the prematerial world, and why and how we came to this lower life. Some concealed realities will also be dealt with: such as who the noble angels are; who the noble Prophets (ptt ﴿2﴾

are, and how they are chosen to be Prophets. We shall also discuss our great father Adam (pth ﴿3﴾

about whom there are many false beliefs such as: he, along with our mother Eve, were ungrateful parents and they were the reason that we were expelled from Paradise because of their first mistake. Further, we shall talk in some detail about fate, Godly Justice, the first devil and how he became a devil, and how we can deliver ourselves from him. These rules and truths are based on sound logic and evidence and taken from the science and knowledge of a great twentieth century scholar. This great and eminent scholar is Mohammad Amin Sheikho (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) who received a wonderful Divine revelation, so that you and we may benefit from his holy, high and sublime knowledge of the Words of the Almighty God, the Holy Qur’an.

chapters.title: Introduction, THE REASON GOD CREATED ADAM AND EVE
chapters.html:
Inspiration and Questions

Throughout the different stages of their life, everyone will certainly query many things. From early childhood, when perception and recognition first arise, they ask questions about whatever they see. For instance, when a child looks at the sky, it may ask, why do the stars shine? Where does the sun go to at night? Where do the clouds come from? – along with a multitude of other questions.

The more a child’s awareness grows, the more the questions will increase, through which it endeavours to gain knowledge of this universe. This continues until the child’s enquiries exceed the limits of the material universe, and it shifts to another, greater field of questioning when it asks about the Creator of this universe, where is He? Why did He create it? This is because inquisitiveness is intrinsic to the human mind. One wonders, what is the reality of these questions? Where do they come from? One might say that they seem to arise from the very spirit of an inquisitive child. However, the truth is something different, for all of these questions come from Al’lah and are addressed to the child, and indeed to all children, by angels through the means of a hidden sound that is emitted from the very depths of this young spirit, so as to encourage and impel it to investigate the aim and purpose for which it was created.

If human beings are persistent in pursuing the reason for their existence, through their enquiries and the ever-changing circumstances they face in their life, they will come to understand the fact that they are more than just flesh and blood. For no sooner do they enjoy the pleasure of some base, earthly desire than this pleasure comes to an end, only to be followed by spiritual emptiness. This is followed by feelings of boredom, dissatisfaction and ennui that creep into their hearts and overwhelm them. They are then compelled to look for whatever might take their mind away from such a miserable situation. Eventually they often find no other choice but to resort to alcohol and drugs, hoping to forget their emotional suffering. This then leads to further dilemma regarding the purpose of this precisely established cosmic system, and for whom it was created.

The questions are numerous, Who supplies this wonderful universe, directs it and arranges its affairs? Who supplies us, directs us and arranges our affairs? Where is He Who controls it and controls us and to Whom everything, in the end, will return? For what purpose was humankind created? Can these questions really be answered? Were we created only to enjoy food, drink and marriage, or to fulfil other earthly desires?

Surely this cannot be the reason you were created or the purpose of your life, because all the creatures and animals that are inferior to you also achieve these same aims. Moreover, they surpass you in achieving these aims and enjoying such desires. If the purpose of our existence is thought to be the enjoyment of eating and drinking, we could say that a cow, for example, may gorge huge quantities of food with great relish and enjoyment, so no matter what, or how much a person tries to eat, can they expect to do better than the cow in this natural physical activity?

If matrimony were our sole purpose on this earth, we would say that birds far exceed humans in this regard, for any cock can have numerous hens. In addition, birds have plumage and feathers of unequalled beauty. For example, the peacock has been given such a marvellous appearance that it would have no need of the knowledge of humankind and their textile factories and manmade clothes to keep them warm and adorn their bodies.

However God has allowed mankind to reach this complex life and the urbanity of civilisation ﴿4﴾

because it is what they want for themselves, and He has given them freedom of choice. In fact, it is not what Al’lah wishes for them, for He would have created the human race to be carefree, as free as the beautiful, captivating birds that need make no effort; and human beings would not drive themselves to exhaustion, but would ignore the burdens of this tiring and complex life. Besides, He would have provided for humans in a similar way to those beautiful birds, which are so appealing to people’s minds and hearts, for in the early morning they fly off hungry and return to their nests at night, fully satisfied; and all this is achieved without making any great effort or doing any tiring work.

So what can be the purpose of our coming to this lower life?

It was said that Al’lah created us to worship Him.

The evidence is in His Saying, ‘

I created jinn-kind and man-kind only to worship Me.

’ ﴿5﴾

This is correct, but for some people this statement will likely create a further question, why, then, did Al’lah create us and order us to worship Him? Is it because He is God Who should have servants to serve Him? Does the Almighty need us to adore Him, even though He is the Self-Existent One Who provides for everyone without requiring provision from anyone? Has He created us and commanded us to worship Him simply to make us experience all sorts of difficulties in following His Orders and avoiding acts that are forbidden to us?

Surely, the true purpose was none of the above, but must be far greater than these, because the Perfection and Supreme Attributes of God are incompatible with such aims. He does not need us; nor does He need our worship. He continues by saying, ‘

I want no provision from them, nor do I want them to feed Me.

’ ﴿6﴾

In the holy saying, Al’lah says, ‘

Oh, My servants! Had the first, the last, the jinn, and the humans of you stood up on one level, asking Me for alms, and had I given everyone what they demanded, that would not have decreased what I have, except to the same degree that the sea may have a lack when a sewing needle enters it.

’ ﴿7﴾

So the question still remains unanswered and, again, we ask ourselves, why were we created? And there is yet a further question, has the Almighty predestined some people to be happy and others to live a miserable life?

There are many unanswered questions for us to ponder dear reader, and to address these questions we shall undertake an interesting literary journey back through the ages and arrive in due course at the time which preceded our coming to this universe and life on earth. Through this we may understand what and where we were, and how we came to this world. We shall read about the amazing Godly realities of the world of first Creation, that is, the world of

al-Azal

; furthermore, our thirst for this knowledge will be quenched with the indisputable answers that this book presents to every possible question. We shall see how Godly Justice manifested itself throughout the whole of Creation when God (Glory to His Names) offered to all the spirits He had created in the pre-material world to undertake the Trust: ﴿8﴾

this was a fair offer carrying no obligation whatsoever.

However, the majority of creatures were afraid and refused to accept it, with the exception of a few spirits that accepted to participate in this daring venture that was offered to them. From these few God formed human beings and jinns.

The Grand God wanted only what is good for His Creation, therefore He brought them into existence and then sent them to this earth to live this worldly life. He granted them cravings and desires to help them to achieve an honourable purpose by means of which they would become able to approach Him and enjoy happiness. Unfortunately, mankind wasted and ultimately lost much of this chance of true happiness by neglecting the Trust.

However, they now have a second chance, but if they fail to understand the reason why they came to this world that chance of true and everlasting happiness will be lost forever.

In his book, the eminent scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho discussed the great question which has long baffled religious scholars and ordinary people alike and was invariably misunderstood by them all. This question concerns the true story about the descent of our father and mother, Adam and Eve (ptt), from the glorious Garden they were in, to the earthly world of daily exertion and difficulties.

This issue was a point of disagreement among all people of the various Scriptures, including Christians, Jews and others. They all stated that our pure parents had made an error of judgement and that it was their father Adam (pth) who caused his offspring to live in unhappiness; they accused Adam and Eve (ptt) of disobedience and ingratitude towards God although they certainly did not deserve this criticism. Our brothers, the Christians, agreed with this point of view, for they believe that our master Jesus (pth) was sent to this world for the sole reason of atoning for their sins, and to make amends for the original sin committed by Adam (pth) by sacrificing his own soul. But the great scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho has brought us the truth about this issue and revealed the true story about the descent of our master Adam (pth) and his wife Eve to this worldly life, and their children later on.

This book begins with a comprehensive and concise study of all that took place in the pre-material world of

al-Azal

and at the beginning of the Creation of this earthly world; it then continues by guiding us towards the only way which can help us to ascertain the truth, and to attain heart vision of these facts of which most people are ignorant. This way is simply to look into the universe and study its miraculous signs, with the aim of searching for the Provider; for once a human recognises their Provider they will have their heart’s eye (third eye) opened and will witness endless realities.

God’s Aim in bringing creatures into being is so that the people on this earth may become acquainted with their Maker, and accept to do good, charitable deeds once they believe in God and His Envoy (cpth) and obtain insight through their third eye (heart’s eye). This insight will enable them to differentiate between goodness and evil, and thereby offer up their good deeds to the Almighty. By following this course a person will live happily in this life, and after their death they will meet their Provider with a pure heart by virtue of the benevolent deeds they offered to His Creation during their lifetime. As a consequence, they will live in eternal bliss in His Paradise.

For further clarity about this indisputable fact, we shall continue by shedding light on the world of first Creation (

al-Azal

world) and the events that preceded our coming to this material world.

chapters.title: Chapter One, THE PRE - MATERIAL WORLD
chapters.html:
Chapter One, THE PRE-MATERIAL WORLD

The World of First Creation

Firstly we shall summarise what was introduced previously: Al’lah existed but nothing existed with Him. There were no jinns, no human beings, no animals or birds, nor other creatures of any type; there was no earth, no sky, no sun, no moon, nor stars. Whatever one might think to the contrary, there is no denying that He has always been the First, for His Existence has no beginning, and nothing came before Him.

This fact can never change. Additionally, He is Almighty, Great and Immense, and whatever one might say, He is not only Great but the Greatest, and not only Immense but the most Immense. His Greatness is without limit and without end. And He is the Last, for nothing will come after Him. The noble verse denotes, ‘He is the First and the Last, the Explicit and the Implicit, and He is Omniscient of everything.’ ﴿9﴾

chapters.title: The Purpose Of Our Creation
chapters.html:
Being the Origin of all virtues and many other additional Attributes, such as Generosity, Charity, Compassion, Favour, Tenderness, Beauty, Grandeur and Majesty that indicate His Perfection, God wanted to create beings so that they could experience His Compassion, and so that He could engulf them in His Benevolence and Charity. One could say that God wanted to create beings in order to enfold them within His Supreme Spirit so that they could enjoy being witness to His Beauty and become absorbed in observing His Perfection. God says in a holy saying (

hadith qudsi

), ‘

I was a hidden treasure, and then I liked to be known, and so I created Creation and acquainted them with Me, so that they knew Me through Me.

’ ﴿10﴾

In analysing the meaning of this holy saying we say that ‘treasure’ is something that is both beautiful and valuable. The treasure referred to is the great Godly Beauty and the supreme Perfection which were ‘hidden’, and unknown to anyone. The phrase ‘

I liked to be known

’ refers to the Generosity and Kindness of Almighty God. It was the Aim of the most Generous (Al’lah) to expose and display His Generosity and Kindness. ‘

And so I created Creation

’ refers to the purpose of our creation, which is the enjoyment of observing the Godly Beauty, and becoming engrossed in watching that endless Perfection. It indicates that God created the whole of Creation in the world called

al-Azal

, the pre-existent world. ‘

I acquainted them with Me

’ means that He showed them His Greatness and Benevolence in creating them. ‘

They knew Me through Me

’ indicates that by looking at themselves they could know Him, after which they could enjoy watching this Glorious Treasure as they gazed upon a part of His Beauty and Perfection.

chapters.title: Godly Justice and the Equality of Creation in the Pre - material World
chapters.html:
Godly Justice and the Equality of Creation in the Pre-material World

When Creation was first brought into existence by Almighty God in the pre-existent world known as al- Azal it was made up of abstract spirits having no shape or substance. All of Creation was of a single type and composition with no difference between them. And they basked in the sublime pleasure of experiencing the great Godly Beauty, the Glorious Treasure. Then God created life as we now know it within this existence. This includes our earthly planet and all its creatures, and all else that now exists on this earth or in the universe, such as mankind, animals, the angels and jinns (ghostlike demons), the sun, moon and stars; in fact, the list is endless.

Before continuing with this important issue, it is first necessary to understand what is meant by the words ‘abstract spirits’, or more properly speaking, learn about the elements of human composition. This is explained as follows:

chapters.title: Components of the Human Being
chapters.html:
The human being is made up of three components: the spirit, the soul and the physical body, all of which were created by God. In order to know about each of these elements we will start with an explanation of the human spirit as it is the most important; it is the main component of this Creation and the reason for the existence and creation of this worldly life as well as of the great universe.

The Spirit

The spirit is the subtle consciousness of man. It is a Godly Light and its centre is in the chest. Its rays spread to all parts of the body through the nerves. This spirit, confined to the body, is aware of its surroundings through the five senses. It sees with the eyes, hears with the ears, smells with the nose, feels and touches with the skin and tastes with the tongue. The tongue is also used to express ideas and thoughts through speech.

For example, if one stands by the seashore, simply watching the sea and becoming aware of the constant movement of the waves, one will naturally be led to feelings of awe and reverence for it. These sentiments come from the ‘spirit’. If we see someone dear to us whose hand is bleeding from a bad wound, we feel sorry for him, and sympathise with him. This pain and grief also come from the ‘spirit’. If we hear that one of our dear relatives has returned safely from a long journey, we are happy at the news. These feelings of pleasure and happiness are possible because of the ‘spirit’. Thus, the spirit is the essential component of man. It glorifies and submits, grieves, enjoys, rejoices, feels contented or is annoyed and angry, and suffers. It is the very centre of our existence.

The spirit is the being which directs itself towards the Creator and communicates with Him. It is the spirit which bows and prostrates itself to Him, glorifies and reveres, thanks and praises Him, turns to Him in repentance and makes covenants with Him. The spirit is always addressed directly in the Qur’an. God says, ‘

Oh, spirit in rest and satisfaction!

’ ﴿11﴾

The spirit is charged with following the unswerving path, for God says, ‘

Behold the spirit and [the Potency] that formed it to perfection, and inspired it with knowledge of its immorality and its piety: successful are those who purify it, and unsuccessful are those who corrupt it!

’ ﴿12﴾

Moreover, the spirit is eternal, which means that it could never cease to exist. It experiences death, but this experience differs from one spirit to another according to its state when leaving the body. God says, ‘

Every spirit shall have a taste of death: in the end to Us shall you be brought back

.’ ﴿13﴾

The sinful spirit will receive painful treatment on Doomsday in order to be cured. God says, ‘

Lest a spirit should [then] say, “Ah! Woe is me for having neglected to be near to God, and was but among those who mocked!”

’ ﴿14﴾

The spirit that believes will enjoy remaining in Paradise, and will not want to leave. God says, ‘

Therein shall you have all that your spirits shall desire.

’ ﴿15﴾

The word ‘spirit’ is derived from the Arabic words for ‘magnificent value’. At the moment of death we cease to exist only in terms of our physical, external body, and this will be recreated on the Day of Resurrection. The Arabic words for the Day of Resurrection mean ‘the day of rising’. It is called so because bodies will rise again on this day to be placed inside the spirits, contrary to the present life where the body surrounds the spirit. To clarify the position of the centre of the spirit, God states in the Holy Qur’an, ‘

Say, “I proudly seek refuge in the Provider of oblivious humankind, the King of oblivious humankind, the Steering God of oblivious humankind, from the evil of the sneaking whisperer, who withdraws [when a person resorts to God]: he who whispers evil in the chests of oblivious humankind, through jinns and oblivious humankind.”

’ ﴿16﴾

In another Fortress ﴿17﴾

He says, ‘

And truly your Provider knows all that their chests hide as well as all that they reveal.

’ ﴿18﴾

And He (Glory to Him) says, ‘

Say, “Whether you hide what is in your chests or reveal it, Al’lah is Aware of it.”

’ ﴿19﴾

It is clear from the holy verses that the centre of the spirit is located in the human chest, but how does it spread throughout the body? The spirit spreads through the nerves, and when the nerves are anaesthetised the spirit retreats from the area that is numbed; the patient will feel no pain even if one of his limbs is amputated, because the spirit is not then present at the point of anaesthesia. God says in the Holy Qur’an, ‘

It is Al’lah Who takes back the spirits when dead and those who have not died, during their sleep. He takes back those on whom He has passed the decree of death, but He sends the rest for an appointed term.

’ ﴿20﴾

As the patient’s spirit leaves their body because of the anaesthesia the spirit also leaves the body because the body is asleep, and a ray of light remains to supervise the body. The soul remains in the body which moves, and the heart beats, but the person sleeping is not aware of anything.

We shall now turn to the women who cut their hands in the story of Joseph (Yusuf) the Prophet (pth). In the Holy Qur’an God says, ‘

When she heard of their cunning [their malicious talk], she sent for them and prepared a banquet; she gave each of them a knife and said to Joseph, “Come out before them.” When they saw him, they did glorify him and [in their amazement] cut their hands, and they said, “God is blameless! No mortal is this! This is none but a pure [noble] angel.”

’ ﴿21﴾

The women cut their hands because their spirits were astonished at the sight of Joseph’s beauty. In this incident, the spirits left their bodies and headed for the Prophet Joseph (pth). They were mesmerised at the sight of his beauty, then became oblivious to all pain and felt nothing when they cut their hands. This came about because their conscious selves left their bodies, flowing outwards through their sense of sight, until they became detached from the other senses, just as happens in the case of anaesthesia when one loses consciousness.

One may notice that a man who is quarrelling fails to feel something that may happen to him during a quarrel, even the stab of a knife. That is because his spirit is occupied with a different concern during the event. However, after it returns to its body, the spirit suffers pain that it did not feel when the injury was first inflicted. The spirit, therefore, travels, but it is the sought-after, good kind of spiritual travelling ﴿22﴾

that takes place when the spirit is allowed to flow freely during its communication with God: when it is directed towards

al-Ka’ba ﴿23﴾

so as to meet the noble spirit of the Envoy (cpth) and to couple with it by means of a bond of love and appreciation. The spirit then rises in this company through the Godly Light where it observes the Godly Perfections and Lights that cause it to become absorbed in supreme Godly Bliss until it adores Him, the Almighty.

This occurs because it has seen a part of His Perfection and Majesty. This is prayer, the real communication with God, which should be performed frequently; ﴿24﴾

for Moslems, this is five times a day. We see that during this communication the body does not move, but the spirit alone rises through the worlds of Godly Lights and Perfection.

To clarify the way in which the spirit travels, we give the following example: let us suppose that there is a man who, while asleep, dreams that he is by the seashore eating good, tasty food, having fun, laughing and enjoying himself, moving from one beautiful place to another that is even more beautiful. We wonder: exactly which part of him feels the happiness and joy? Which part of him is moved? In fact, it is his conscious self, his ‘spirit’ that is moved. The body lies in bed, its heart beating in the chest that moves up and down rhythmically, and blood flows through his veins. The man’s body remains still whilst it is his spirit which travels to the land of dreams as he sleeps.

The Soul

The soul is the support with the Godly Light and flows into the blood. Its centre in the body is the physical heart, and it is the power that animates all systems and cells of the body. It moves through the body and provides its nourishment, thus the life of the body is dependent on it. It is the administrative power of the purpose, requirements, demands and desires of the spirit. The soul is under the command of the spirit that moves within the nerves by sending its rays through the nervous system. The spirit directs and controls all the voluntary organs, and the involuntary ones such as the heart and lungs, over which man has no control. The souls of human beings, animals and all other living creatures are the same, but the Prophets and Envoys (ptt) have sacred souls; that is, they have no impurities or base purpose whatsoever because the spirits of these people have not been contaminated by the worldly marks of life and its evils. That is why these souls remain virtuous, pure and sacred, and therefore they express nothing but goodness and perfection. Wherever they settle, goodness, bliss, blessings, happiness and the delightful, eternal Beatitude of Al’lah spread over all those who approach them, and all who surround them.

In a prophetic saying the Envoy Mohammad (cpth ﴿25﴾

explained the soul and how its rays are carried through the body by the blood. He said, ‘

Satan flows through a son of Adam like the blood circulates in the body.

’ ﴿26﴾

This is referred to in the noble verse which states, ‘

They ask you concerning the soul, say, “The soul is at the Command of my Provider. It is only too little omniscience that is got to you [human beings].”

’ ﴿27﴾

‘

They ask you concerning the soul,

’ – Actually they asked him about it just to frustrate and defeat him, but God the Almighty answered, ‘

Say’ – (to them) ‘The soul is at the Command of my Provider.

’ – The words ‘

the Command of my Provider

’ indicate Providence and show that Godly Support spreads throughout existence.

The life and energy of a human being, as well as of all living things, including the smallest insects, the biggest animals and every species of plant, are all only possible with the Support of God, the Almighty. Everything moves with His Provision and by His Command. If God withdrew His Support, that is the soul, from all creatures, everything would become motionless, lifeless, and cease to exist. ﴿28﴾

The existence of the soul in Creation can be compared to the electric current which powers so many machines: if the power is disconnected, the machines will stop functioning. Similarly, the soul is poured into the heart of the human being and its rays flow into the blood, which then carries nourishment and oxygen to all parts of the body, and removes the waste products by the natural process of physical elimination.

In the Qur’anic verse, the phrase ‘

is at the Command of my Provider

’ refers to this supply to the heart and the blood which completes the circle of life. If that supply is stopped the entire physical body will become motionless and lifeless. The meaning of the word ‘soul’ as mentioned in the Holy Qur’an differs according to its relevance in the verses.

The soul, in general, is the life support which can be either for the physical heart or for the core of the spirit, as the Almighty says in the noble verse, ‘

Raised high above ranks, [He is] the Owner of the beautiful Godly Revelation: at His Command, He lets the soul descend upon whom He pleases of His servants so as to warn of the Day of Meeting.

’ ﴿29﴾

The soul, in this holy verse, means the Godly Light and spiritual Divine life poured into the hearts of the Prophets and Envoys (ptt) and whoever is with them and follows them as did the noble companions and followers of our master Mohammad (cpth). This confirms what we have already stated. God’s Saying is, ‘

The Messiah Jesus, son of Mary, was no more than an Envoy of Al’lah and His Word which He gave to Mary, and was a soul created by Him.

’ ﴿30﴾

This soul, mentioned above, is nothing more than that Godly Provision of great light and sublime revelation which Al’lah provided to the honourable spirit of our master Jesus (pth) through our master Gabriel (pth).

Generally, the soul supplies life: it is either the life of the heart of the spirit as stated in the verses mentioned above, or the lifeforce of the physical body; and it is dedicated to all mankind and to all creatures without discrimination. The phrase ‘

at the Command of my Provider

’ indicates clearly that the Godly Providence which the body needs in order to be alive is at the Command of Almighty God; that is to say, nothing could exist without His Commands, which is clear in His Sublime Names: the All-Living and the Sustainer. Life could not exist without God and His great Supplying. After explaining that to them he (cpth) replied, ‘

It is only too little omniscience that has got to you [human beings].

’ The statement ‘

it is only too little omniscience that has got to you

’ does not refer to the Envoy of God but to those who ask, because in the original Arabic it is in the plural form. If it had meant the Prophet (cpth) it would have been in the singular. He is the speaker; this means: say to them, Mohammad, ‘

It is only too little omniscience that has got to you

’, meaning the challengers.

In brief: we say that man’s thorough contemplation of all aspects of this universe will lead them to the undeniable fact that there is a great Creator and a wise Disposer. As a result their path will become straight, and this straightness will generate good deeds and trust in God’s Satisfaction with them. These actions and trust become man’s means to get closer to God, and they will acquire perfection from their Creator by communicating with Him (prayer). Then they will also love those who are perfect, and the master of perfection, the Envoy Mohammad (cpth). In this way their spirit will accompany that of the Envoy (cpth) who is always close to Al’lah, and they will witness, with their third eye, the luminous Provision of God prevailing in everything in existence. This prevalent luminous Provision is what we call the ‘soul’.

From the above, it is clear to us that there is a great difference and contrast between the ‘soul’ and the ‘spirit’. In fact, this was not clarified by anyone since the master of Prophets (cptt ﴿31﴾

and until the great man, Mohammad Amin Sheikho, did so. At the time scientists and philosophers alike were greatly astonished by this phenomenon.

The Body

The body, which consists of flesh, nerves, bones and blood et cetera, is the garment of the spirit, its vessel, and its means to achieve all of its needs: its demands, aims, deviations or virtues and distinguished good deeds. It is the body that will speak out against the spirit on the Day of Resurrection and will bear witness to its choices and the deeds it has performed. In this respect, the Almighty says, ‘

But when they refuse to come into it [the Fire], their hearing, their sight and their skins will bear witness against them as to all their deeds.

’ ﴿32﴾

So, concerning man’s body when it bears witness against them on Resurrection Day, this is nothing other than evidence that the spirit will be separated from the body and it will be responsible for all its deeds, and will account for them. It will then enter either Paradise or Fire. However, the body is simply subservient to the spirit as is everything else in Creation: it bears no responsibility and will not be held to account.

The body is the physical structure of the human being. Originally, God created it from soil, which is part of the makeup of the material body, and the elements of the earth, so that it will be in harmony with those elements. The body obtains its nourishment from those elements and depends on them for sustenance.

Within the body, the soul spreads to generate its life and power in its various forms.

To elucidate further we shall clarify the outcome of each component of the human being after death:

1-

The body

is buried in the ground.

2-

The soul

is taken back by the angel of death, as referred to in the following verse, ‘

Say, “The angel of death who has been given charge of you will take you back [your souls]; then to your Provider you shall all return.”

’ ﴿33﴾

The angel of death removes the soul from the body as soon as its earthly physical life comes to an end, that is, when the lifetime term appointed to a person has expired, according to the Will of the Almighty. At this time Godly Support for this soul stops. So, the soul is the Godly Supply which keeps each person alive in this life. This can be compared to the electricity that enables machines to function in order to produce lighting, goods, transportation, and all other items considered necessary for contemporary life. The important thing is that the soul has no feelings, consciousness, senses or awareness, but rather it supplies the body with life and power: the soul is not the conscious self which expresses its feelings and speaks with others, for this is how we describe the spirit.

3-

The spirit

is, as we have seen, the conscious feeling and perceptive self. It senses, enjoys and appreciates things, it suffers and it expresses its ideas and thoughts.

After death, the soul is withdrawn by the angel of death, and the body becomes still and lifeless. It is then that God takes back the spirit which has experienced death, and after the body has died the spirit leaves its current state in this present life, for in the grave the state of the spirit changes. God says, ‘

Every spirit shall have a taste of death.

’ ﴿34﴾

Here we clarify that death does not mean the cessation of the spirit’s existence, but the separation of the spirit from the body. Until this moment, the body had been the means for the spirit to carry out all of its deeds, so death is the cessation of these deeds. One should note that the verb ‘to die’ in Arabic means ‘to cease’, and does not indicate that the spirit no longer exists.

It is the spirit (rather than the soul) that is always addressed in the Qur’an and is responsible for following the straight, unswerving path. It resides in blissful Heavens or in Hell during the interval between the moment of death and Doomsday. God says in the Holy Qur’an, ‘

Oh, spirit in rest and satisfaction! Return to your Provider, well-pleased and well-pleasing. Enter into My servants, and enter My Paradise.

’ ﴿35﴾

The spirit is the core of the human being and the centre of their existence, while the body and the soul are the means to achieve their inclinations and desires whether they be high or low, in this lower life. The spirit is taken back by Al’lah, whereas the soul is taken back by the angel of death, and this is the clear difference between the spirit and the soul. Al’lah takes back the spirits during their sleep; that is, He takes back the conscious self, so that a person’s senses and physical feelings are inactivated while they are asleep. Nevertheless, the body remains alive while the soul is poured upon it, imbuing life into it, and causing the heart to beat. When Al’lah wants them to wake up, He sends their spirit back again, ‘

It is He Who takes back your spirits by night, and knows what you have done by day.

’ ﴿36﴾

When we die, Al’lah takes back the spirit with all its rays, and it does not then return to its body until the Day of Resurrection. This is the day on which life is breathed into the bodies again, ‘It is Al’lah Who takes back the spirits when dead and those who have not died, during their sleep. He takes back those on whom He has passed the decree of death, but He sends the rest for an appointed term. Surely, there are signs in this for thinking people.’ ﴿37﴾

To summarise: the spirit is in the Hands of the Compassionate by night, and He directs it according to what is appropriate to its state. It is the same after death, when the spirit is either captive in the tomb, occupied with its own pain and great loss, or dwells in one of the gardens of Paradise where it enjoys an elevated state of being close to God that it has been granted because of its love for the Almighty. This will ensue according to the good deeds it has to offer from its time spent on earth, ‘

Each spirit is the hostage of its own deeds, except the benevolent ones who offered good deeds: they are in paradises wondering.

’ ﴿38﴾

The Mind and Thought

In order to derive maximum benefit from this topic, and before proceeding further, we shall clarify what is meant by the ‘mind’.

Firstly, however, we shall differentiate between ‘mind’ and ‘thought’ because throughout the ages mankind has failed to make any proper distinction between them due to either their lack of understanding or their alienation from the source of true knowledge, namely: the Noble Qur’an. They sometimes say ‘thought’ and at other times ‘mind’ without clarifying the difference between them.

The Mind

The mind is a spiritual quality that becomes attached to the spirit. When the spirit assimilates a certain fact which then becomes linked to it, the spirit becomes distinguished and characterised by this; this, in turn, becomes a mind. The spiritual concepts are everything that becomes a mind for the spirit. The spirit is like a mirror. When it directs itself towards something, this thing becomes imprinted on the spirit. The spirit is originally a pure, blank surface but when something is imprinted on it and it becomes preoccupied by that thing, this thing is then called ‘mind’. The mind is spiritual; thought is cerebral; the soul is dynamic; and the body is a mount and a container for them all. When the spirit wishes for something and is completely truthful in pursuing it, it directs its radiation to the brain which acts accordingly and an imprint is created. This imprint on the spirit is called ‘mind’.

The spirit has a radiation field which travels like the rays of the sun, but at a far greater speed. If you are honest, true to God and loyal to His Envoy (cpth), you will access a ray to eternity, and also to

al-Azal

, the pre-material world. The spirit reaches this state spiritually before reaching it physically, ﴿39﴾

and this also becomes a mind for the spirit. When the spirit fully contemplates death and believes in it, it will reach into the Hereafter and observe what happens there. Those who see by the light of their hearts and spirits, as did the Envoy Mohammad (cpth), those people are the companions of the Prophets (ptt), the true, the martyrs, and the ones who have the ability to do good deeds. Those people are good company, and the best example is the noble companions of Prophet Mohammad (cpth).

Mankind and animals had acquired specific mind prematerially in the world of

al-Azal ﴿40﴾

which Al’lah imprinted on the pages of all spirits before their coming to this world to carry out their missions to perfection. God says in the Noble Qur’an, ‘

Pharaoh said [to our master Moses and Aaron], “Who then, Oh Moses, is the Provider of you?” He said, “Our [his and Aaron’s] Provider is He Who gave everything its Creation, then gave guidance to it.”

’ ﴿41﴾

And another of His Sayings (Glory to His Names) is, ‘

Make [people’s spirits] glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High, Who has created [everything] and proportioned [it] well, Who has estimated [a livelihood] and guided them [to it].

’ ﴿42﴾

This mind acquired in

al-Azal

is also referred to in the noble verse, ‘

Who has taught by printing.

’ ﴿43﴾

The word ‘printing’ here refers to writing. In the Arabic language, for example, we talk about the ‘printing’ of a government minister, which means that when a minister writes a directive related to his department, this directive will become law. Therefore, when the minister’s statements are printed on paper, what he has written is put into effect. The word ‘printing’ reported in this noble verse refers to what Al’lah has imprinted on the pages of the spirits, the instincts He has put there, and the desires He placed there in the

al-Azal

world; for each creature has a special nature, and each has appropriate desires.

Let us take the suckling infant as an example: who guides it to its mother’s breast from the first moment that it is born? As soon as it leaves its mother’s womb, it moves its lips and they are ready to suck. So, too, as the duckling leaves its egg it runs to the water and swims with amazing skill and mastery. And there are endless further examples of creatures large and small who, immediately after birth, are able to walk or fly in order to find the sustenance they need. Who taught the infant to suckle as soon as it comes into this world? Who guided all creatures, great or small, to immediately seek out the nourishment they require to survive and grow?

It is the Potency of the Great Creator, the Wise and the All- Knowing.

On the surface of each spirit He imprinted whatever suits its particular way of life and what it requires in order to achieve this; therefore one finds that every creature is guided innately by the instincts Al’lah implanted in its spirit. In this way its life is established, its continuity is ensured and its happiness is achieved without the need for it to be shown the way. These instincts and desires which are implanted within the spirits are what show every creature how to proceed in this earthly existence. Had it not been for this imprint all Creation would have remained confused, directionless, incapable of performing any task, wanting nothing and therefore being guided toward nothing.

We could say, then, that teaching is figuratively carried out by the means of ‘printing’, that is, the teaching of all Creation in how to proceed in this life truly arises from what was written with the Hand of the Wise, the All-Knowing, on each page of every spirit. Glory to Him Who has motivated every creature and given them these desires to prompt them to enjoy the pleasures of existence and to live a happy life on this earth. This is the inspired mind: that is, what has been imprinted on the spirit of each creature since

al-Azal

, the world of spirits, in order to perform their tasks. The animal comes and goes in this life according to the impression that is stamped on it, and it cannot change its function. The human being is the only creature who has the ability to change and modify, to make new imprints, and to perceive new things in this lifetime.

The mind of man is achieved on two levels:

1-

Awareness that comes from our own experience or from what we learn from other people. This awareness depends on how things appear to be.

2-

An awareness of the deeper reality that comes directly from God, and which leads to the attainment of certainty and knowing without doubt what is right and true; as the Almighty God has ordered us in the Holy Qur’an saying, ‘No, indeed! If you only attain knowledge of certainty, you shall surely see Hell-fire.’ ﴿44﴾

The extent to which the mind is achieved on the first level depends on the truthfulness and determination of the spirit and its advance towards the thing it desires. We will give you an example: a man faces difficulties when first learning how to drive a car and will use all his senses to focus on the task at hand. Finally, with practice and determination, everything becomes very easy for him. Soon he will be seen driving while seemingly absorbed in talking to others in the car, or listening to the radio; but without any additional effort or particular concentration, he stops at red traffic lights, starts at the green lights and avoids accidents.

Let us suppose that someone has learned to swim and he falls accidentally into a pool or river. Before he is fully aware of what has happened, his arms and legs will move automatically to bring him up to the surface of the water and prevent him from drowning. All this happens even before his thought process or his will start to work: this is the mind. His spirit is programmed to swim and it applies this knowledge unconsciously.

In regards to becoming fully aware of the facts in one’s mind, a light is needed that is stronger than the physical lights that we can see, such as the natural light of the sun and the moon, or the manufactured light supplied by electricity and other sources.

It is the Light of Almighty God that is needed. However, this depends on many things, such as whether man follows the right path, their truthfulness with their Provider, and their obedience in practising the Orders of God which they have heard about from His Envoys (ptt). Therefore, in many of the Qur’anic verses (ayahs) we see that God tells His noble Envoys (ptt) to inform His servants about His Message, calling them ‘

those who become fully aware.

’

So, the mind is what the spirit perceives and contains. In order for the spirit to absorb and achieve what is necessary man should direct himself towards that which their spirit should absorb; and their mind will then become equivalent to the level of their determination and seriousness. For example, at school, we find that the student who pays full and careful attention to his teacher, and is interested in the lesson, will understand what he has been taught and will retain the information. Meanwhile, the distracted students who do not care about the details or the teacher’s explanation will remember little of the lesson.

We understand from this that the mind is not fully utilised without profound, contemplative thought and this is stated in many verses (ayahs) of the Holy Qur’an where the phrase ‘

those who think

’ is always followed by the phrase ‘

those who become fully aware.

’ God says, ‘

And it is He Who provided the earth and set there on mountains standing firm as anchors, and [flowing]rivers: and fruit of every type He made in pairs, two and two. He caused the night to veil the day. Behold! Truly, in these things there are signs for those who think. And in the earth are tracts [diverse though neighbouring], and gardens of vines and plants, and palm trees - growing similar and dissimilar: watered with the same water. Yet some of them We make more excellent than others, preferable to eat. Behold! Truly, in these things there are signs for those who become fully aware.

’ ﴿45﴾

In another Fortress, God says, ‘

With it He produces for you plants, olives, date-palms, grapes and every type of fruit. Truly, in this is a sign for those who think. He has made subject to you the night and the day, the sun and the moon; and the stars are in subjection, by His Command. Truly in these are signs for men who become fully aware.

’ ﴿46﴾

From the above, we conclude that the ‘mind’ cannot be fully utilised without profound thought. Almighty God does not mention ‘the mind’ and ‘thought’ in vain. There is a difference between them, as we have previously clarified.

Further examples are: the shuttle of a loom needs the appropriate thread to weave silk or woollen cloth with beautiful, colourful patterns. And a printing machine must be loaded with inks to print words and pictures on blank pages. Similarly, when thought aligns with the spirit, because of the spirit’s fear of death and its horrible consequences, it produces the mind and the process of spiritual witnessing (with the third eye). In this way thought will run fruitfully and the spirit will continue witnessing realities by its means which allows the heart’s insight (the third eye) to open. The Holy Qur’an speaks about the presence of the mind in the spirit when God says, ‘What, have they not journeyed in the land so that they have hearts to ponder [to fully realise]?’ ﴿47﴾

This verse shows that the mind is in the heart, the heart of the spirit; it is not in the head which contains the brain, the mechanism for thinking.

Thought

The word ‘thought’ is

al-fikr

in Arabic. In idiomatic language

al-fikr

is a portmanteau word blending two Arabic verbs:

fak’kaka

and

ra’a

which mean ‘disassemble’ and ‘see’; that is to say, when things seen with the eye, heard with the ear, or perceived by the other senses come to the mechanism of the brain, it starts the process of breaking down and re-assembling, analysis and inference. This happens when a person is true in their endeavours to achieve something. The light of the spirit goes to the brain and there the spirit sees what it needs. God, the Almighty, distinguished man from His other creatures with the ability to think. And as noted in the noble saying (hadith), ‘

An hour of thinking about the nature of the universe is better than seventy years worshipping.

’ ﴿48﴾

As stated previously the centre of thought is in the brain, and by means of the process of thought man can disassemble, analyse and understand. It is the only means for man’s escape and salvation from the claws of their love for this low world and its fatal flaws. Through careful, analytical thought man can rise, advance, and soar up to the highest rank, and if they neglect the ability to think, they will remain blind and incapable of seeing anything except the reflection of things, so that they become even lower than animals in rank.

By means of this power of thought man can protect themself from forbidden desires. They will then experience great joy in soaring upwards and drawing nearer to their Provider. All of the modern inventions, industries and technology that we see nowadays are brought about through the means of thought and truthfulness in worldly affairs. Here a distinction should be made: the selfish man who invents something simply for their own benefit, may well bring misery to others in order to achieve their own satisfaction and happiness. But the man who always strives to bring benefits to others regardless of their own needs is the selfless man. Our example of those who use their thought process only to focus on this lower, earthly world, with its contemptible extremes and cravings, is what we hear and see about some European and Oriental humanist pretenders.

Thinking and truthfulness in real life and eternal happiness can only be achieved by searching for Almighty God as He alone is the Source of life, true happiness and benevolence. We give the example of the group of companions of the noble Envoy Mohammad (cpth) as well as the companions of the other Envoys (ptt) when they were truthfully searching for Almighty God. They acknowledged Him and attested fully to His bright and alluring Light. They spread knowledge, happiness, mercy, sympathy and humanity all over the world. Men became like brothers and true, beloved friends to each other.

Through His Justice and Compassion, God gave this power of thought to every human being without discrimination or exception.

Thus the mind is realised through truthfulness and determination. If a man is truthful in doing something, the light of the spirit flows up to the brain, the process of thought is set in motion, and production begins.

There are further aspects relating to the spirit, mind and thought, which will be explained in following paragraphs. For now, however, we shall return to our main subject.

chapters.title: What Caused Mankind to Come to This World?
chapters.html:
In

al-Azal

world, the pre-material world, as we saw previously, when God first created creatures, they had been mere spirits without form or substance: man and animals, the earth, angels and jinns. One can say that on that day all creatures were of the same kind and quality and there was no difference between them. All these spirits had enjoyed witnessing the treasure of the grand Godly Beauty and loved it to the point of infatuation.

If Creation were left to enjoy witnessing a constant degree of Divine Godly Beauty they would eventually become bored of their status and situation. In order to achieve complete happiness and benevolence it was necessary that their ability to view the Godly Beauty should be advanced from its current level to one that is both higher and infinite. To clarify this, we may say that if a man sits in an orchard of remarkable beauty and stays there for a long time, they will undoubtedly become bored of it, and will no longer appreciate its beauty. To maintain their pleasure, they would have to move to an even more beautiful orchard than their own.

Boredom

Certainly, boredom and apathy creep into our spirits for they naturally feel weary of constantly being in the same state. They become bored with the repetition and regularity of even the most joyful and beautiful experiences, whatever they may be. A creature cannot advance from one state of ability to witness the Divine Beauty to a higher one unless they have done good deeds which ensure that their Creator is Satisfied with them. Such deeds will act like an elevator carrying them nearer to God. In the same way, God offered all these spirits an exodus from the realm where they had nothing to do. This exodus would lead them into a world where their good deeds would help them to come closer to their Creator, where they could seek access to the Glorious Treasure, in order to drink continuously and endlessly from the oceans of beauty and perfection.

The Effect of Good Deeds in the Elevation of the Spirit

To show the effect of good deeds on the spirit’s elevation and its gaining closeness to its Creator, we give the following example: let us imagine a commander fighting a battle along with his soldiers. When they come back after the battle, will all the soldiers be in the same psychological and spiritual state, and on an equal footing with each other? Undoubtedly, they will not! The braver soldiers who have done well and made greater sacrifices will come back feeling themselves closer to their commander, with a higher status and enjoying a greater share of spiritual wellbeing than the others. This analogy applies to sons and fathers, students and teachers, disciples and their guide, and servants and their Creator.

One of the firm rules of the spirit is that it cannot spiritually approach its Creator unless it has a good deed upon which it can depend, and the greater the sacrifice and the good deeds, the closer its approach will become. This spiritual side, by which we mean the confidence produced by good deeds in the spirit of the one who does them, makes it go ahead and rise up towards its Creator. And so it will be delighted by its closeness to Him, and will therefore enjoy a state of bliss in proportion to its deed. This important aspect, that is to say this confidence, is the basis of closeness to God and the secret of happiness. This is why Almighty God made this world an abode of good deeds and a pathway to the other world where the Heavens conceal endless spiritual bliss, and rivers flowing with abundant bounty and blessings: high ranks for the truthful before an Omnipotent King.

The Effect of Yearning in Generating Deeds and Allocating Their Values

Why did Almighty God put that yearning in our spirit?

Having explained the value of deeds as being the basis of happiness, enjoyment and a reason for the spirit’s advancement and perfection, we should deal with another point, that is, yearning. If good deeds are the means that draw a human nearer to their Creator and lead them to sensing God’s Satisfaction with them, there must be the motivation and impulse that drives them towards those deeds, for without this yearning or desire a human being is not able even to initiate the good deed, much less implement it. Desire makes a man look for the deed willingly and carry it out happily. Without this yearning they would have no wish to go in search of any deeds and, what is more, they would remain inert and unable to experience any sense of happiness.

Yearning is the stimulus to achieving appreciation and happiness. It gives value to an act which, otherwise, would be worthless in the eyes of the doer. The more attractive a sacrifice is to the spirit, the more valuable it will be, and the greater effect it will have on the spirit. If a man has no particular desire for money then charity has no meaning, and they will not gain any spiritual elevation by donating money to charitable causes. Similarly, we have the example of averting men’s gaze from women, and abstaining from performing forbidden acts. If the spirit did not like women, then chastity and averting one’s gaze would have no meaning, so the virtuous believer would have failed to find those honourable indications of chastity and purity which would otherwise be present in his spirit. We see that simply by wanting something, proportionate value is given to every good deed. To summarise the above: the greater the sacrifice, the greater the deed arising from it will be in the eyes of the doer, and the greater the relative elevation and raising of the spirit will be.

Almighty God says, ‘

The love of desirable things is made alluring for men – women, children, gold and silver treasures piled up high, horses with fine markings, livestock, and farmland – these may be the joys of this life, but Al’lah has the best place to return to.

’ ﴿49﴾

The following is a detailed explanation of this verse, ‘

The love of desirable things is made alluring for men

’ – Without yearning the universe will not function. These worldly desires are enticing and by making them alluring, life progresses in due order, so that every human being may be aware of their beginning as a drop of semen and their eventual end, that is, death at the appointed time. So if you abandon these enticements for the Sake of God you will become confident that Al’lah is Pleased with you and you will naturally draw closer to Him. ‘

Women

’ - All of us like women. Every human must desire certain things if they expose their spirit to their charm and beauty. The spirit naturally inclines towards desire but the pure person never looks at anything at all that is unlawful. The true believer remains true to God’s Limits. ‘

Children

’ – By means of their children, the believer draws nearer to Al’lah. ‘

Gold and silver treasures piled up high

’ – And thereby they do good deeds. ‘

Horses with fine markings

’ – Distinguished in war and the holy fight. ‘

Livestock, and farmland

’ – Cattle, orchards and farms. ‘

These may be the joys of this life

’ – You will leave all the above things one day, so why has Almighty God made all these wonderful enticements for humans? Is it just for us to be conceited about them? ‘

But Al’lah has the best place to return to [Paradise with flowing rivers].

’ – Alternatively, you should employ these desirable things to gain God’s Satisfaction; in return you will be rewarded with His Blessings, and once you attain the link with Him, the Almighty, you will be able to control that yearning and derive goodness and other benefits from it.

The deeds of the believer are extremely important in this worldly life, and through such enticements they gain greater happiness than those who do not believe.

If you abandon those desires for no reason other than having God’s Satisfaction, you will find far greater pleasure and happiness than the pleasure derived from mere enticements. This is because earthly desires include attractions, so if you forego this attraction you will become assured of God’s Satisfaction and draw closer to Him. If you sacrifice your yearning for God’s Sake you will make use of those things in a virtuous way and gain His Satisfaction. Those enticements lead humanity to Paradise if they are believers and to Fire if they are not. The believer who raises their children with morally virtuous qualities and spends their money in doing good deeds, and giving charity, will enter Paradise. This man will have access to Paradise when he raises horses and struggles through them to spread God’s Word, and also raises the cattle and uses his farms and orchards for lofty purposes: all that will be a way for him to enter Paradise. But for a human who fails to achieve true belief, their children, their wealth, and all that they have will be like a curse for them. Actually this worldly life is a path to the Hereafter; the believer takes that path and employs everything they have simply to achieve God’s Satisfaction and finally to win the life in the Hereafter.

To summarise the above we say that true belief is the basic foundation. It gives rise to happiness, for it leads to performing good deeds through which the believer can approach the Almighty God. With that approach they will derive the greatest pleasure and happiness, far more than any they might achieve in this materialistic world. And finally, good deeds cause the believer to draw nearer to Al’lah and have an approach to Him that is unequalled by any other means.

The Effect of the Freedom of Choice on the Value of Deeds

With reference to all that we have stated above about the value of a good deed and the effect of yearning, we should now speak about the freedom of choice that makes a man voluntarily and willingly carry out that deed. God the Almighty gave mankind the freedom of choice which gives us the ability to do a deed without any obligation; in fact, no man can take even the smallest step towards their Creator through their actions, or find them valuable in their own eyes, unless such a man has freedom of choice. This is a choice from options given to us by the Creator, as He alone knows what we have done in the past and are going to do in the future. God says, ‘

Say, “The Truth is from your Provider. Let him who will, believe, and let him who will, disbelieve.”

’ ﴿50﴾

And here we must point out that the Holy Qur’an is replete with Qur’anic verses that refer to freedom of choice and the will of Creation. We give the following example by way of an explanation: let us suppose that a prince was walking along and he decided to purchase some items, whereupon one of his retinue rushed forward voluntarily and carried the goods for him. I wonder, is the state of that man who carried the goods the same as if he did not rush forward of his own free will and the prince had to ask him to do this? Without doubt, if he carried out this action through his own free will he would be spiritually closer to his prince.

So, to undertake deeds through personal freedom and choice gives these deeds the greatest value which the spirit can then rely on when drawing nearer to its Creator, for the spirit derives great joy in being close to His Noble Honour and becoming immersed in witnessing His Beauty and Perfection equivalent to the deeds it has done. This leads one to the question, how and when did Almighty God give us the freedom of choice?

chapters.title: Offering the Trust and Man’s Acceptance in the Al - Azal World
chapters.html:
Offering the Trust and Man’s Acceptance in the Al-Azal World

The Almighty says, ‘

We offered the Trust to the heavens, earth and mountains and they refused to bear it for they feared it; Man bore it [of his own volition]. Was man unjust [to himself] and ignorant [of its results]?... [Truly, he was not]

.’ ﴿51﴾

What is the ‘Trust’?

To understand what is meant by the word ‘Trust’ we shall give the following example: if I owned certain items and I left them with a friend of mine on condition that I would take them back after some time, then these items are entrusted to my friend as long as they are with him. Similarly, the will of all Creation is originally in the Possession of their Creator and subject to His Power and, therefore, the spirits have no free will or choice.

However, because God wanted to give them the most precious gift, He showed them the means by which they could attain it. He offered to place this free will into trust with the spirits, and allow them to follow the path which would lead to the achievement of their deeds resulting from their desires. The Almighty says, ‘

We offered the Trust to the heavens, earth and mountains and they refused to bear it for they feared it; Man bore it [of his own volition]. Was man unjust [to himself] and ignorant [of its results]?... [Truly, he was not].

’ ﴿52﴾

The granting of freedom of choice is indicated by the word ‘Trust’.

In the world of

al-Azal

, the pre-material world, God offered this ‘Trust’ to all the spirits without discrimination and showed them that the shouldering of this Trust – that is to say, the freedom of choice of action – may be a very dangerous thing. A man can rise, through their work, to the highest rank, or their deeds can humiliate them and reduce them to the lowest rank.

Therefore, out of God’s Mercy for Creation, He made it clear to them that if they accepted this ‘Trust’ and came into this worldly existence, He would send them a Book to serve as the light and true guidance for their every act. If they are illuminated by His Light when they begin to action a particular desire, if they seek His Guidance and ask Him for inspiration in their movements, their path will be straight, their actions safe and compliant with those indicated to them in His Book. In this way they will be protected from committing any deed that is evil and from undertaking wrongful actions. Their deeds will be the cause of their rise and deliverance. When they come to God after death their virtuous humanitarian acts will be the basis of their closeness to God, so that they will succeed in their desire to be nearer to Him, by rising successively through the paradises of eternal delight.

If they accept this Trust and lead their existence without being guided by His Light or seeking His Guidance in relation to their deeds, they will certainly fail to follow the right path which would lead them to happiness, and therefore all their work and deeds will result in causing harm and damage to the rest of Creation. When they finally leave this world, they will face their Creator, ashamed of their wrongful acts, despised because of their shameful deeds, and humiliated by their disgrace and lack of gratitude. The evil deed will be like a veil preventing the spirit from drawing near to the Almighty. It will be unable to turn towards Him but, rather, it will withdraw in diffidence and shame. Then, when it remembers all that it has witnessed in the pre-material world and realises its failure to be close to His Honour and its loss of the Glorious Treasure, intense feelings of sorrow, painfully burning, will inflame within itself all of which will force them to throw themselves into the Fire. They will hope to forget their great pain and spiritual agony which are alleviated by the pain of Fire and the torture of burning, that is, they will escape from Hell to Fire. According to this meaning ‘Hell’ is the spiritual pain of the disbeliever or the inner burning of their spirit, and the word ‘Fire’ is used to describe Al’lah’s Fire which cures the disbeliever in the same way that a hospital treats and cures its patients.

There are many Qur’anic verses which reveal that this Fire is a dwelling-place where shunning spirits are treated, and that the spirit that has distanced itself from God throws itself into the Fire of its own free will, in order to forget its infernal moral pains. Of these noble verses we mention God’s Saying, ‘

However, on that Day their torture will not be inflicted upon them by anyone [other than themselves].

’ ﴿53﴾

There is a holy verse, ‘

Leave alone those who take their religion to be mere play and amusement, and are deceived by the life of this world. But bring to minds by it [the Qur’an] [for fear] that a spirit will deliver itself to ruin because of what it has acquired.

’ This verse refers to bravery in throwing oneself into one’s own destruction. The irreligious, those who live in sin, will throw themselves into the Fire because of their spiritual pain, and ‘

It will find for itself no protector or intercessor except Al’lah.

’ This means that at that moment, there will be noone to protect you except Al’lah; at that moment you will choose to deliver yourself to Al’lah because of your spiritual pain. ‘

And if it offers every ransom [or reparation], none will be accepted.

’ This sentence denotes that in the Hereafter, nothing that a sinful man has amassed will be accepted. ‘

Those are the ones who have delivered themselves to ruin because of what they have acquired.

’… That is, they will throw themselves into the Fire because of the horrible impact of their evil deeds on their spirits. ‘

They will have a drink of severe heat and grievous torment: for they persisted in their unbelief

’ ﴿54﴾

… That is, they disregarded all the signs they saw and neglected to consider them. Therefore, in the life to come they will throw themselves into the Fire to escape from the fire of shame which will burn them: their spiritual pain is so great that, seeing no alternative, they throw themselves into the Fire! And His Saying (Glory to His Names) also refers to them, ‘

These are the ones who buy error in place of guidance, and torment in place of forgiveness. Ah, what makes them patient in the face of the Fire?

’ ﴿55﴾

In a prophetic saying, the Envoy Mohammad (cpth) said, ‘

Man will be so constrained by the sweat of shame on Doomsday that he will request, “My Provider, relieve me even to the Fire.”

’ ﴿56﴾

To emphasise this, in another saying, he said, ‘

Shame will befall man on Doomsday to the extent that he says, “Oh my Provider, sending me to the Fire would be easier to tolerate than what I am suffering”, although he knows the great torture that will result.

’ ﴿57﴾

God showed all this to the spirits on the day that He offered the Trust to them; so they were fully aware of these facts and were aware also of the outcome if they failed to follow the right path. They saw the good that would ensue if they bore the Trust and the sorrows that would befall them if they neglected to adhere to it. Then, at this same critical moment that Godly Favour and Divine Justice appeared to all creatures, I tell you that all creatures retreated and were afraid to proceed to this test, afraid that it may bring about failure and misery even if good and happiness would eventually result from it. All the spirits were afraid of the Trust and refused to carry it except one category that embarked on a great adventure and made a commitment to their Provider not to break away from Him for even a moment.

Thereupon, their Provider accepted their promise and He expanded and valued the risk they had undertaken. He promised them Paradise for all Eternity if they redeemed their pledge. The Holy Qur’an indicated God’s Offer and Promise when He says, ‘

You who believe, be pious [see by Al’lah’s Light] and speak apposite speech. He will make your deeds right and forgive you your sins. Those who obey Al’lah and His Envoy will achieve a great success. We offered the Trust to the heavens, earth and mountains and they refused to bear it for they feared it; Man bore it [of his own volition]. Was man unjust [to himself] and ignorant [of its results]?... [Truly, he was not].

’ ﴿58﴾

The heavens, earth and mountains include also the spirits and creatures that they contain. The word ‘man’ included the two kinds: human beings and jinns, as the Holy Qur’an indicated elsewhere. The statement ‘

Was man unjust [to himself] and ignorant [of its results]?

’ does not attribute injustice and ignorance to Mankind, but it is a statement of praise and enhancement. It is a positive statement in the form of a question, but with the question mark omitted so as to emphasise the intended meaning, ‘Was mankind unjust to himself by this pledge? Were they ignorant of the good obtained once they decided to bear the Trust?’ Or were they aware of the endless happiness to come thereafter? So they went ahead and took a risk, and consequently they were the most honourable creature.

Oh Mankind: that was your attitude on that great day and that was your position among the whole of Creation. You accepted to leave the

al-Azal

world and go out into this earthly world, the dwelling-place of deeds, in order to achieve good work. You accepted to have desires (yearnings), not for the reason that you would gain enjoyment from them, but for that they would be your sole motive for performing good deeds. In addition, you took a risk in shouldering the Trust so that your deeds should be important and valuable in your own eyes. You accepted to be granted your own free will so that your Provider would fulfil all your wishes and give you the power to achieve them. Then, you made a covenant with your Provider that you would stay always illuminated by His Light so that your will should be in accordance with what He legislated in His Book, and in order not to deviate from your choice. Indeed, you aspired to all that in order to be the creature most worthy of knowing Him and the most fortunate in seeing the Beauty of this Great Treasure and gazing at the Face of your Noble Provider.

chapters.title: Who Are the Noble Angels?
chapters.html:
As mentioned previously; we saw how human beings have carried the Trust, namely, the freedom of choice, while the rest of the spirits refrained from bearing it, afraid of what their destiny might be if they were unable to keep the Trust according to God’s Will. There is another category of these spirits who refused to bear the Trust altogether, loathed these yearnings and desires and dispensed with them completely. They dared not advance to the extent that Mankind did. They did not want to have free will or a choice, and decided to relinquish the possession of their free will to their Creator. And so they were called ‘angels’. In Arabic, the word ‘angels’ means those who surrendered themselves to God. They sacrificed the craving in order to stay close to their Provider. Due to such action and sacrifice, they had the way and the means to take them close to their Creator. However, the true man who faces up to his yearning, directs it according to his Creator’s Will, and does his work depending on his own free choice, will have a higher position than that of the angels, and will take greater precedence over them in this matter.

As a response to the angels’ choice, the Almighty chose not to give them bodies like those of human beings, so they have no physical requirements and therefore they are devoid of the material desires towards which humanity is inclined. They do not eat or drink; they do not get married or reproduce, or enjoy any other such human needs.

chapters.title: Animals, Plants and Material Things
chapters.html:
Finally, we want to talk about a group whose spirits did not comply in dispensing with their desires, nor did they wish to sacrifice the pleasure and enjoyment allied to them. But in addition to that, they did not dare to bear the Trust by which they would have free will. So they asked God if they could have the ability to desire, provided that their free will would be restricted. This category includes all kinds of animals, plants and solid matter. These three groups asked their Creator to take them out of

al-Azal

and into this earthly world, to grant them the desire by which they can sample His Favour, and to bind their desire to a task that they would carry out in the service of Mankind. Thus their service to this noble creature would be a good deed and a means by which they would draw closer to their Creator. Their Provider then showed them the universe and all the tasks and services it included in order that life on earth could progress and be properly and perfectly available to all Creation.
