Each of these creatures chose one task: for example, the camel asked to be devoted and subservient to carry man and their goods. Some plants chose to be food and nourishment for humankind, and the sun chose to serve as a shining light for this honourable creature.

So, every creature chose a specific task for which it became fully responsible. God’s Will then required that each of these spirits should have the physical make-up suitable to its function, and senses that help it to do its job. So, the universe that we now see appears to be established according to the most wonderful conditions and the most perfect, strict discipline. All that it contains demonstrates the Wisdom of the Wise, the Science of the Omniscient, the Efficiency of the Estimator and the Compassion of the All-Compassionate, the All-Merciful. God says, ‘

You will never find any fault with what the All-Compassionate creates. Look again! Do you see any flaws? Look again and again! Your sight will turn back to you, weak and defeated.

’ ﴿59﴾

A specific group of Qur’anic verses refers to the devotion of this category of creatures and their subservience in the service of Man. God says through the mouth of His Envoy (pth), ‘

It is He Who has made the earth hospitable for you; so travel its regions and eat His Provision. It is His to distribute and allot as He wishes.

’ ﴿60﴾

Another verse says, ‘

It is He Who created all that is on the earth for you, then turned to the heaven with manifestation and ripened it, making seven heavens: He is Omniscient of everything.

’ ﴿61﴾

And a further verse states, ‘

Al’lah is He Who has created the heavens and the earth and sent down water from the sky, thereby brought forth fruits as provision for you; He has devoted the ships for you, that they may sail through the sea by His Command; and He has devoted rivers for you. He has devoted the sun and the moon, both constantly pursuing their courses; He has devoted the night and the day for you.

’ ﴿62﴾

Oh, Mankind! Consider how all that is in the universe is drawing nearer to its Creator through their service to you. So, if you redeemed your pledge you would surpass all creatures and rise above them; but if you distanced yourself from your Creator and gave in to your cravings your deeds would be bad and you would be degraded to a position lower than that of any animal. God says, ‘

Surely, those who disbelieve, from among the people of the Scripture, and those that obey other gods besides Al’lah will abide in the fire of Hell; they are the worst of all the creatures. Surely, those who believe and do good deeds are the best of all the creatures. The reward they receive from their Provider is the Gardens of Eternity, underneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Al’lah is well-pleased with them and they with Him. That is for him who fears his Provider.

’ ﴿63﴾

chapters.title: Preference and Competition in Al - Azal World
chapters.html:
Preference and Competition in Al-Azal World

Until the establishment of man’s position among all creatures no member of this category had become superior to another or favoured over another, and there was still no Prophet or Envoy. Adam and all other human beings and jinns were still at one and the same level in the Hands of their Creator. Not one of them had yet performed any deed by which they might be preferred to another, for all creatures are God’s dependants; and it is only by actual deeds that one will be distinguished from another: in the Hands of the Just God. In order to make the principle of justice universal and so that none of us should have any protest against God, He told all of Adam’s sons as well as the jinns that He would place the ability to yearn or desire within them. He also reminded them of the pledge that they accepted – to look at desire by the Light of their Noble Creator – and He warned them of the consequences if they broke away from Him even for a moment. Then God showed them this world and what it contains, and whilst implanting desires into their spirits He reminded them of their promise, saying, ‘

Am I not your Provider?

– That is to say, ‘Am I not the One Who created you and sustains you, ensuring your life? After this, could you break away from Me and look at your desires without being illuminated by My Light?’ As soon as they heard the statement ‘

Am I not your Provider?

’ all these spirits replied, ‘

Yes

’ – meaning ‘Yes, You are our Provider.’ The noble verse indicated this, ‘

[Prophet], when your Provider took out the offspring of Adam’s sons as they were superior among all creatures ﴿64﴾

and made them witness against their spirits, He said, “Am I not your Provider?” They said, “Yes, [we bear witness that You are].”

’ ﴿65﴾

Until this moment all of Adam’s sons had enjoyed the same level and not one had been distinguished above another. But the reply ‘

Yes

’ was not spoken in unison and by maintaining their own points of view each of Adam’s sons acquired a different position and rank, such as Prophet, believer or unbeliever, according to their reply to their Provider:

Some of them looked at ‘desire’; they admired it and were overwhelmed by it and became veiled from their Creator, their Obliger, the One Who had settled it upon them. These spirits were the spirits of all infidels, as ‘infidelity’ in Arabic means ‘veiling’. The desires veiled the infidels from their Creator so they then indulged themselves in their cravings and forgot the pledge that they had taken.

There were spirits that, at first, were determined to remember their pledge to their Creator and said, ‘Yes’. That is to say, ‘You are our Provider and we should not leave You.’ But as soon as they felt the force of their yearning they were infatuated with it and they, too, forgot their pledge. This group includes the hypocrites who said, ‘

“We believed” with their tongues, but their hearts did not believe.

’ ﴿66﴾

There are other spirits who looked at their yearning, admired it and were inclined towards it, but they remembered their pledge to their Creator and returned to Him, feeling remorse at their failure. This category includes the disobedient people who are influenced by this world when they come out to it, but if they are reminded they will remember and turn back, repenting their negligence and regretting their past omission.

Mankind is called

al-nas

in Arabic. The word

al-nas

– which is a generic name for all sons of Adam – derived its pronunciation from the Arabic verb

nasiya

(‘to forget’ in English).

They were called this because their coming to this world, the world of shapes and bodies, made them forget the knowledge of God that they had previously in the world of

al-Azal

, the world of spirits. The physical body became the veil which prevented the spirit from recognising its weakness, its absolute need for its Creator, and the continuity of its previous knowledge of the Creator.

Almighty God created this worldly life to be like a school to make them remember Him and draw closer to Him through contemplating the many wonders of the universe in order to be guided to their Creator. But if they failed to do so they would continue to forget and also forget themselves, and even fail to recognise the One Who created them, and why He created them. Additionally, they did not see that it is Al’lah Who founded Creation, and that their life and continuity come directly from Him so that they should remember Him again, and deliver themselves from the terrible affliction of oblivion. The Almighty God addressed them on the Day of Resurrection, ‘

So taste [the punishment], since you forgot [ignored] the meeting on this Day of yours [the Day of Accounting]. Did We Ourself forget you [of proper cure]?... [Truly, We did not]

. ﴿67﴾

So taste the abiding torment [fire of regret] for all what you used to do [of bad acts].

’ ﴿68﴾

As for the spirits that remembered their pledge, they did not feel their yearning except by the Light of their God, and never turned away from Him: these are the spirits of the true believers. They saw the yearning as a favour bestowed on them by their Creator, so they thanked Him for His Favour and praised Him for His Grace. This category includes the spirits of the Prophets (ptt), the Envoys (ptt), and the greatest believers. When those spirits said ‘Yes’ they were overwhelmed with love for their Creator, acknowledged His Favour and praised His Gift. Among those spirits was the spirit of our master Mohammad (cpth) who was far in advance of all other spirits in his course towards Almighty God, and who praised Him for His Grace and Favour more than any other spirit. This is why he (cpth) became the master of all Creation, and the leader of all Envoys (ptt).

At that time, God looked at Adam’s sons after they took up their individual stances, so He knew that the spirits of the hypocrites and the infidels who drew further away from their Provider and failed to view their yearning by their Creator’s Light, were filled with maleficence and spiritual illnesses because of that distance. So they had to come out to this earthly world so that God would remove these afflictions from their spirits. Then He would chastise them to help them repent and return to Him to achieve their eternal happiness. On the other hand, He knew that the believers, those who looked at desire by their Creator’s Light and knew their Provider’s Favour, had their spirits filled with goodness simply by entering into His Presence. So, they must also come out to this earthly world in order to reveal the perfection of their spirits.

So all the spirits replied to their Provider on that day, ‘

Yes, [we bear witness that You are].’ Then the Almighty continued His Saying, ‘[This I did] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, “We had forgotten that.”

’ ﴿69﴾

– This means that God addressed us with the words, ‘Be careful not to say such a thing tomorrow. I have sent you this Revelation now to prevent you saying that. Now I remind you of the bond you took upon yourselves.’

Summary

Before giving them the yearning God asked the creatures that accepted to carry the Trust, that is, the freedom of choice, ‘

Am I not your Provider?

’ This was mentioned previously when Al’lah the Almighty said, ‘

[Prophet], when your Provider took out the offspring of Adam’s sons as they were superior among all creatures and made them witness against their spirits, He said, “Am I not your Provider?” They said, “Yes, [we bear witness that You are].” [This I did] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, “We had forgotten that.”

’ ﴿70﴾

After He had given them yearning, they were divided into four categories according to their individual positions and ranks:

Some people got the certificate due to their truthfulness with Almighty Al’lah. They are the Prophets and Envoys of God (ptt); and the Envoy Mohammad (cpth) is the master of all human beings for he was ranked the highest.

The true believers come after them. They achieved lower grades, and accordingly the Envoy (cpth) referred to them when he said, ‘

I was sent to complete the noble merits of morality.

’ ﴿71﴾

The unsuccessful who still have an ability to succeed again in this life. In this world those who have the ability can rise. God granted humans different spans of life as a second chance so that if they work hard by following the way of belief they will succeed, receive God’s Consent and become the same as the noble companions of the Prophet (cpth). These were originally the unsuccessful ones; but if they consider and reflect upon all the marvels of this universe such as the sun, the moon and the stars, for example, and of the beginning and the end of this Creation, they will not only pass the test but they even will compete with the people who preceded them and were superior to them. The noble saying of God’s Envoy (cpth) serves them, ‘

I was sent as a teacher.

’ ﴿72﴾

– That is, a teacher of faith and the way of believing in God.

Finally there were those who were useless: they changed their minds, and were out and out liars who would never be guided – God granted them fewer years. They die before reaching the age of adulthood, and then they will have only one paradise in the life to come. God says, ‘

And He raised some of you above others according to their ranks.

’ ﴿73﴾

– These children who die before they are sixteen years old will be eternalised in the bliss of Paradise where they offer services to the dwellers of Paradise: and that is the view of Godly Mercy and Justice.

In brief we say that when God created the spirits, He showed them the way: ‘If you come to this world and follow the right way without leaving Me; if you become illuminated by My Light, you will have great gains, but if not, you will face a great loss.’ Man and jinns replied, ‘It is ours’, that is, ‘We will keep this promise.’ When God placed the yearning within them some people were true to God and others had wicked desires in their hearts. Then God looked at the creatures: those who were truthful obtained perfection and they will go out to this world and appear in all their perfection, for they have succeeded. To those who were not truthful and had wicked desires enclosed within their spirits God will grant them their every desire in this world. Then, He will ensure that they suffer hardship in order to help them repent and come back to the right way.

We give a comparison here: at school some people are totally successful in the first semester whereas others are not, and have to make greater effort in the second semester. This world is like a second semester, a second chance for them to make things right. God says in the Qur’an, ‘

Your Provider is the quick Pursuer and He is the All-Forgiver and the All-Merciful.

’ ﴿74﴾

Therefore, the Almighty Al’lah straitens a human by subjecting them to difficulties after first fulfilling their desires so they can put them into action. This strain and tension are nothing but the Mercy of Al’lah so that the negligent, unsuccessful human may return to the Side of their Provider, the All-Forgiving, the All-Merciful; and Al’lah’s Light rises again in their spirit. However, Al’lah the Almighty has demanded that all His servants should fulfil their covenant to Him and He has praised highly those who do not break the bonds to which they bound themselves to fulfil their promise in the

al-Azal

world. God said, ‘

Those who fulfil the pledges they make in God’s Name and do not break their bonds.

’ ﴿75﴾

In another verse, God said, ‘

Those who are faithful to their trusts and pledges.

’ ﴿76﴾

God also said, ‘

You who believe, fulfil your contracts.

’ ﴿77﴾

The Almighty Al’lah said, ‘

Honour your pledges: you will be questioned about your pledges.

’ ﴿78﴾

The virtuous Qur’anic verses mentioned above, confirm how Al’lah the Almighty claimed that His servants should fulfil the pledges they made to Him in the

al-Azal

world before they came to this worldly life.

chapters.title: Fate The Spirit’s Responsibility Concerning Fate
chapters.html:
The issue of Fate has a very important link to the previous topics of the pre-material world (

al-Azal

) as well as to the cause of humankind coming into this worldly life; the following link makes it easy to understand.

The Arabic word for ‘Fate’ means a just judgement established after certain consideration. In order to understand the meaning of ‘Fate’ we give this example: let us suppose that there is a teacher who has a number of students; he looks at them before the exam which usually takes place at the end of the year.

No doubt he can judge by what he knows of their ability and behaviour during the school year which of them will definitely fail and who will pass. This final judgement, which cannot be wrong, can be called ‘Fate’ or ‘judgement’; it means to take a decision after due consideration. We see that the teacher can estimate the grade of each successful student; this can be called ‘Fate’ or ‘estimation’.

For further illustration, we give another example as follows: when a driver looks at the fuel tanks of several cars and sees the fuel level on the gauge in each car he can guess how many kilometres each car can run without needing to be refilled. This calculation that he does for each car is also what we can call ‘Fate’ or ‘estimation’.

Similarly, God estimated a position for every man after He had observed and scientifically assessed what their spirits contained in the

al-Azal

world. The example above shows us that God does not oblige anyone to choose this way or that, but because He had previously known the states of all the creatures, as a Godly Science, He was Able to estimate their positions accordingly.

Mankind might miscalculate for the lack of scientific knowledge that would enable them to take into account even minute things. But God never miscalculates as His Estimation is based upon comprehensive Omniscience.

When God called to the creatures in the

al-Azal

world, ‘

Am I not your Provider?

’ and they replied, ‘

Yes

’, He looked at them and knew, scientifically, the goodness hidden in the spirits of those who saw their desire by His Light, and the perfection that filled their spirits. In addition, He knew, scientifically, what is hidden in the spirits of those who followed their desires and withdrew from Him, and He witnessed the wickedness and spiritual illness that was settled within the spirit of each one of them. He then judged what level of goodness would result from those who drew close to Him when they come to this world, and what level of perfection would emanate from them. In addition, He judged what amount of wickedness and degradation would result from those who withdrew from Him when they came to this world, and the failure that would surround them.

God has ordained this, that is to say, He gave a firm judgement because of His Omniscience, that is, His complete Knowledge of the states of both categories. He also estimated the position that each person would reach through their own deeds depending on the degree of their closeness to Him. Here it is important that we categorically refute the terrible lies of those who say that God created some people to be happy and others to be unhappy, and that He singled out some people for Paradise and others for Fire.

God did not distinguish between one human being and another, as all creatures are His dependents, but those who listened to their Creator’s Recommendation and saw their yearning and desires by His Light are the ones who will be happy. When they come to this world, their reality and the perfection that was printed on their spirits would be disclosed for all to see. It is those who choose to withdraw from their Creator who will be unhappy. When they come to this world their wickedness will be obvious to people, and their own evil deeds will act as witnesses against them.

This is Fate, this Justice of God is the same for all of His creatures. This world is simply a gauge for spirits; the perfect man will naturally show their perfection and the man distanced from God will show their baseness and wickedness. God says in the Qur’an, ‘

We have made all what is on earth as a temptation for it so as to test them; which of them is best in deeds.

’ ﴿79﴾

And He says, ‘

Alif Lam Mim

. ﴿80﴾

Did oblivious people reckon to be left to say, “We believed”, without testing them? We have already tested those who were before them so that Al’lah may scientifically know those who were truthful and the liars.

’ ﴿81﴾

And the verse says, ‘

Your Provider knows best who strays from His Path, and it is He Who knows best who is rightly guided.

’ ﴿82﴾

The mark of happy people is that they will respond willingly if they are called to faith. The mark of unhappy people is that if you remind them they will still not remember; if they see the way of guidance they will ignore it; but if they see the way that will lead them astray they will certainly follow it.

These undeniable facts, which we mention in our research in this book and others, manifest the Justice of God to His creatures and His Compassion to them. Believers witness these facts during their lifetime which increases their love for their Creator.

As for those people who do not pay attention, they do not see these facts because their personal desires act as a veil between them and this vision. These facts will appear clearly to all those heedless people after death. At that moment all of them will acknowledge their Creator’s Favour toward them, confess His Justice and Compassion, and praise Him for His Care for them.

God says in the Qur’an, ‘

The close of their request [the two parties: the people of Paradise and the people of Fire] will be, “All praise is to God, the Provider of the worlds.”

’ ﴿83﴾

Three Groups Remain in Charge

According to this revelation about the

al-Azal

world, we say, there are three categories of human beings:

The first one has received the final diploma: they are the noble Prophets and Envoys (ptt).

Those who succeeded but their success was not perfect and lacked only a few marks; they will achieve further success in this world. The Prophet (cpth) says, ‘

I was sent to complete the noble merits of morality.

’ ﴿84﴾

The third category failed. However, if those people work hard in this world they, too, will succeed, and the means which will help them is to believe through contemplation of this universe, as did our master Abraham (pth). The Envoy (cpth) says, ‘

I was sent as a teacher.

’ ﴿85﴾

– That is to say, a teacher of faith. In another saying he (cpth) says, ‘

I was sent as an inviter and a preacher.

’ ﴿86﴾

– That is, to invite people to the faith and preach to those who reach out to it.

There is a way for everybody through which they can ponder upon something and eventually rise high by means of it. One has only to seek to recognise this ‘something’; for every human being is qualified for such advancement.

On the other hand, those who die under the age of sixteen are no longer in charge of bearing the Trust, for as they grow up and their disobedience and regression increase further, they will fail completely in this earthly life, which will prevent them from entering Paradise. Because of His Knowledge of their condition in the

al-Azal

world God, in His Mercy, decided that they should die before they reach the accepted age of responsibility.

chapters.title: What Happened to the Spirits after They Broke away from God?
chapters.html:
The Almighty referred to the spirits which had forsaken their Provider in the

al-Azal

world when He mentioned the word ‘death’ before the word ‘life’ in the noble verse, ‘

Who has created death and life so that He may test which of you excels.

’ ﴿87﴾

– When the spirits chose to give way to their desires and turn away from Him, becoming disconnected by their actions, they began to descend into darkness and oblivion. Merciful Al’lah stopped their freefall and, although their actions caused them to be deprived of their lives in Paradise, He attached them to the spine of our master Adam (pth ﴿88﴾

and sent them to the physical world, which halted their downward spiral.

This verse explains the fate of the spirits who turned away from Al’lah. In

al-Azal

, the pre-material world, some spirits succumbed to the temptations of lust, which caused them to drift far from the Presence of Al’lah. They abandoned their Provider, and their isolation from Al’lah the Almighty caused them to become spiritually lifeless. ﴿89﴾

To stop their fall and give them a second chance ﴿90﴾

Al’lah (Glory to Him) sent these spirits to the world in our present form – the human body – so that they might have the opportunity to regain purity of heart and eternal life. So, if those chosen few, the spirits who bear the Trust, wish to recover the heart life that was lost when they turned away from God in

al-Azal

, they have only to contemplate the universe until they come to believe in God; they must also love Al’lah’s Envoy (cpth) who is the paradigm for humankind. Only then will they be able to return to their Provider and receive again the gift of heart life. After He attached those spirits to the spine of our master Adam (pth), the Almighty let them pass through the spines of his male descendants until the time comes for a spirit to be sent to this world when His Will decides to do so.

This is true of all spirits except for the spirits of the Prophets and Envoys (ptt); they kept their word, retained faith with their covenant so their light was not extinguished; in fact the brightness and illumination of their light increased. The greatest Envoy, Mohammad (cpth), possessed the strongest light; its brightness was greater than that of all the Prophets and Envoys (ptt). And so the Prophet Mohammad (cpth) became a source of light for them too, and remains so to this day, for his light can never be extinguished or concealed.

Those noble spirits were not attached to the spine of our master Adam (pth); they remained in God’s Presence until He, the Almighty, chose the proper time for their coming to this world.

Qur’anic Verses Confirm the World of

Al-Azal

The Almighty God referred to the pre-material world (al- Azal) through many verses in the Holy Qur’an such as when He says,

‘

They said, “Our Provider, twice You have caused us to die and twice You have given us life.”

’ ﴿91﴾

– This verse is a proof of the

al-Azal

world. The first time that people died was when their spirits were attached to the spine of our master Adam (pth); and the second time of death is when these spirits became distracted by worldly desires and distanced themselves from God.

Death, in reality, is the withdrawal from Almighty God. In the

al-Azal

world all spirits were living with God, enjoying a link with Him, and He was manifesting Himself to them with life and lights. But then, after God accepted from them a binding promise that they would not break away from Him, they broke that promise and became immersed in the pleasures of their desires. Therefore they became disconnected from their Provider, the Source of life, and they caused their own death at that time. ‘

They said, “Our Provider, twice You have caused us to die.”

’ – They blamed God for their death although the fact is that it was they who caused their spirits to die when they preferred their desires instead of God. They thought ill of God, just as Lucifer did when he said to his Lord, ‘

Because You have thrown me out of the way.

’ ﴿92﴾

He also blamed God for his mistake, and not himself. Similarly, those people had held bad thoughts about God since the

al-Azal

world, and although the facts will become clear to them in the life to come, they will still maintain their attitude of ascribing all the bad things in their lives to God.

The reason for this is that they will be aware of the realities of things but they will still be unaware of the Godly Supreme Self. They will not see the Supreme Names of God and therefore they will continue to know nothing about Him, and maintain the same poor opinion of Him.

Consequently, in the Hereafter, they will be told, ‘

It is this [ill] thought you had about your Provider that has ruined you, so that you are now among the lost.

’ ﴿93﴾

And in another verse, ‘

Those who think evil thoughts about God, a turn of evil shall befall them.

’ ﴿94﴾

As for the rest of the previous verse, ‘

And twice You have given us life

’ ﴿95﴾

we say that the first life was given in the

al-Azal

world when Al’lah gave humans the freedom of choice and they witnessed His Majesty. The second life was given in this earthly world when He revived them once again and gave them physical bodies. The spirits regained their ability to see, to hear and to taste, which gave them the chance to return to their former state and become connected with their Provider once again.

As stated in the noble verse, the Envoy Mohammad (cpth) said, ‘

And I am the first of those who have submitted to Him.

’ ﴿96﴾

– This refers to the

al-Azal

world when God asked the human spirits, ‘

Am I not your Provider?

’ ﴿97﴾

There and then he, Mohammad (cpth), was the first spirit, the precedent for all mankind, who replied, ‘Oh yes, my Provider.’ Thus he (cpth) was the first servant of God.

And in another Fortress the Almighty says, ‘

Strive for God as is His Due: He has chosen you and laid no hardship on you in the religion. This is the way of your forefather Abraham.

It was he who called you Muslims previously.

’ ﴿98﴾

– That is, it was Abraham (pth) who selected you in the

al-Azal

world to become his companions.

Our master Jesus (pth) said to his people when he was still in the cradle, what the noble verse stated, ‘

I am a servant of Al’lah. He granted me the Book and made me a Prophet.

’ ﴿99﴾

Firstly, in the

al-Azal

world, the Almighty told all people that they should not break away from Him; but they disobeyed Him and became entrenched in their desires, and thus withdrew from Him. As for our master Jesus (pth), he was aware of worldly desires but paid no attention to them. He never left his Provider and remained always under His Light.

Secondly, when making the agreement the Almighty obtained a binding promise from Jesus (pth) that he would always be merciful and tender and never change, whatever he might face in the future. He (pth) obeyed God and fulfilled his promise.

Thirdly, the Almighty asked him to submit to His Envoy, Mohammad (cpth) the leading Prophet, as mentioned in the pact of the Prophets (ptt); and Jesus (pth) accepted this too.

Fourthly, the Almighty asked Jesus (pth) to be His Envoy during this difficult time, and he replied, ‘I am at Your Command, my Provider.’

Fifthly, his Provider told him, ‘You will meet with crushing situations and people will say bad things about you, and reject you.’ However, he did not care for all this but cared only about God’s Satisfaction. Thus by obeying his Provider he became an obedient servant of God before he came to this world, and he continued to be so thereafter.

‘

He granted me the Book.

’ – How did God grant Jesus (pth) the Book when he was still a baby and definitely not forty years old? This is because his spirit (pth) was aware of the Book and had known it since the

al-Azal

world. Jesus (pth) addressed his people, saying, ‘He granted me the Book in the past and I will announce it in the future. He gave it to me in order to pour it into your hearts and inform you of the Messages of my Provider.’ ‘

And made me a Prophet.

’ – ‘This is because I worship Him as is His Due. I have obeyed Him since the

al-Azal

world, therefore I have received a great light from Him.’ By His light, Jesus (pth) disclosed everything and became aware of previous peoples and nations. Did God then make him a Prophet if he was unworthy to be so? Not at all; for eventually he was lacerated and he experienced great suffering. Jesus said to his people, ‘

And made me a Prophet.

’ – That is, ‘I prophesy what is right and true and see by the Light of God.’ But sadly, despite all of this, his people did not believe him; worse still, they tried to crucify him.

We have learnt about the behaviour of the noble spirits in the

al-Azal

world which qualified them to be Prophets and Envoys.

We shall now investigate how they became Prophets and Envoys (ptt) once again in this earthly life.

chapters.title: Who Are the Noble Prophets and Envoys of God?
chapters.html:
Prophets and Envoys are people like us. They were created as we all were, and God took them from their mother’s wombs as He did with us. God made wives and families for them and allowed them to grow and flourish as we do. In fact they do not differ from any other human being concerning their creation and physical composition. Their bodies function like all others: eating and drinking, and walking in the market place, for example. The noble verse in the Qur’an refers to that, ‘

They said, “What is this Prophet who eats food and walks in the markets?”

’ ﴿100﴾

And God says, ‘

We never sent Envoys before you but they eat food and walk in the markets.

’ ﴿101﴾

If the Prophets and Envoys (ptt) were the same as all other people concerning the origin of their creation and their physical composition, why were they superior to all others to the point where they became worthy of receiving the Messages of their Provider and inviting the people of their nations to their Creator?

We say that amongst all of God’s Creation mankind was the only one to take it upon himself to bear the Trust in the

al-Azal

world because they wished to reach the high position that God had offered to all creatures. Therefore God distinguished them with a precious gift and a wonderful system by which they can reach that position that they had already faced; and they can eclipse the rest of Creation if they make full use of the system.

This gift and that system is, quite simply, the power of thought! By means of this valuable gift Man is differentiated from animals and all other creatures.

By the power of thought Man can recognise the Creator of the universe and obtain knowledge of Him that no other creature can have. By thinking, Man can be guided to the right way, the straight path that leads to Al’lah. By this means, people have the ability to differentiate between good and bad, and to achieve different ranks; the more one thinks and contemplates, the more superior and elevated one will become. The Prophets and Envoys (ptt) are simply people who are distinguished from others by making full use of this valuable gift. Since these noble men first became aware of their own consciousness they started to think of themselves and of what is around them. They looked at the earth and what is on it, and the sky and what is in it; they looked at the sun, the moon and the stars with an air of total contemplation: thinking, wondering and appreciating. This action then guided them to acknowledge the Existence of a Great Watchful Power and a Wise Moving Hand that provides this entire universe with life: supplying and managing all that it requires.

They noticed that this Hand never withdraws Its Support from this universe, not even for the blink of an eye, nor does It forget the universe for a single moment. There and then, their spirits submitted to this Grand Creator gratefully and reverently: they bowed to His Prestige with emotion and enhancement; they clung to the portals of His Love and to the witnessing of His Perfection; and never turned away from them, even for a moment. So, they are constantly directing themselves toward God and entering into His Presence, and they are always witnessing the Lights of the Owner of Majesty and Beauty. In the noble saying, the Prophet says, ‘

We, companies of Prophets, our eyes sleep but our hearts never do.

’ ﴿102﴾

This constant entering into God’s Presence and this continuous illumination by the Creator’s Light created piercing vision in the hearts of these men. So, by God’s Light, they became fully aware of what was true and what was untrue, and they distinguished between vice and virtue, as they recognised the level way and were guided to the straight path. This constant and continuous witnessing was the reason for the impeccability of their spirits which protected them from making any error, just as it was the reason for their purification and for preventing them from committing any bad deed. In addition, their constant attendance in God’s Presence helped them to gain virtue and perfection; as a result, their hearts were filled with mercy, compassion, sympathy and tenderness. God says, addressing His Envoy Mohammad (cpth), ‘

By a bit of mercy from Al’lah, you [Prophet] were gentle [in your dealings] with them

’ ﴿103﴾

Because of such illumination by God’s Light and their great closeness to Him, and because of the perfect qualities and mercy their spirits acquired from God, they were worthy of being chosen by their Creator and were selected by Him to be guides for His creatures. They became responsible for receiving His Message and announcing it to His servants. God says, ‘

They said, “The All-Compassionate has begotten a child.” Glory to Him, rather they are purified, strictly true servants. They do not speak before Him, and by His Order they act.

’ ﴿104﴾

And God says, ‘

We made them leaders guiding by Our Command, and inspired them in doing good acts, establishing communication with Me and achieving purification, and they were strictly true servants of Us.

’ ﴿105﴾

So when God wanted to bring us to this life He chose one of these noble spirits, our master Adam (pth), to be the father of all human beings and their first Missionary, Prophet and Envoy (pth). God then finalised these matters with our master Mohammad (cpth) who was the final Prophet.

chapters.title: Chapter Two, ADAM AND EVE
chapters.html:
Mankind’s Exodus to This World

When God wanted to bring humankind to this world, the world of solid physical shapes and bodies, He put into place laws and a set of rules for that, and of utmost importance He specified that everyone should have parents, that is, a father and a mother. The father carries the spirits of all of his children and offspring in his back, ﴿106﴾

and then the child’s spirit moves from the father into the mother’s womb, carried within a sperm which cannot be seen by the naked eye as it is so minute. It settles within the womb to be nourished, and to grow day by day, until it becomes a fully formed human being.

All people, therefore, were in the back of their father Adam (pth), and from him they were procreated. God says, ‘

We first created [the ancestors of] man from an essence of clay; then We made him semen in a firm residence. We made the semen into a clot, and the clot into a lump of flesh. This We fashioned into bones, then clothed the bones with flesh, thus bringing forth another Creation. Blessed is Al’lah, the Best of creators.

’ ﴿107﴾

The Creation of our master Adam (pth) was unique and an exception to the system through which the rest of humankind have come into this worldly life and multiplied. Almighty God created Adam’s body from soil. Then He sent his spirit into that body for, as we have learnt, Adam had no earthly father. It was the same with the Creation of our master Jesus, son of Mary (pth), when God sent the spirit of our master Jesus (pth) into his mother’s womb, carried by an angel. He did not use a human father to place this noble spirit within her. God says, ‘

For God, the example of Jesus is the same as that of Adam: He created him from soil, then He said to him ‘Be’, and he came into being.

’ ﴿108﴾

chapters.title: Who Is Adam (pth)?
chapters.html:
Adam (pth) is the first human being that God brought into existence on this earth and He made him the father of all humankind. All people were procreated from Adam and the lineages of all of them can be traced back to him. We see, therefore, that all people are children of this noble man: however far away their homes and countries may be, and however much their houses may vary, and despite the colour of their skin, they are all brothers and sisters.

God selected this Envoy, our master Adam (pth), because of the true love for Him and the yearning for perfection that He saw in his spirit. It was these undeniable attributes that ensured that Adam (pth) stood before his offspring as their first tutor. He showed them the ability of humans to surpass and rise high above all other creatures, giving them many outstanding examples through his own love for his Provider. Whoever follows such examples will be a virtuous human being whose perfection and great love for the Creator will promote them above all other aspects of Creation and give them the highest degree and standing in God’s Estimation.

The Almighty formed Adam’s perfect body from soil and then breathed his soul into it. Thus our master Adam (pth) came out to this world in the form of a perfect man and uniform human being. The noble verse indicates this, ‘

Well done is everything He has created and He started the Creation of Man from clay.

’ ﴿109﴾

God chose to create the first Man from the earth in order to create harmony between Man and the food which provides the necessary sustenance for their body, and from which it grows. As all plants, fruits and foods originate from soil and turn back to soil in the end, it is the same with the human body: from soil and back to soil. This is stated in the noble verse when God says, ‘

From earth We have created you and into it We shall return you and out of it We shall bring you once again [another time].

’ ﴿110﴾

chapters.title: Our Master Adam (pth), God’s Viceroy on Earth
chapters.html:
As previously mentioned, Mankind accepted the high position which God offered to all His Creation in the al- Azal world, as it would help them to acquire the highest degree of knowledge of their Provider and become worthy of enjoying greater shares of His Revelation. Adam (pth) was, on that great day, one of the true men who derived justice, wisdom, tenderness, compassion, and all the other qualities of perfection by their sublime flowing towards God. So, due to Adam’s (pth) truthfulness and his advance in the fields of love for God and His Creation, and his closeness to Him, and because of the qualifications of perfection that Al’lah scientifically recognised in him, his Provider chose him to be His successor on His Land. He was chosen for all the reasons above in order to establish justice and truth among all people, and to spread goodness and righteousness on the earth.

In fact, the successor of God is the exemplary being who is qualified to be God’s viceroy on this earth: he informs His creatures about His Orders, informs them about Him and, by keeping company with them, guides them into His Presence. We confirm that the rank of such succession is so great that the successor will be responsible for bearing the burden of carrying out the following three matters:

He will be the viceroy of God in delivering His Commands and Messages to His Creation.

He will be a ruler, watching over the execution of such Orders and helping the truth to be spread among His subjects.

He will be a centre for the descent of Godly Manifestations so that whoever attaches themselves to him will find him as a shining lamp to guide their spirits. In this way his companionship will help them to witness the Supreme Attributes of Al’lah and His Perfection.

The noble verse indicates this when God says, addressing our master David (pth), ‘

David, We have made you a successor in the land. Rule with justice among people.

’ ﴿111﴾

This successor holds the position of giving appropriate signs and guidance in addition to their position of ruling as viceroy. God says, ‘

Those men upon whom We bestowed the Book, wisdom, and Prophethood.

’ ﴿112﴾

Because of the knowledge of his Provider and His Supreme Attributes that the successor of God acquires, and due to the love and infatuation for his Creator that is impressed on his heart, he deserves to become a mediator between Al’lah and every human being in Creation. He informs them of His Orders, tells them about His Perfection and Supreme Attributes, and shows them the way that leads to knowledge of Him. If they attach themselves to him and approach God in his company, he will be like a shining lamp for them and escort their spirits into God’s Presence. By the light of this lamp they will be able to see an aspect of the Godly Names, witness Godly Perfection, and become infatuated with it. He will enable them to obtain a torch of the Godly Light by which they can see goodness and know that it is truly good, and see evil and know that it is really evil.

In this way, the successor’s relationship to Creation will be similar to that of a kindly father to his children, or a rational child to his siblings and parents. He will be the one who shows them the greatest affection and will be the most helpful to them.

For this reason, he will be the most beloved creature to God, the most honoured, the most highly-ranked and the one closest to Him. This is the degree of success for which humanity was created by God the Almighty and, too, this is the level which the noble angels wished to attain.

Before creating Adam (pth) and bringing him to this world Al’lah, the Almighty, told His angels that He would make a successor of His on earth. The noble verse serves, ‘

Then, your Provider said to the angels, “I will make a successor of Mine on earth.”

’ ﴿113﴾

The Angels’ Attitude towards Adam

God related this to His angels to make them fully aware of this human’s position so that their spirits would bind with him and enter into the Presence of their Creator in his company. In this way their knowledge about the Creator and their witnessing of Godly Perfection would increase even further. As the rank of such succession would result in the successor’s great closeness to the Creator, the angels wished to keep the honour of this great rank for themselves because of the innumerable blessings it leads to for its owner. Therefore, they addressed their Provider saying, ‘

Will You place on it those who will corrupt and shed blood?

’ – That is, ‘Will this creature do as the jinn have already done, and act as the devil and his offspring have previously behaved?’ Jinn-kind were created before humankind. The noble verse refers to this when God says, ‘

We created Man from dried clay, from purified mud heated [by God’s Light], and before [them] the jinn, from the pure flame of fire.

’ ﴿114﴾

The angels said this because they saw how Satan and his offspring had corrupted the land by shunning Al’lah. Then they continued, ‘While we glorify with Your Praise’ – Meaning that ‘We make the spirits of Your creatures glorify Your Favour by inspiring them, telling them about Your Charity and the great Care for which You are praised.’ The angels inspire you by saying, ‘Man, turn towards God, think and search for your own happiness. Spirit, obey God’s Words, contemplate the universe, and find the signs that signify Al’lah.’ ‘

And purify for You?

’ – ‘So, we purify their spirits by their entry into Your Presence; we purify them for You. We make them glorify the things for which You are praised, and purify their hearts so that they are fit to enter Your Presence. If You make us successors, we will do whatever will benefit Your creatures; we will be the means by which their spirits will be led to You and enter Your Presence.’ The Almighty then addressed them, ‘

He said, “I know what you do not know”

’ – That is, ‘I know things about the ability and the qualifications of this man that you do not know. Adam is superior to you and is even more elevated than you.’

Similarly, a perfect believer is more elevated than the noble angels, and any person has the potential to be higher than everything, although an unbeliever is the lowest of everything. The animal comes to this world and serves its purpose, and it will be punished in this world if it deviates from what it is supposed to do. It will have no resort to Fire on Doomsday for it receives its due punishment only in this lower life. As for the unbelievers, tomorrow they will throw themselves into the Fire; for even a dog is better than those people who do not believe.

The angels hoped, secretly, to be given such a rank of succession as they were sure of their truthfulness with their Creator and their loyalty to Him alone. They thought themselves worthy of this rank because of their excellent knowledge of His Supreme Names and their inclination to none but Him. So they said these words secretly because they did not know what degree of perfection had settled in Adam’s (pth) spirit and what great level of love for the Provider was enclosed within his heart. They were not aware that he was greatly superior to them in this field which, in fact, none of them could ever approach. This is why their Provider addressed them, saying, ‘

I know what you do not know.

’

God does not bestow His Favour on any of His Creation except with the utmost justice and according to the qualification and worthiness that they effectively demonstrate. So, too, as the spirit does not bind itself to any other spirit unless it personally observes its own excellence and superiority over it, the Almighty wanted to show the angels Adam’s efficiency, the perfection within his spirit and the love contained in his heart for his Creator. So, as previously mentioned, He created Adam from clay, formed his body perfectly and then breathed the soul into it. This is how Adam (pth) became a human being just as we are, with the same physical composition as anyone else.

When he (pth) came into this existence he looked at himself and then contemplated the universe and its harmony, so he could recognise his Creator and revere Him. Adam (pth) praised the Favour his Creator had shown him and appreciated His Charity. Through such praise and appreciation his spirit turned towards Almighty God, and entered into His Presence.

What Names Did God Teach to Adam?

The human spirit is like a clean mirror. Wherever you direct it, the image of whatever it is facing is printed upon it. In the same way, the spirit of our master Adam (pth) acquired impressions of the Godly Attributes, so that he gained knowledge of all of them. He witnessed aspects of the Wisdom of the Wise One, of the Sciences of the Omniscient, of the Potency of the Omnipotent, of the Compassion of the Compassionate One and other of God’s Supreme Attributes that caused him to bask in his own infatuation for his Creator and absorbed in seeing His Perfection.

The noble verse refers to this when God says, ‘

He taught Adam all the Names.

’ ﴿115﴾

– That is: the Compassionate, the Omniscient, the Omnipotent, the Patient, and all of the other Supreme Attributes of God are the Names He taught to our master Adam (pth). They are the Names of the Godly Presence which qualify one for the rank of successor to God on earth.

The one who attains knowledge of the Name of God the Compassionate, is worthy of being God’s viceroy to His creatures.

The reason for this is because Godly Mercy has been imprinted on his spirit, due to his love for God and his perfect leaning towards Him. The Almighty states this when He addresses His Envoy, our master Mohammad (cpth), ‘

By a bit of mercy from Al’lah, you [Prophet] were gentle [in your dealings] with them – had you been harsh, or hard-hearted, they would have dispersed and left you – so pardon them and ask forgiveness for them. Take counsel with them in the conduct of affairs; but when you are resolved [on a course of action], put your trust in Al’lah: Al’lah loves those who put their trust in Him.

’ ﴿116﴾

He also says, ‘

There has now come to you an Envoy of your own, one who grieves at your sinfulness and is solicitous over you, and to true believers he is clement and merciful.

’ ﴿117﴾

Through the compassion which was impressed on the spirit of the Envoy (cpth) – acquired through his closeness to his Creator – he became lenient with all humans, was kind in the way he treated them, was eager to guide them and point them in the right direction, and was tender and considerate with them. These qualities are required by the rank of succession, and they were present in the spirits of both our master Mohammad (cpth) and our master Adam (pth) before him. These qualities were also intrinsic in the spirits of every other Envoy, Prophet and leader, to a level in proportion to their entry into the Presence of their Creator and their closeness to Him.

Anyone who has not entered into Al’lah’s Presence and who has not had these Godly Attributes impressed on his spirit is not fit to rise to such a high position. God referred to the fulfilment of this quality in the spirits of the noble companions of His Envoy (cpth), saying, ‘

Mohammad, Al’lah’s Envoy, and those who keep company with him are strict with the unbelievers but merciful to one another.

’ ﴿118﴾

Returning to the words about our master Adam (pth), we say that he attained knowledge of God’s Attributes and Names – such as the Compassionate, the Just, the Clement, the Patient, the Forgiving and the other Names – because of the extent to which these qualities were imprinted on his own pure spirit; therefore he too had the same qualities and was merciful, just, patient and so forth, and he (pth) rightly deserved the level he attained.

With regard to what some people think, namely that the Almighty taught our master Adam (pth) the names of everyday items such as utensils, animals, plants and other objects and beings: this has nothing to do with the sublime meaning that is indicated by the noble verse, and does not fit with the context of the verses. For him to ascend to the rank of the successor of God on His land, and to become a leader and a guide for His servants, it would not be necessary for God to teach him the names of mundane items. Rather, what was required was that his heart should be coloured with kindness and mercy and various other perfect qualities.

Then after the superior knowledge that Adam (pth) attained about the Supreme Names of God and which none of the angels could attain, even though they are close to God, the Almighty wanted to show Adam’s (pth) position to the angels who requested such succession for themselves. He wanted also to demonstrate his worthiness to rise to this rank of succession and become a leader for them with whom they could enter into Al’lah’s Presence. So God ordered Adam to show the angels the Godly Attributes which had coloured his spirit, the impression of which had been imprinted on his spirit. Our master Adam (pth) showed these Names to the angels. That is what the noble verse denotes when God says, ‘

Then, he displayed them to the angels.

’

The Discussion between the Angels and Adam

Then our master Adam (pth) asked them about the meanings that were enfolded within God’s Supreme Attributes such as the Omnipotent, the Patient, the Omniscient and the Commissioner.

God ordered the angels to disclose whatever they knew about each of those Attributes when He says, ‘

Then, He said, “Tell Me about the Names of these”

’ – That is: ‘Tell Me the significance and the meanings of the Names that Adam showed to you.’ For example, they were to explain the meaning behind God’s Names such as: the Sovereign, the All-Powerful, the Subduer, and other Names, one after another. He did this because only those who are close to their Creator can understand the sublime meanings of God’s Supreme Attributes. ‘

“If you are truthful.”

’ – That is, in being competent to qualify for the succession. If they were genuine in this they should exceed Adam (pth) in levels of enlightenment. For such succession is not given haphazardly, but is granted to the one who surpasses all others, particularly his contemporaries, in his superior knowledge about God’s Supreme Names. Once he reaches this high degree of knowledge he will then become worthy of such a rank of succession.

Then the angels explained the knowledge they had, each according to the degree of its closeness to Al’lah. This is what the noble verse expressed, ‘

They said, “Glory to You.”

’ – Meaning ‘What great Perfection and Grandeur belong to You!’ ‘

“We have no science except what You taught us”

’ – That is: ‘We know nothing other than what You have taught us; we replied according to what we understood by entering into Your Presence and according to how truthful we were with You.’ ‘

“You are the Omniscient”

’ – That is: ‘You know everything about each one of us and about the level of our knowledge of Your Names.’ ‘

“The Wise.”

’ – That is: ‘All Your Actions are based on wisdom: You are Wise in Your acts and in Your choices. You allocate a degree of knowledge to every creature according to the truthfulness and closeness You receive from it. We do not say this as any kind of objection. We only wish to achieve that rank and hope to draw closer to You. You know best who is the most competent and worthy to attain such a high rank.’ God then wanted to show them Adam’s superior level of knowledge and his suitability for the rank of succession. He then ordered Adam (pth) to tell them about the Names of God which they spoke about, ‘

He said, “Adam, tell them about their Names.”

’ – That is: ‘Speak about My Supreme Names that they have explained and discussed, or alternatively, tell them about the Attributes you showed them.’ ‘

When he told them about their Names.

’ This refers to how Adam (pth) spoke to them in detail about the Godly Attributes that were shown to them, which revealed his scientific knowledge of them. It also revealed his level of advancement over the angels in that same knowledge and the expression of it. When he spoke about the Perfection of God which is encompassed within these Attributes, which was possible only because of his elevated entrance into the Presence of his Provider, his words surpassed all those of the angels so that his greater level of excellence could not be questioned. Then their Provider addressed them, as mentioned in the noble verse, ‘

God said, “Did I not say to you that I scientifically know the unseen of the heavens and the earth?”

’ – Meaning ‘Adam is higher than you,’ ‘

“And I scientifically know what you reveal.”

’ – Meaning ‘I already know the truth that you now acknowledge and reveal,’ ‘

“As well as what you were hiding.”

’ ﴿119﴾

– This means ‘What you were hiding by asking for the succession for yourselves.’

The Unseen World

The ‘

unseen

’ mentioned in the verse above refers to everything that is unknown to all the beings of Creation. It refers to hidden things, matters of which these beings have no knowledge, whether they are things which have already happened or will happen in the future; these hidden things encompass all that God has created or will create, whether in the heavens or on the earth. Almighty God has this all-encompassing knowledge because He is the Creator and the Originator of all things. Everything contained in the heavens or on the earth moves through Him and lives by His Sustenance: their very existence, their extent and their continuity depend on God’s unceasing Supply and Manifestation. He is Omniscient of every spirit and of all that it contains. Therefore He already knew what degree of knowledge the angels had in their spirits and the function that was suitable for each one according to one’s level of knowledge, just as He knew the qualifications and capacities of the great man, Adam (pth).

As for the beings of Creation, they know nothing except what they receive from God, not even what is concealed within their own spirits or what degree of science and knowledge they have. This was also the case with the angels when they secretly asked for the succession for themselves. They thought that they had sufficient competence to acquire that status, but were unaware of the precedence of our master Adam (pth) or of his level of eminence in that field. That is the reason God showed them the truth and revealed to them that their knowledge was of a lesser degree. We can understand from the statement ‘

As well as what you were hiding

’ that is contained in God’s Statement, ‘

I scientifically know what you reveal as well as what you were hiding

’, that when the angels asked, “

Will You place on it those who will corrupt and shed blood while we glorify with Your Praise and purify for You?”

their question was only a spiritual one, meaning that they said it secretly to themselves. Nonetheless, Almighty God was Aware of this and answered them in His Address to His angels; when the noble verses mention, ‘

He said

’ and ‘

they said

’, these were only spiritual words, uttered secretly.

Whenever the angels asked a question secretly, God projected the answer to the question into the same secret place from where it had originated. In this way He made them aware of the knowledge of our master Adam (pth) until such time as their spirits admitted His Wisdom, submitted to His Selection and His Omniscience, and surrendered to Him. Just as the statement ‘

I scientifically know what you reveal

’ shows us God’s Knowledge of what the angels revealed regarding their admitting the truth about Adam’s (pth) right of succession, their surrendering to God and confessing His Wisdom in His Choice, similarly, the statement ‘

As well as what you were hiding

’, that is, requesting the succession for themselves, shows us His Knowledge of all that they were concealing.

Almighty God mentioned these two sayings in order to make us aware of His Omniscience. There is no difference between His Knowledge of the secret things which a creature hides within itself and the open things spoken aloud, ‘

You have no need to speak aloud, for He has knowledge of all that is secret, and even of what is behind it.

’ ﴿120﴾

He also says, ‘

Whether you speak privately or openly, He knows what is centred in the chests, shall He Who has created all things not know them all? He is the All-Kind, the All-Knowing.

’ ﴿121﴾

Having revealed the meaning of the word ‘

Names

’ which means ‘Attributes’, as mentioned in the previous verses, we shall now answer the following question, why have we interpreted God’s Statement, ‘

He said, “Adam, tell them about their Names”

’ to mean that he should tell them about God’s Attributes which Adam had shown them, although the word in the noble verse was ‘

their Names

’ rather than ‘My Names’?

We explain it as follows: we have seen that the purpose of this account is simply to show us the eminence of our master Adam (pth) and his superiority over the noble angels in his knowledge of God’s Attributes. This was what had made him worthy of rising to the rank of succession. We have also clarified that this implies that the intended meaning of the word ‘

Names

’ mentioned in this account is the ‘Godly Attributes’. The course of this account clearly refutes any other meaning. Therefore the repetition of the word ‘

Names

’ in this narrative emphasises that they are the Godly Names. It is clear, therefore, that the words ‘

their Names

’ do not mean the angels’ names, but means the Godly Names that were shown to them. To know the names of the angels would not be a reason to grant our master Adam (pth) greater spiritual value before God; nor would it give him a higher rank than that of the angels.

You may ask why we do not interpret the statement ‘

When he told them about their Names

’ to refer to what they knew about the Names of their Provider. If we explained the meaning of the verse in such a way, our master Adam (pth) would not then have risen to a level surpassing that of all the angels, because he could only have told them something that they already knew. Consequently, he would not have deserved his succession nor could he have risen to a rank higher than that of the angels, since he would not have added any further enlightenment in relation to the Names that were shown to them. He would merely have been at the same level as any one of them. Thus by speaking to them about the Godly Names that were shown to them and giving them an exalted revelation he advanced beyond them all.

The Difference between ‘Their Names’ and ‘My Names’

Now we shall reveal the difference between the words ‘

their Names

’ as mentioned in the noble verses and the words ‘My Names’ which are the subject of our discussion. If the address in the noble verse had been ‘Tell them about My Names’ instead of ‘

Tell them about their Names

’, the meaning would have been completely different: the statement ‘tell them about My Names’ would mean that Adam should have given them comprehensive knowledge about each of His Names. As no creature can have comprehensive knowledge of the Name ‘the Compassionate’, or know the degree of God’s Compassion in order to fully acquaint other people with it – as is also the case with the Name ‘the Omniscient’ and all of the other Godly Names – the verse did not say, ‘Tell them about My Names’ but ‘

Tell them about their Names

’ – That is: ‘Those of their Names which you have displayed to them and which they have explained.’ This was in order to disclose the degree of Adam’s knowledge of them, and the perfection they contained, according to his nearness to God.

In fact, nobody knows the Attributes of Al’lah except Al’lah the Almighty, and no one can have comprehensive knowledge of them because they are both limitless and eternal. The fact is that a person can only witness the Godly Names to a level that is in proportion to their closeness to Al’lah, the Almighty; therefore they can acquaint others with only a limited degree of knowledge of God’s Mercy, Clemency, Omniscience and other Attributes.

Al’lah is Vast and Omniscient. No matter what level of knowledge of God’s Attributes you attain, these Attributes are infinitely more extensive than this; whatever rank you reach in that knowledge, your Provider (Glory to Him) is higher still and more sublime. Above even the most knowledgeable there is always the One Who is All-Knowing.

When Adam’s (pth) precedence over the noble angels in his knowledge of God’s Attributes was made apparent to them, God ordered them to enter into His Presence accompanied by Adam. This was so they would accept him as a shining light for their spirits and the leader in their entry into His Presence. And so He ordered them to prostrate themselves before our master Adam (pth). God says, ‘

Then We said to the angels, “Prostrate yourselves before Adam.”

’ – That is: ‘Ask to gain science and knowledge through him. Connect yourselves with him in order to enter into My Presence, and thereby view wonderful panoramas higher and more sublime than yours.’ Then ‘

They prostrated themselves.

’ ﴿122﴾

– All of them.

God’s Purpose behind His Order of Prostration

You may ask, what is this prostration which the Almighty ordered the angels to do?

Prostration is explained as follows: it is asking for what you need through spiritual submission and appreciation. To prostrate oneself to God means to ask Him for help and sustenance.

The Almighty God referred to this meaning in many verses of the Holy Qur’an, such as when He says, ‘

Do you not see how all that is in the heavens and on the earth, [including] the sun and the moon and the stars, the mountains and the trees, the beasts, the countless oblivious people and many who deserve the scourge: all prostrate themselves before Al’lah?

’ ﴿123﴾

He also says, ‘

All who dwell in the heavens and on the earth prostrate themselves before God willingly or unwillingly; they have their shadows, morning and evening.

’ ﴿124﴾

In another verse He says, ‘

The star and the trees prostrate themselves.

’ ﴿125﴾

The prostration before God of all those who dwell in the heavens and on the earth, and of the sun and the moon and the stars, of the mountains and the trees, of the animals: this is nothing but their surrender to Him because they need Him. They are asking Him to continue to provide them with life, because if this divine Providence leaves them for even the blink of an eye, they will no longer exist and no trace of them will remain. For this reason, everything in the universe submits to God, continually directing itself toward Him and is, therefore, sustained by Him.

We understand from the above that prostration is not intended as the bowing of the head and placing forehead, palms of the hands and the feet on the ground, as understood by the average person. In reality this physical position is only a symbol and an expression of the submission of the spirit. The spirit prostrates to someone when it appreciates the favour received from them or wants to request something from them. When we prostrate ourselves during our communication with God, it means that we thank our Creator for His Favour in teaching us and guiding us to what leads to our wellbeing and happiness. In the same way we ask for His Help and Support in order to be able to apply the sublime instructions He gave us after reading the Opening Fortress (

al-Ftiha Surah

).

There is another prostration: this is the prostration to those people whose rank and knowledge you revere so as to receive more from them. Through such appreciation and this request for more, you attach yourself to them. If they are believers, you will enter the spirit of the Envoy (pth) through them and by this entry you become able to witness God’s Perfection. This is called intercession.

chapters.title: The Reality of Intercession
chapters.html:
The nature of the human spirit means that it is predisposed to appreciate Godly Perfection. However, for this appreciation and glorification the spirit needs an eye with which to see and witness. The human eye enables us to see only those things which have shape and form and are illuminated by means of physical lights such as the light of the sun, the moon, electricity and other means.

Regarding the eye of the heart, that is the heart of the spirit, or the third eye, it sees only by the Light of Al’lah which comes to His Envoy (cpth). This Light is not only everlasting but constantly increasing. Physical lights, on the other hand, are faint and insignificant compared to the Light of Al’lah, and only a slight touch of the Light of the Great Creator (Glory to His Names). If a spirit were to enter into Al’lah’s Presence during its communication with Him, and thereby acquired perfection for itself it would gain this ability and would attain that eye which, when opened, would enable it to witness the Godly Perfection. Then if this believer was to look around, they would soon see the people of perfection and notice how they also followed this glorious way, and would love them. The higher the level of perfection that these people of perfection attain above that of this believer, the more love and passion they will feel towards them, the more appreciation they inspire, and the more magnificence they will have. Since the Envoy (cpth) is superior to all other believers in this field, as he (cpth) is the master of the people of perfection and holds the highest rank, being the nearest one to God, you will find that a believer will love God’s Envoy (cpth).

This believer will revere him due to the perfection which they attained from their Provider. For a true believer there is no human being with a more elevated rank or with greater prestige than God’s Envoy (cpth). When they hear somebody mention the Envoy (cpth) their love for him will be kindled and their spirit will surge towards the Envoy (cpth) like a flash of lightning; this spirit will then accompany him and be connected with his noble spirit. However, the states of these beloved are so elevated that they cannot truly be compared to anything, or be said to resemble anything else.

The love that this believer has for the Envoy (cpth) will expand gradually, and their link with him and their communication with God through him will keep on rising. They will continue to advance along the path of appreciation, glorification and reverence until they reach a state when the two spirits have coupled with one another. This will form a bond of appreciation, love and reverence for the Envoy (cpth). This is true intercession. As the spirit of the Envoy (cpth) is always in attendance in God’s Presence, a believer who is bound to the Envoy (cpth) is qualified to enter into God’s Presence in his company. At the moment of entry, by the light of the Envoy (cpth) – that is, the one sent by God to be a shining light and a mercy for all worlds – this believer will see the Light of God, by which they will witness an aspect of Al’lah’s Attributes. They will then become passionate about what they see and will prostrate themself before the Presence of God, fully absorbed in observing God’s Attributes. They will observe how Al’lah manifests Himself through the Name ‘the Compassionate’, overwhelming all of Creation with His endless Compassion; they will see how, through the Name ‘the Clement’, He surrounds all of Creation with His Clemency. They will view all of the other Godly Names, such as the Wise, the Omniscient, the Most High, the Grand, a viewing that causes them to become totally absorbed in those Names and fully surrender to this Merciful and Kind Provider. It is their link with the Envoy (cpth) and their communication with God through him (cpth) which will have led them to such great Godly Favour, such high witnessing, and eternal happiness. On my life, we say that is true intercession.

It is an intercession of love for, and spiritual company with, that noble and venerable spirit (cpth).

Evidence and Examples of Intercession

In Arabic, the word ‘intercession’ means ‘coupling’, derived from the word ‘couple’, and refers to two things which are bound to each other and remain linked together. The noble verse refers to this spiritual link with the Envoy (cpth) and to this true intercession and binding when God says, ‘

Al’lah and His angels keep in communication with the Prophet. You who believe, communicate yourselves with Al’lah through him and fully surrender.

’ ﴿126﴾

‘

Communicate yourselves with Al’lah through him

’ – That is, connect your spirits to the noble spirit of the Envoy (cpth) so that he will facilitate your ascension into God’s Presence, because communication with Al’lah is a link between a human being and their Provider, and it cannot be accomplished except through the mediator (cpth). God says, ‘

When you [Mohammad] are in them, and you establish communication [prayer] with God for them.

’ ﴿127﴾

This communication does not only refer to the prayers of people moving and prostrating their body. Correct communication is accomplished when the Envoy (cpth) is in your spirit and you enter, accompanied by him, into Al’lah’s Presence. This is the reality of true communication. The Almighty did not say, ‘When you are among them’, so true communication is performed by intercession with the Envoy (cpth), and then the link with God is attained through his companionship.

To perform communication the Envoy (cpth) must be in your spirit, because entering God’s Presence is achieved through the company and intercession of the one (cpth) that God sent to take you back to Him, the Almighty. Through this intercession he (cpth) teaches you how to pray. After he says to you, ‘

In the Name of God, the All-Compassionate, the All-Merciful

’ he then says, ‘

Praise is to God.

’ – ‘Oh my brother.’ ‘

The Provider of all worlds.

’ This is communication with Al’lah. Then, when he (cpth) recites God’s Orders to you, you bow in obedience and submit to the Great God, and prostrate yourself asking for God’s Help to obey Him. Without this spiritual link and the company of God’s Envoy (cpth), and without communication with God through him (cpth), the believer would not have attained this transcendence; nor would they have attained such insight and witnessing or their total surrender to God.

Intercession Is the Way and Means Leading to Piety (Seeing by Al’lah’s Light)

After that spiritual journey in communication, the believer returns having had Al’lah’s Light kindled in their spirit. It was lit in their heart by their love for their Creator after they witnessed Al’lah’s Perfection, and because of what they observed of His Sympathy, Tenderness, Clemency and Mercy for all His creatures. In fact, love is not attained until after this witnessing. Do you know what benefit is brought by this Godly Light that is ignited in the heart of the believer? Through this Light they will see the reality that is hidden behind the external image. Thus they will not be seduced by the shapes or forms of things, nor will they be deceived by the images of people. Their eye of discernment will be opened and they will be able to see by Al’lah’s Light, and so this believer will have become a person who can distinguish virtue from vice and truth from falsehood. They will see what is good and know that it is really good, and will therefore be inclined towards it, just as they will see what is evil and know that it is really evil, and so will loathe and renounce it. That is the sublime degree to which every person should rise, and that is piety – seeing by Al’lah’s Light – which can be achieved through intercession.

This is what God the Almighty urged believers to attain when He prompted them, ‘

You who believe, seek piety [see by Al’lah’s Light] and believe in His Envoy. He will grant you two portions of His Compassion and make a light for you by which you can go, and He will forgive you. Al’lah is All-Forgiving and All-Merciful.

’ ﴿128﴾

He also says, ‘

You who believe, if you become pious [illuminated by Al’lah’s Light], He will grant you the power of discrimination and veil your sins from you and forgive you. Al’lah is of great bounty.

’ ﴿129﴾

We confirm that piety means to see by Al’lah’s Light, and it is a result of your intercession with God’s Envoy (cpth) and your entry into God’s Presence with him (cpth). With this, your spirit will become illuminated by Al’lah’s Light which will protect you from falling into the abyss of sin and wrongdoing. The person to whom Al’lah has not granted a Light will never find it. Intercession, then, is a spiritual state. The Envoy (cpth) made the greatest and highest approach towards his Provider; this is the Envoy (cpth) upon whom the greatest Manifestation and the brightest Light and Support descend from Al’lah; if he directs his spirit towards those of his companions who come close to him, and who believe in his mission and in what he brought to them from Al’lah, then that Godly Light will flow through the Envoy (cpth) and enter into his companions and those who believe in him (cpth). In this way the great Envoy (cpth) will be a mediator between God and His Creation, and a means to lessen the intensity of that Manifestation in order that the spirit can receive it and support it; that is the reality of intercession. God says, ‘

Those who pray seek the means to approach their Provider, the nearest means. They crave His Mercy and fear His Punishment.

’ ﴿130﴾

And so we understand that intercession is not for the disobedient or for the people who carry out terrible deeds. If Al’lah, the Almighty, manifests Himself directly to the hearts of people without the Envoy’s (cpth) mediation, it will overwhelm their spirits which will crack and be unable to bear that Godly Manifestation. They will be in such a state of shock that they may lose their minds because of the force of that Light, as happened with those who went to meet God with our master Moses (pth). They were shocked because they did not appreciate him. However, your Provider is Wise and therefore He chose the Envoys (ptt) who were the most loving men to Him from among all the people, and who were the most able to bear His Light so that they could be mediators between Him and His servants.

It was because of God’s Mercy and Tenderness for His Creation that He ordered the Envoy (cpth) to direct his noble spirit towards the believers in order to be a means for the Godly Light to flow into their hearts, and to be a mediator between them and their Provider. They then receive purification and forgiveness by means of this Light and regain their spiritual wellbeing. God says, ‘

And communicate their spirits with God through your spirit, for your communication will give them comfort. Al’lah knows all and hears all.

’ ﴿131﴾

The prostration of our master Joseph’s father, mother and brothers demonstrates their veneration and appreciation of Joseph’s knowledge after they realised his precedence and excellence over and above them in his knowledge of, and belief in, Al’lah.
