Through such admiration and reverence for him their spirits were bound to his and entered into God’s Presence with him. This is indicated by the noble verse wherein God says, ‘

He raised his parents to the throne while they fell in prostration before him. He said, “Oh father, this is the interpretation of my old vision; my Provider has fulfilled it.”

’ ﴿132﴾

This meaning is also confirmed in the noble verse which details the submission of the magicians to our master Moses (pth). God says, ‘

We inspired Moses, “Now throw down your staff,” and thereupon it swallowed up their false device. Thus, the truth prevailed and their actions proved to be in vain. They were defeated and put to shame, and the enchanters prostrated themselves before Moses.

’ ﴿133﴾

In spite of their great number and their powerful tricks, when these magicians were shown how our master Moses (pth) had frustrated their tricks they appreciated his knowledge and praised it, and their spirits drew near to him, submitting to his great knowledge. Through their spiritual approach to him, and through his pure and chaste spirit, reality was revealed to them clearly and plainly; no sooner had they submitted than ‘

They said, “We have believed in the Provider of the worlds, the Provider of Moses and Aaron.”

’ ﴿134﴾

When Pharaoh threatened them with terrible punishment and crucifixion, they addressed him with the truth that their spirits had witnessed and they paid no attention to his intimidation, ‘

They said, “We shall never prefer you to the clear signs which have come to us, nor to Him Who has created us. Therefore do your worst, you can only decide matters of this present life. We have put our faith in our Provider so that He may forgive us our sins and the witchcraft you have forced us to practise. Better is Al’lah and more Lasting. He that comes before his Provider laden with sin shall be consigned to Hell, where he shall neither live nor die. But he that comes before Him with true faith and good deeds shall be exalted to the highest ranks, gardens of lasting bliss under which the rivers flow and there they will stay. Such shall be the recompense of those who purify themselves.”

’ ﴿135﴾

One wonders how the magicians were able to disclose such a revelation, although they had been brought directly to Pharaoh from different cities, and had never met our master Moses (pth) previously or even heard of any of his guidance. In fact, simply by praising and appreciating his knowledge their spirits became bound to his so that they entered into God’s Presence by means of him. There they witnessed reality and spoke the words that indicated their undeniable faith. They are, in this respect, like the Queen of Sheba (Saba’) who extolled the possessions of our master Solomon (pth) when ‘

She was bidden to enter the edifice; when she saw it, she thought it was a pool of water and bared her legs. But Solomon said, “It is an edifice paved with glass.”

’ She then despised her own possessions and admired those of our master Solomon (pth), as well as his great prestige. No sooner she had looked at him with eyes full of admiration than her spirit entered into God’s Presence through his chaste spirit. Her words expressed her spiritual state, for, ‘

She said, “My Provider, I have done wrong to myself. Now I submit with Solomon to God, the Provider of the worlds.”

’ ﴿136﴾

Appreciation (One of the Rules of the Spirit) and Its Results

This is an important point. Our behaviour is affected by the appreciation and admiration that our spirit has for another that surpasses our own in some respect. This admiration can decide the course that a person takes and can determine their direction in life. That is because the spirit that appreciates and admires another spirit becomes strongly attached to it, and will always accompany it wholeheartedly. That is one of the firm rules of the spirit that was set down by its Creator. You will find no replacement for God’s Rules, and you will find no change in God’s Laws. However, this appreciation and reverence for others differs from one spirit to another, according to what one likes and what their spirit inclines towards. Some spirits glorify others because of their science and knowledge, their possessions and position of authority, their perfection and high morals, or for various other considerations. That is because each person has preferred inclinations and favourite interests on which they focus above all else. For this reason, people only appreciate those who surpass them in these things and who excel to a greater extent than them in these respects. This is why the brothers of our master Joseph (pth) – and his parents too – appreciated his perfection, because their spirits preferred virtue and perfection to all else in this life.

As for the Pharaoh’s magicians, who were experts in the science of magic, they deferred to the superior knowledge of our master Moses (pth) after he showed them what had defeated their entire repertoire of magic. No sooner had he thrown down his staff for it to swallow up all of their false devices than they prostrated themselves before him (pth).

Balqees, the Queen of Sheba, also prostrated herself before our master Solomon (pth). She admired him only because she had great possessions; the moment that she eyed his possessions, she was in awe of him because his possessions were greater than hers. Then her spirit became bound to his, submitting to Al’lah, the Almighty. This admiration and spiritual submission causes that which is enfolded within superior spirits to be reflected onto the lesser spirits that appreciate them, and this quality is then imprinted on the surface of the latter.

The supremacy of our master Joseph (pth) in his love for Al’lah and his knowledge about His Attributes was reflected onto the spirits of his parents and siblings, so that he became a leader for them in this field. We saw that the faith and knowledge that were enfolded within the spirit of our master Moses (pth) were reflected onto the spirits of the magicians, who then spoke certain words. What happened between the Queen of Sheba and our master Solomon (pth) was similar. So, if you admire a person you will surely enter in the same way that they do, and will drink from the same spiritual springs they drink from, so that their spiritual state will be impressed upon your spirit too. But be aware that if they are a disbeliever, the contents of their spirit will be clearly manifested in your spirit.

However, if they possess perfection and faith, you will sense this perfection and enter with them through the portals of true belief. That is why the Envoy Mohammad (cpth) said, when invoking God, ‘

Oh, God of all! May You not let a disbeliever oblige me, lest my heart will love him.

’ ﴿137﴾

He (cpth) implored God in this way because he knew the rules of the spirit and he was afraid that goodness might reach him at the hands of a disbeliever. If this happened his heart (cpth) would incline towards the disbeliever and then be affected by his spiritual state. Look at God’s Envoy (cpth), the master of Creation, and how he invokes this supplication so as to preserve the pureness of his own spirit. What kind of state, then, would we find ourselves in if our spirits were to appreciate and glorify people who were unfaithful and inclined to disbelief? In contrast, what would our state be if our hearts were to incline towards God’s Envoy (cpth), with admiration and reverence? These facts are also proved by his (cpth) saying, ‘

Man adopts his close friend’s faith; you should therefore be careful when choosing an intimate friend.

’ ﴿138﴾

However, the path of glorifying God’s Envoy (cpth) and appreciating the people of perfection who came after him as guides is available to you only if you yourself are one of the people of perfection, for only those who are perfect can appreciate perfection.

Thus, if you want to accompany God’s Envoy (cpth) spiritually, you should contemplate these cosmic signs until you believe, without any doubt, that there is no god but Al’lah. If you really believe, your faith will prevent you from disobeying Al’lah, and will ensure that you straighten yourself out for His Orders. Then you will be confident that Al’lah is Pleased with you, and your spirit will approach Him, the Almighty, and will derive perfection from Al’lah through communicating with Him. This will cause you to appreciate and praise those who surpass you in perfection, and you can then enter into the spirit of the master of the perfect ones (cpth) by means of them. Appreciating God’s Envoy (cpth) and coupling with him enables your spirit to enter into God’s Presence through him, and to rise in the realms of Godly Love. God says, ‘

Oh, spirit in rest and satisfaction! Return to your Provider, well-pleased and wellpleasing. Enter into My servants, and enter My Paradise.

’ ﴿139﴾

We shall leave this topic here and return to talk about the way of true belief in detail at the end of this research.

The Angels’ Prostration to Adam

So the noble angels prostrated themselves before our master Adam (pth) when ordered to do so by Al’lah, the Almighty. As soon as they realised Adam’s superiority and excellence in perfection and scientific knowledge they all prostrated themselves before him. Their obeisance to him (pth) expressed their appreciation and spiritual submission to the position of this noble Envoy (pth) and confirmed their request to enter the Presence of the Great Creator in his company.

This is the reality of intercession: it is a combination of, and an association between, two spirits and their companionship in the way of approaching God. The weak attach their spirit to the strong to help them to attain spiritual elevation, reflections of perfect qualities and to enable the weak to mount the ladders of sacredness and perfection. The spirit of the weak one will increasingly acquire sublime love, divine knowledge and nearness to God from the spirit of the strong one: namely, the Envoy. And indeed, the spirits of the angels were bound to the spirit of Adam (pth) in order to ascend to the High Presence of God in his (pth) company, just as the spirits of the noble Envoys (ptt) ascended by means of the spirit of our Envoy Mohammad (cpth) in the Night Journey, ﴿140﴾

through the elevators of holiness and perfection.

In fact, there are many of God’s Purposes behind His mentioning this story in the Holy Qur’an; one of these Purposes is that He wanted to draw our attention to the great benefits of connection with the elevated spirits. We should, therefore, take the noble angels’ prostration to Adam (pth) as the perfect example for us to follow and a pattern that we should imitate.

chapters.title: Who Are the Jinn - kind?
chapters.html:
Who Are the Jinn-kind?

As shown before, in the world of

al-Azal

and the first Creation (the world of incorporeal spirits) which preceded our coming to this material world, we have seen Godly Justice manifested throughout the whole of Creation in the most splendid raiment of perfection. The Almighty did not prefer some people to others or create a particular group to be prophets and another group to be disbelievers. Instead, each man had the free will to choose and then their choice was fulfilled.

Thus, the Almighty did not make one person into a disbeliever and another into a believer, nor did He create a devil in the first world, the world of

al-Azal

. The distinction and differentiation between the ranks arose due to the differing degrees of spiritual direction towards God that became evident, and the various degrees of constant communication with Him and adherence to Him. It was also due to the differences in the level of shunning Him and of turning towards other things rather than to God, and of the level of immersion in desires and withdrawal from Him (Glory to His Names).

For further clarification, we add the following: when Al’lah the Almighty offered the bearing of the Trust to the spirits in the

al-Azal

world, there were spirits who accepted what was offered and others who refused. Then when He wished to temper the covenant by exposing those spirits who bore the Trust to desire, those who agreed to shoulder the Trust became distinguished from one another. The Almighty looked into all of the spirits to see their truthfulness towards Him, and He found they were not all the same. There were some spirits who plunged into yearnings and desires till these intensified inside them, thus reducing their capacities and abilities to reach the higher grades of approaching Al’lah the Almighty than those who undertook the charge of mankind. He called them ‘Jinn’ which means ‘the veiled ones’ in Arabic, as He concealed them and separated them from the world of mankind who were less absorbed in their yearnings. This can be compared to separating the hardworking student from the lazy one who has limited abilities, in case the latter might affect him if they were together at school. Jinn-kind could never reach the ranks of Prophecy as they themselves state in the noble verse when the Almighty says, ‘

Some of us are righteous and others less so; we follow different paths.

’ ﴿141﴾

Because of their debility Al’lah the Almighty made physical qualities for them to suit the desires of their spirits, and so that their spirits remained surrounding their bodies. Their shapes do not differ from those of mankind but fire is the essence of the Creation of their bodies, whereas man was created from mud. Thus, the differentiation was according to the capacities of each, and the purpose in separating them from mankind was to avoid the effect of their weakness upon our faith. Those whose spirits exit their world to enter the world of mankind are named ‘devils’, and those of humankind whose spirits deteriorate to the level of the jinns’ world are called ‘devils’ too. Their world is like ours, the earth is one and so is the universe, they function as we do: they eat and drink, intermarry and breed.

Similarly, because of Al’lah’s Mercy and Tenderness for the human race, He made them of two kinds (men and women) and separated them from each other (when He ordered women to be veiled from the men except those whom He defined in the Holy Qur’an) since women have fewer abilities than men. That is why the Almighty entrusted men with them so that they should help them to enter Paradise. God says, ‘

Men are in charge of women.

’ ﴿142﴾

There are many verses which show that the word ‘Man’, as mentioned in the verse ‘

Man bore it

’, includes both humankind and jinn-kind; for example, when God says, ‘

I created jinn-kind and mankind only to worship Me. I want no provision from them nor do I want them to feed Me.

’ ﴿143﴾

So both of them are in charge of worship, because they will both be asked about their sins, as mentioned in God’s Saying, ‘

On that Day neither mankind nor jinn will be asked about their sins! Which, then, of your Provider’s Blessings do you both deny? The guilty will be known by their mark and will be seized by their foreheads and their feet.

’ ﴿144﴾

This signifies that in the Hereafter all matters will be exposed because the two angels will have registered the deeds of everyone of mankind and jinn-kind and there will be no discussion: the good will be taken immediately to Paradise, and the bad to Hell and then to the Fire.

And in another of God’s Sayings, ‘

Oh you assembly of jinns and men! Did there not come to you Envoys of your own, setting forth unto you My Revelations

’ ﴿145﴾

– which denotes that there is also an admonition for both of them. From this we see that God never actually created a devil at all. He created only mankind and jinn-kind both of whom undertook possession of their own free will without any external coercion or favouritism, so that the results and consequences of their own deeds, be they good or bad, would fall upon them both.

chapters.title: Who Was the First Devil? How Did He Become a Devil?
chapters.html:
The Almighty ordered the angels to prostrate themselves before Adam (pth), ‘

Then, We said to the angels, “Prostrate yourselves before Adam

”. They prostrated themselves’ – meaning that they all obeyed God as they knew that He was their Creator and Provider. That is, all obeyed ‘

except Lucifer [Satan]

’ for he was one of the jinn-kind. The Almighty had brought him together with the angels and let him attend that festival of prostration so as to elevate his rank and uplift him. But because of his ignorance Lucifer rejected it and did not prostrate himself. He had mistaken what was right for what was wrong and therefore he was called Iblis, the Arabic word which denotes this state. Lucifer knew nothing about Al’lah except that He was the Creator. He was the one ‘

who rejected

’ the Direction to prostrate himself ‘

and disdained

’ Adam, saying that he was greater and better than Adam. ‘

He was one of the disbelievers.

’ – This means that he failed to think of God’s Signs. If he had given them some thought and honoured them, he would have submitted to Adam (pth) and acquired a great share of perfection and happiness. But by refusing to do so and being disdainful it indicates that he did not know his Provider. ‘

He [Lucifer] said, “Do I prostrate myself to whom You have created out of mud?”

’ ﴿146﴾

– What he meant was that Adam was not like him. He also said, ‘

“I am better than he; You have created me out of fire but him out of mud.”

’ ﴿147﴾

Although Lucifer had entered the Heaven of our great master Adam (pth); although he had tasted the Godly Manifestation that had descended upon our master Adam (pth); although he had witnessed the world of angels who had been immersed in Adam’s Paradise (just as he had), and who had all prostrated themselves together: he was, nevertheless, envious of Adam’s rank (pth), and failed to revere him (pth) due to his own egotism.

Therefore, he did not prostrate himself but turned away and withdrew from Adam (pth) and from Al’lah. Thus he deviated from what was right and deprived himself of the heart life that had come to him from the Living One, the Sustainer. The springs of his spirit dried up until they became inflamed and they burned, and he turned into a mutinous devil. The word for ‘devil’ in Arabic is shaitan, a portmanteau word in idiomatic language, a blending of two Arabic verbs: shatana and shata which mean ‘to draw far away’ and ‘to be burned’. So, Iblis drew far away until he burned with the flames of his distance from God and His Envoy Adam (pth) and he became a devil. The word for ‘mutinous’ in Arabic is marid, another portmanteau word blending two Arabic verbs: radda meaning ‘to refuse’ and rada which means ‘to seek’. So the devil set about refusing what was right and seeking what was false.

In another verse the devil also said, ‘

See You? This is the one whom You have honoured above me!

’ thereby accusing God of injustice when He chose Adam (pth) over him. He did not realise that Adam (pth) acquired that rank because of his truthfulness before his Provider, and his adherence, love and obedience to Him. The devil continued, ‘

“If You give me respite till the Day of Resurrection, I will surely bring his descendants under my sway, all but a few!”

’ ﴿148﴾

– This was how he ascribed actions to himself; and since that time, blinded by his own envy, he declared himself to be the enemy of Adam’s children. This is mentioned in another Fortress where he says, ‘

“I will take of Your servants a portion marked off,”

’ which means that anyone who follows him will be his. He then continues by saying, ‘

“I will mislead them, and I will raise vain hopes in them.”

’ – That is, he would cause his followers to become driven by the deception of their wishes and daydreams, and would ‘

“order them to slit the ears of cattle.”

’ – Although it is claimed that this procedure is done to prevent cattle from being alarmed, actually it causes them to suffer intense pain. They do what the devil said with the words, ‘

“I shall order them to tamper with Al’lah’s Creation.”

’ – Meaning, just as they castrate sheep. Actually, castration does make sheep grow fatter, but it also means that they have no energy or nourishment within them. ‘

Indeed, whoever, forsaking God, takes Satan for a friend, has of a surety suffered a loss that is manifest.

’ ﴿149﴾

– And this is so because his sole purpose is to cause harm to the whole of humanity.

The noble angels prostrated themselves to Adam (pth) because of the perfection enfolded within their spirits as the result of their direction to Al’lah, whereas the devil knew nothing about Godly Perfection, acquired no scientific knowledge of Al’lah’s Attributes, nor did he enter into God’s Presence even once. His spirit, therefore, failed to become coloured with any of the tints of perfection. This foolish and ignorant being did not glorify his Provider. Therefore, when the Almighty ordered him to prostrate himself before our master Adam (pth), he ‘

rejected and disdained this. He was one of the disbelievers.

’ ﴿150﴾

The Holy Qur’an refers to the devil’s refusal and his arrogance in other verses, such as the following words of the Almighty, ‘

Then We said to the angels, “Prostrate yourselves before Adam.” They all prostrated themselves, except Lucifer who said, “Do I prostrate myself to one whom You have created out of mud?”

’ ﴿151﴾

In another verse, ‘

We said to the angels, “Prostrate yourselves before Adam.” Then they prostrated themselves, except Lucifer who was one of the jinn-kind; he disobeyed his Provider’s Command.

’ ﴿152﴾

Through these exalted verses you can see that the devil’s disdain for prostration and his refusal to do so resulted from his disbelief in his Creator. He was, therefore, blind to the truth, and the perfection of our master Adam (pth) was concealed from him.

chapters.title: What Is the Meaning of Disbelief?
chapters.html:
The Almighty said about the devil that ‘

He was one of the disbelievers.

’ The word ‘

was

’ denotes that Lucifer was a disbeliever before the Almighty ordered His angels to prostrate themselves to Adam (pth). As for the statement ‘

one of the disbelievers

’, it means that the devil was ungrateful for the Grace of the Creator, unthankful for God’s Favour. In fact, disbelief is not meant to be the denial of the Existence of the Creator or the refusal to acknowledge Him. Rather, it is to be blind to the Godly Graces, to turn away from the Benefactor and feel ungrateful for His Favour. The following verses refer to this meaning and reveal Satan’s confession and acknowledgement of his Provider and Creator. The Almighty says, ‘

They all prostrated themselves, except Lucifer who said, “Do I prostrate myself to one whom You have created out of mud?”

’ ﴿153﴾

And in another verse, Lucifer said, ‘

“I am better than he; You have created me out of fire but him out of mud?”’ ﴿154﴾

Also, he said to his Provider, ‘

“My Provider, give me respite to the Day when they will be resurrected.”

’ ﴿155﴾

Lucifer, as stated in these verses and others mentioned in the Holy Qur’an, originally confessed to the Existence of the Creator and His Providence, yet his spirit holds no trace of appreciation of God’s Favour and Graces. He did not approach his Creator once nor did he have any knowledge about His Perfection or inclination towards Him.

What we understand here is that unless a human ponders upon the Graces of the Creator and sees God’s Favour conferred upon them, they are not true believers, even if they admit the Existence of their Creator. As long as their state remains the same, whereby they are unable to recognise the rank of the noble Envoys (ptt), their spirits will fail to bind with those of the Envoys and enter the Presence of Al’lah in their company.

Rather, they will remain rejected, distant from these noble men and, as a consequence, distant from Al’lah.

In addition, based on the previous verses, we can refute many of the wrongful claims which some people adopt, such as when they say that Lucifer was the leader of the angels and that he had devoted himself to the worship of God. He, according to their claim, did not leave even the smallest spot in the sky where he did not prostrate himself to God. However, in one such moment all his deeds came to nothing. People who make such false claims seek to sow doubts about God’s Justice in people’s hearts and to make them mistrust the benefit of their good deeds.

All these pretences disagree with the open Qur’an; for, as we have seen, Lucifer had not once entered the Presence of his Creator nor had he ever prostrated himself to Him. On the contrary, he was one of the disbelievers. Apart from this, he was not an angel, but one of the jinn-kind as mentioned previously. Indeed, disbelief and lack of perfection prevent the sight of the spirit from witnessing reality, confine it to perceiving only the form, and attaching it to capricious notions. This is what happened to the devil who alleged that fire was better than mud, and did not know that knowledge of Al’lah is what raises one’s rank and elevates them above all others. The Almighty has indicated the unbelievers’ inability to witness reality and to recognise God’s Envoys (ptt) in His Address to our Envoy Mohammad (cpth), in the following noble verse, ‘

You find them looking at you, but they do not see you [your reality].

’ ﴿156﴾

This was also indicated in what the people of Midian said to their Envoy, our master Sho’aib (pth), ‘

They said, “You are surely bewitched. You are but a mortal like ourselves. Indeed, we believe that you are lying.”

’ ﴿157﴾

This is what was said by the people of ‘Ad and Thamoud, and this is also what is said by every unbeliever; and this is the state of anyone who is far from Al’lah. From here on, it is clear to us that recognition of God’s Envoys (ptt) and their glorification – as well as that of the true guides – can only be achieved by a person after they reach true belief in God. This is a belief that is based on total realisation and understanding. If a person glorifies and praises Al’lah the Almighty, and appreciates His Favour and Charity, they will approach Him and derive perfection from Him. Such a person will then admire those who possess perfection. He, the Great and the Almighty, is the First and the Last; He guides the hearts of all who believe in Him, and lets them walk on the right path.

In fact, we have two choices before us:

To be with Al’lah.

To be with the devil (may God protect us and you from this spiritual disease).

When a person forgets to mention Al’lah in their spirit Satan rushes to them, whispering evil so as to destroy them step by step. As for the believer, they pay attention to whatever satanic temptation the devil has sent into their spirit, and remember what caused Satan to approach them: namely that they have forgotten to mention Al’lah and to communicate with His Envoy (cpth). As soon as they remember God and communicate with His Envoy (cpth), whereby their spirits become overwhelmed with Godly Light, the devil will flee and will avoid them thereafter. The noble verse states, ‘

When those who seek piety [see by Al’lah’s Light] are touched by a passing satanic temptation, they remember [Al’lah] and then they become enlightened.

’ ﴿158﴾

However, the Almighty warned us about the devil and exposed his ways. The noble verse mentioned what the devil said, ‘

He said, “Because You have thrown me out of the way, Lo! I will waylay them within Your straight Path, then I will come to them from between their hands and from behind them, from their right and their left: nor will You find in most of them, gratitude [for Your Mercies].”

’ ﴿159﴾

‘

He said, “Because You have thrown me out of the way,”

’ – This means that the devil blamed God for His oppression, and this is a characteristic of everyone who has distanced themself from God.

The Almighty does not like vile deeds, abuse or aggression. He showed you the right way and the wrong way, then He warned you about following the wrong way. He sent you Envoys, Laws and angels to remind you. So, His Favour is granted in accordance with one’s diligence. Whoever works hard will rise up; and whoever is true in their seeking the truth will gain God’s Blessings. The liar will not be granted any gift. The Almighty bid you to do what is right and good. All of Creation are equal to each other in their origin, but whoever follows the Godly Laws will be elevated. The devil continued, ‘

Lo! I will waylay them within Your straight Path,

’ – That is, ‘I will do my best to prevent them following the right way’; ‘

Then I will come to them from between their hands

’ – When they are at work; ‘

And from behind them,

’ – ‘I will invite them to work for the future; ‘

From their right

’ – That is, through the right way, such as when they perform their communication with God and do good deeds, or when performing great deeds whereby they become conceited; ‘

And their left

’ – This refers to passing through the ways of harm or of vice: if an obedient follower has a small slip, or a wrongful deed is committed by a disobedient one, Satan drives them to despair of the Mercy of God. ‘

Nor will You find, in most of them, gratitude [for Your Mercies].

’

chapters.title: Why Would Al’lah Allow the Devil to Affect Someone?
chapters.html:
In the Holy Qur’an, the Almighty says, ‘

Truly, We have made the devils leaders for those who do not believe.

’ ﴿160﴾

However, Al’lah the Almighty does not allow Satan to reach the deserving ones with his whispers and false visions in a haphazard and fruitless fashion, without letting them profit from this victimisation: and what happens is merely treatment and cure for those whose ailments and guilt have intensified.

To clarify this, we present the following example: let us suppose that some food has become spoiled inside a man’s stomach due to his overeating, which leads to severe indigestion, and causes him painful cramps that may become life threatening: would it be reasonable for the doctor to leave him writhing in pain? Would he not prescribe an antidote or laxative for him, to expel the poisonous matter? Similarly, a wicked yearning that has taken hold within the spirit because it has shunned its Maker is, in fact, the overindulgence of the spirit and an ailment of the heart. Therefore, out of the Almighty’s Compassion for that person, He removes this yearning from their heart by letting them carry out the deed they insist on doing, because their spirit has become aggravated by this inclination and fully occupied by it. With that, the spirit’s field is no longer occupied by this yearning, and this state is always followed by affliction.

Driving this yearning out of the spirit takes place after Satan and his followers have thus induced the spirit when they controlled the person who has turned away from their Provider.

They accomplish this by insinuating bad ideas into their spirit, spitting, and using other avenues of entry through which the devil can pervade a neglectful spirit. When this person commits a single sin, Al’lah the Almighty sends them an affliction, so that they may retreat from their wrongdoing. Through such distress and painful torture a treatment is effected, with the aim of purifying the spirit and cleansing it of any germs that would generate cravings or excessive desires. This distress provides a reason for the spirit to withdraw from its erroneous ways and turn in repentance to its Provider, and thereby its cure can be achieved. Al’lah says, ‘

What can Al’lah gain by your punishment if you are grateful [in offering good acts], and you believe, yet Al’lah is Thankful and Omniscient?

’ ﴿161﴾

By this we understand that if someone returns to their Creator and believes in Him willingly and voluntarily, their actions will surely lead them to being illuminated by God’s Light. They will therefore witness the realities of the destructive desires in which people have indulged themselves and to which they have totally devoted themselves. Having become aware of this, any righteous person would naturally turn away feeling deeply saddened and weeping for these people, and wishing to save them if they could.

On the other hand, if a person remains absorbed in wrongdoing, insists on acting against what is right, and avoiding true realisation and enlightenment by Al’lah’s Light, they will never – no matter what happens – give up their wicked desires and renounce what has overcome them. This is in their own hands; but as long as they remain in such a deplorable state, they will completely neglect to offer up charity and goodness, and will continue to deviate from the way that leads to the achievement of worldly and eternal bliss. This is the reason the Almighty has sent humanity out into this lower life: simply to strive for this and to make every effort to find it. Therefore, out of Al’lah’s Mercy for such people, He firstly drives out the vicious desire that has settled in their spirits, and then He follows this expulsion with treatment and cure.

The Way to Spiritual Health

Through this state of distress or disease these people stop paying attention to their own evil yearnings and their spirit temporarily becomes free of the many mean things that have been rankling inside it; they then renounce this world and all that it contains.

If this is the case they then have two options before them:

Either they follow the path that leads to faith, having been given every opportunity and having had the way cleared before them. In this case, by virtue of the hardship described, none of their prior base desires would remain within their spirit. These cravings would have hindered the spirit from thinking of God’s Signs and considering the universe, and this would be the process through which the spirit would recognise its Creator and Provider, thus allowing it to fully and truly believe in Him.

Or they may try to forget what has already happened to them, without seizing this opportunity, when their spirits have become free of their yearning and no longer cling to the lower life in which they had been engrossed. Instead of taking advantage of the great opportunity that arises when the distress or illness has been removed from them, they return to their pre-occupation with this world, and devote themselves to it completely. With that the wicked lust – whose germ has faded but not yet died – will grow once again inside their spirits, and consequently they will return to their previous state and continue to do what they had been doing previously. However, Godly Compassion will continue to direct all kinds of distress and catastrophe to them. As Al’lah says, ‘

Those who disbelieve shall be unceasingly afflicted

’ – according to what bad deeds they have committed – ‘

with misfortune, or it may settle close to their home until Al’lah’s Promise is fulfilled. Al’lah will not fail in His Promise.

’ ﴿162﴾

If a person takes the opportunity to return to Al’lah after the affliction has been lifted from them – so that they abandon this inferior world and its people, and strictly adopt the path that leads to belief in God – true faith will certainly flow into their spirit. Then these adversities will have brought them great goodness, beneficial results and an important change in their lives. Their days will become rich with the offering up of charity and goodness, and will be full of pleasure and everlasting bliss.

chapters.title: The State of Our Master Adam in Paradise
chapters.html:
Having shown the angels Adam’s superiority over them in his knowledge about the Perfection of his Provider, the Almighty then wanted to show them his precedence over them in his love for the Creator. For further illustration, we give the following example: suppose that a mother had told her two little children not to run in the courtyard of their house in case they should fall and hurt themselves. One day she returned home, having been out for some time, and one of the children ran up to her as soon as he caught sight of her. He had completely forgotten his mother’s instructions because he loved her and had missed her during her absence; needless to say, he fell down. The other child, however, remembered his mother’s instructions and did not run to greet her as his sibling did. But I wonder, which of the two children has greater love for their mother? Is it not the one who, due to his love for her, forgot her earlier words of warning that is more attached and more loving to her?

Similarly, the Almighty knew well that whatever degree of love the noble angels attain they will not reach a degree of love for their Creator whereby they may forget His Orders. It was not so with Adam (pth); for he surpassed them in this field and advanced so far beyond them that they could not approach his level. To show the angels the rank of this Envoy (pth) and to display the reason for his superiority over them in knowing God, the Almighty designed a scenario for Adam’s accession to the rank of succession in a way that revealed the reality of this eminent Envoy (pth) and what intense love his heart held for his Creator. Therefore after the noble angels prostrated themselves to Adam (pth) and Lucifer refused and derided this, Al’lah the Almighty ordered our master Adam (pth) and his wife to dwell in Paradise, as indicated in the noble verse. God says, ‘

Then We said, “Oh, Adam! Dwell in Paradise – you and your wife – and eat whatever you want from it, happily and freely. Never come near this tree, in order not to be one of the unjust.”

’ ﴿163﴾

The spirits of our master Adam and his wife (ptt) surrounded their two noble bodies so that their enjoyment of this lower life was spiritual, and the fruit would not have entered into their stomachs for this would have required physical effort to digest it. The word ‘

Paradise

’ does not refer to a place high up in the heavens where our master Adam (pth) first dwelled, but which he then had to leave, although some people may think that it was so. The verses disprove the idea that Al’lah caused him to descend to the earth on which we now live, for the reality is different. At the beginning of this account, the Almighty God mentioned that He had informed the angels of His Will, which was that He would make a successor to Him on earth when He said, ‘

“I am creating man from mud.”

’ ﴿164﴾

Mud exists on earth, not in the heavens. Besides, the verses reported by Al’lah in the Holy Qur’an through which He reveals the origin of humanity and the beginning of Creation also deny such a belief. Instead, they show that humans have been on the earth on which we now live since they were first created. God says, ‘

For God, the example of Jesus is the same as that of Adam; He created him from soil, then He said to him, “Be” and he came into being.

’ ﴿165﴾

‘

Al’lah has brought you forth from the earth like a plant and then to the earth He will restore you; then He will bring you out of it afresh.

’ ﴿166﴾

‘

It was He Who made you from the earth and gave you dwellings upon it.

’ ﴿167﴾

‘

From earth We have created you, and into earth We shall return you, and out of it We shall bring you once again.

’ ﴿168﴾

chapters.title: What is Paradise?
chapters.html:
The Almighty created our master Adam and his wife (ptt) from the earth and let them live there in a state of Paradise.

Paradise is the hidden spiritual bliss which a person finds within himself and enjoys, without revealing it to anyone else. Our master Adam (pth) and his wife entered into God’s Presence, and were directed towards Him. There they witnessed the Godly Perfection to an extent that was beyond comparison to any other pleasure or ecstasy. That is what we should understand from the word ‘Paradise’, for the human spirit that believes will find no pleasure, bliss, or tranquillity like that which is experienced when looking at the Beauty of its Creator and witnessing His Loftiest Perfection. Our master Adam (pth) and his wife became immersed in a state of spiritual bliss, where they then remained: this is a state that is completely different from the material state in which we now live.

In earlier passages we have learnt that a person has a spirit, a soul and a body. In this worldly life the spirit is surrounded by and restrained within its body. It sees with the eyes, hears with the ears and tastes with the tongue. Since our bodily state has control over our spiritual one, a person cannot live unless the body receives a sufficient share of food and drink, and is adequately clothed. The body must inevitably make appropriate efforts to get what is needed to sustain it, including comfort and sleep. When Al’lah the Almighty brought our master Adam (pth) and his wife into being, they were in a state that was different to what people now experience. His spirit surrounded its body like the flame of a candle completely surrounds the wick.

Because of this situation, he did not need ears to hear or eyes to see, nor did he need a tongue with which to taste or speak, because his entire spirit was doing all of those things. Besides that, his body needed nothing at that time, because there was no hunger or thirst, no heat or coldness, nor toil or fatigue. The spirit was placed on the body and surrounded it, with the state of the spirit overruling that of the body. Its entry into Al’lah’s Presence was constant and never ending. And we swear that this is the state of all dwellers in Paradise in the Hereafter. Referring to the state of our master Adam (pth) at the beginning of his life, Al’lah says, ‘

Then We said, “Oh, Adam, this is an enemy for you and for your wife also, so do not let him get you to leave Paradise lest you become tired; you neither feel hungry nor naked therein, and you do not feel thirsty, nor does the heat of the sun injure you.”

’ ﴿169﴾

With regard to eating, our master Adam (pth) did eat while in this spiritual state – that is to say, in Paradise – but it was a form of eating which consisted only of tasting, which is also how all people will eat in Paradise in the Afterlife. The rays of the spirit that surround the body flow to the fruit, continuously tasting it, just as the rays of the sun flow to the depths of water, even though the body of the sun does not physically approach the lake or river in question. This continuous tasting may take a long time, sometimes lasting for months, but a person will never feel satiated or satisfied. The closer the spirit is to its Creator, the more it will taste and enjoy the things it eats, because its tasting and enjoyment will be proportional to its soundness and happiness.

This is the state of those who dwell in Paradise, which is the same state as that of our master Adam (pth) and his wife when Al’lah brought them into existence. They were in the Paradise of Bliss witnessing the great Godly Beauty. Besides this, their spirits were eating happily and freely from the earth; that is, they were constantly tasting, but never feeling heaviness or discomfort.

The Almighty cautioned our master Adam (pth) and his wife not to approach the tree. The word ‘

tree

’ here does not mean a specific tree of a certain kind, but it is a generic name for all kinds of trees and plants and could refer to any one of them, be it wheat, apple or pomegranate, for example. All trees and plants are encompassed within the word ‘

tree

’ as they are all, in reality, the same concerning their inclusion of the materials which are vital to the growth of the body and the flowing of life within it, even though every variety will have a different shape, size and taste. As for the meaning intended by God’s Saying, ‘

“Never come near”

’, it is that He instructed them not to put the actual physical fruit into their mouths. When any food enters the mouth it must be chewed and digested in order to move to the stomach, and consequently, a person’s condition will change from one state to another one, whereby the overall control is with the body and the spirit retreats within. The spirit will then become surrounded by the body which requires physical effort and will have to seek out the needs and material requirements of the body.

Life then will become dependent upon invigorating the body and providing it with the sustenance necessary for its existence. In this state, the body will weaken and frequently feel hungry and thirsty, and consequently the spirit will be in pain when the body needs this nourishment. Undoubtedly, the maintenance of life in this state requires steady physical effort and continuous toil. And what is more, the spirit’s ability to taste and enjoy things will be masked, and this can then take place only through intermediaries. It will not be able to taste things, except by means of the tongue, and it will be the same with the senses of sight, hearing and smell. In addition to all that, there will be a limit to the amount that the spirit will be able to enjoy, as the body will be sated by a certain amount of food and drink, and if it has more than it needs it will become confused and, consequently, the spirit will start to suffer pain. Taste is limited in this case, and one must work so as to provide for the needs of the body and, therefore, cannot stop working. Physical exertion may then lead to exhaustion. The noble verse refers to that wherein God says, ‘

“Never come near this tree in order not to be of the unjust.”

’ ﴿170﴾

– That is, ‘unjust to yourselves, when you become tired from labouring.’ This means, ‘Do not put this fruit near to your mouths, but instead, taste it and eat from it spiritually. If you put the fruit into your mouths, you will torment yourselves, and expose yourselves to great effort and fatigue in order to satisfy the requirements of the body.’

The spirits of our master Adam (pth) and his wife were placed over their noble bodies, so that their enjoyment of this world was a sublime spiritual taste. The fruits were not meant to go into their stomachs for it requires digestion and, later on, tiring, physical effort. The Almighty warned them against the devil and his enmity, to which the noble verse refers when God says, ‘

Then We said, “Oh, Adam, this is an enemy for you and for your wife also, so do not let him get you to leave Paradise lest you become tired.”

’ ﴿171﴾

– Due to hard physical work.

So our master Adam (pth) learnt of the troubles of life that his eating from the tree would bring and the resulting efforts and tiredness that living would require from him. He realised that God advised him not to eat from it simply to spare him such troubles; yet his great love for his Creator caused him to forget Al’lah’s Recommendation. This is the rank that qualified this august Envoy to be God’s successor on His Land and which made all the noble angels prostrate themselves to him. As mentioned before, our master Adam (pth) and his wife dwelt in the blissful state of entering into Al’lah’s Presence and enjoying their witnessing of that great Godly Beauty. They clung to it, wanting never to alter that state. Can the enjoyment of viewing the Face of God be equal to any other bliss? Can a true believer ever be satisfied with anything less than this?

chapters.title: How Did Our Master Adam (pth) and His Wife Leave Paradise?
chapters.html:
From this point on, the devil was most gratified to find an opening through which he could enter in order to turn that noble Prophet (pth) away from his Creator and cause him to descend from the state in which he existed. God says, ‘

The devil whispered to him saying, “Oh Adam! Shall I guide you to the tree of eternity [to continually see the Face of God] and to an immortal sublime property?”

’ ﴿172﴾

– That is, ‘May I guide you to the tree which, if you eat from it, will allow you to remain forever in this blissful state? Your spirit will still be able to enter into Al’lah’s Presence and will be directed towards Him forever.’ Then he swore by the Almighty God that he was merely giving good advice to both Adam (pth) and his wife.

However, since nobody appreciates the great except for the great, our master Adam (pth) was overcome by his love for God, and this caused him to forget His Advice that he should not eat the fruit from any tree. Al’lah says, ‘

We have covenanted to Adam before but he forgot and We found no intention of his

’ ﴿173﴾

– That is, ‘Adam simply forgot Our Advice, and We found that he had no intention of disobeying Our Command.’ The situation with his wife was similar, and they both ate from the tree; that is, they physically ate its fruit because of their love for Al’lah.

With that their spirits shifted from one state to another and followed the substance that was entering their bodies; their spirits then became surrounded by their bodies, whereas previously the spirits had surrounded the bodies. Consequently they were in the state that all mankind now experiences (the worldly state), feeling the pain of hunger and the suffering of thirst. God says, ‘

Then, the devil whispered to them so as to show them what was hidden from them of their shameful deeds [that displeased them].

’ ﴿174﴾

– Thus indicating the devil’s purpose behind his whispering. By this whispering, he wanted to upset Adam (pth) and his wife and cause them great distress by turning them away from God and their ability to enter into His Presence. In fact, Adam and his wife were free from any feeling of sadness or anguish as they were absorbed in witnessing Godly Beauty and Perfection. As long as mankind is in God’s Presence, their spirit is overwhelmed in His Manifestation and devoted to witnessing His Beauty and this Manifestation; therefore grief and anguish could never creep into their spirit.

Yet when Adam (pth) and his wife put the fruit into their mouths and their spirits entered their bodies, they became aware that they had gone against God’s Advice, and their spirits then withdrew from God in shame and diffidence. Adam and his wife, Eve, became extremely distressed because of the new situation they had moved to where they became surrounded by a state of unhappiness and suffering. This is what the noble verse referred to when God said, ‘

When they tasted the tree [fruit], their shameful deeds [that displeased them] appeared to them.

’ – That is, they became aware of the unpleasant things which were caused by their descending from that beautiful spiritual state in which they had been. Their life became sad and unhappy due to such a change and the shame and diffidence that they felt.

Adam (pth) and his wife then tried to regain the previous state. God said, ‘

They started to place the leaves of Paradise over themselves.

’ – Leaves protect fruit from being damaged, help it to grow well and also to have a fresh and beautiful appearance. ‘

The leaves of Paradise

’ – This means that they took refuge and showed humility whereby that blissful and beautiful spiritual state they had had previously might come back to them. What we understand by the statement ‘

They started to place the leaves of Paradise over themselves

’ is that they immediately took the initiative to seek refuge and submit to God, wishing to enjoy again that Godly Manifestation which was the reason for their spiritual bliss and their constant pleasure in being close to their Provider. ‘

Their Provider called out to them, saying, “Did I not forbid you to approach that tree? Did I not warn you that Satan was a sworn enemy for you?” They replied, “Oh our Provider, we have wronged ourselves, pardon us and have mercy on us, or we shall surely be among the lost.”

’ ﴿175﴾

Returning to the verses of al-Baqara Fortress, the following noble verse refers to the bodily state of our master Adam (pth) and his wife after they physically ate the fruit. Due to his withdrawal from God, the devil became envious and mean, and was driven to turn them away due to his own jealousy. God says, ‘

Then, the devil made them lapse away from it and got them out of where they had been.

’ The devil said to Adam (pth), ‘Oh Adam, your Provider has never advised you that you should not eat the fruit of the tree. So, believe me, if you eat the fruit you will remain forever in Paradise.’ Since our master Adam (pth) had no power of thought, he forgot God’s Command and ate the fruit, which caused his spirit to go inside his body and his approach to Al’lah to become obstructed. The statement ‘

Then, the devil made them lapse away from it

’ shows that it was the devil’s lies that made them shift from the state of spiritual tasting which was made up of tasting only, to the bodily state. In this way he drove them away from their previous state of immaterial bliss. With their altered state they had to provide for their bodily needs and material demands, which they had never considered beforehand. Al’lah says, ‘

We said, “Go hence, and may you be enemies to each other. The earth will be a dwelling place for you, and will provide you with sustenance for a while.”

’ ﴿176﴾

The statement ‘

We said, “Go hence”

’ means that they had to leave the spiritual state and descend to this lower life, seek their own livelihood, and make constant efforts to meet the needs and demands that this life entails. That was the new state in which our master Adam (pth) and his wife found themselves, and so it was with their children after them. The statement ‘

and may you be enemies to each other

’ means that the non-believer will do their utmost to antagonise the believer, and demonstrates that the wisdom contained in this account shows the enmity that the devil and his offspring, who have turned away from God, bear for humanity.

Those of humankind who follow God’s Words will realise what the devil did to deceive our master Adam (pth), falsely swearing to him in order to try to turn him away from Al’lah. This will help these believers not to be deceived or tempted by the devil. Meanwhile, the unbelievers among Lucifer’s offspring – who are some of the jinn-kind – will be with him as enemies of Adam’s children, in order to turn them away from what is right in order to unsettle their faith. The statement ‘

and may you be enemies to each other

’ means that the devil will be an enemy of humanity. This statement aims to acquaint us with the fact that God the Almighty engineered humanity’s exodus to this worldly life in this way in order to give those humans who are prepared for perfection a practical lesson about the devil’s enmity and deception. With this, they become acquainted with him and will be cautious about his temptation. All of that shows us the Compassion and the Clemency of God the Almighty, for Al’lah is Clement and Merciful. The statement, ‘

The earth will be a dwelling place for you, and will provide you with sustenance for a while

’ refers to the human lifetime, and denotes that a person has a limited age and a pre-ordained moment of death.

That is because a person’s life in this world depends on the healthiness of their body and its maintenance, so that it is able to function properly. When the main bodily organs stop working at the moment of death, the soul will leave the body. Once the body becomes cold the spirit will also leave the body and follow the soul, for it cannot remain in a cold environment. The angels’ task is to take the soul but God will take the spirit. They will leave the body together, but the spirit will remain connected to the body and will continue to observe it.

On the other hand, life in the Hereafter is eternal. In the other abode, the spirit will have control since it will surround the body, and so the body will have no power or function from that day on, and will not be subject to senility, weakness or debility. It will only serve as something that the spirit will rest upon on the day when it has life. Since the spirit is a luminous essence that is not affected by the weakening and dissolution that happens to the components of the body, life in the other abode will be eternal. The statement ‘

The earth will be a dwelling place for you, and will provide you with sustenance for a while

’, also denotes that the existence of humanity on the earth has a certain finite term. When this earthly term ends this life will finish with it, and then people will go to the other abode where each person will face the outcome of their deeds and efforts.

Thus, by Adam’s (pth) physical eating from the tree, the noble angels became aware of the high degree of love our master Adam (pth) had for his Provider and his superiority over them in this matter. This ban on physical eating was only a test by which the Almighty, Who is Omniscient of all that is contained within every spirit, revealed the honour of our master Adam (pth) and his love for Him. It then became clear to the noble angels that Adam’s precedence and excellence over them in the knowledge of Al’lah’s Names was the result of his advancing beyond them in his love for Al’lah.

At this point, some questions may arise in the minds of the reader, such as:

chapters.title: How Did Adam Forget the Advice of Al’lah? How Could the Devil Have Deceived Him?
chapters.html:
Can the devil enter into the spirits of Prophets? Do the Prophets disobey Al’lah? How can we find congruity between what our master Adam (pth) did when he ate fruit from the tree, and what the Holy Qur’an proclaims about the impeccability of Prophets and the impossibility of a Prophet contravening any of God’s Commands?

We say that these are serious issues that have the potential to cause a lot of people to lose their footing. If a person does not fully understand this issue, and does not realise the perfection of God’s Envoys (cptt) and their spiritual sublimity, and that it is impossible for any Prophet to ever violate any of God’s Commands, this person will certainly slip and fall into the infernal state of shunning Al’lah. As long as such a person’s spirit is veiled from witnessing the perfection with which the spirits of God’s Envoys (cptt) are coloured no-one will be able to bring them back towards Al’lah. This is because the human spirit is naturally disposed, as we know, to love perfection. It cannot appreciate somebody or attach itself to anybody in a sincere way if it finds imperfection in the other person or that they deviate from the truth. That is one of the unalterable rules of the spirit.

To enter into the discipline of certain spiritual belief and seeing by Al’lah’s Light, it is necessary to love God’s Envoys (cptt) and accompany them wholeheartedly. Therefore, in entering into God’s Presence through being in such company, how would it be possible for a spirit to love and accompany these Envoys of God (cptt) if it found even a single defect in them? This spirit would undoubtedly remain veiled from Al’lah and totally deprived of the opportunity to approach Him.

We clarify these important points as follows:

In order to understand the first point, about how our master Adam (pth) forgot the Advice that Al’lah gave him, we should return to Adam’s original state. This refers to his first state in Paradise: the state of approaching God before moving to the lower worldly life, that is, before descending from his spiritual state to the bodily one which all of us are currently experiencing.

Humans have a mind plus the ability to think for themselves in this world, whereas in Paradise, they are free of thought and only have a mind. The ability to think which is situated in the brain – a precious gift which Al’lah the Almighty has given to humanity – is the means by which we attain knowledge and understand reality in this earthly world. When the eye sees, the ear hears, or the tongue tastes, these senses are transferred to the spirit, which transmits these perceptions to the brain, when it is truly seeking the truth. ﴿177﴾

In the brain, the power of thought carries out the processes of comparing, contrasting, dismantling and assembling; it is then that the spirit attains what it is asking for, whether that is positive or negative.

It is the ability to think that decides on the Existence of the Organiser through our observing cosmic discipline; it deduces the Existence of the Actor through our viewing His Actions; and it gains knowledge of the Provider because of His Provision for all Creation. The spirit fully realises these facts that are decided by the power of thought, witnesses them by itself and becomes certain of them. These facts are etched on the blank surface of the spirit and never leave it. It fully realises the fact of God’s Existence and then witnesses the Attributes of Al’lah, the Almighty. This is the ultimate aim behind the existence of humanity in this lower, worldly life.

Thinking, therefore, is the process of contrasting, comparing, dismantling and assembling that are performed by the brain so that it can discern the reality of all things. As for total realisation (the mind), this is the witnessing of these facts and viewing them with the eye of the spirit (the third eye). When thought is serious, it will surely lead its owner to total realisation and these facts will be fully absorbed by the spirit at a fundamental level. These facts then remain stored in the memory and the spirit, so that when a person needs access to one of these true facts, the rays of thought are reflected onto what the spirit has previously incorporated into its mind. The facts that were stored in the spirit shine upon it, and with that the person remembers them.

Whilst on the topic of thinking and the mind, we should explain briefly the process of thought and its ability to comprehend facts. In order to understand a particular matter it is necessary for the spirit to concentrate on it, for the power of thought acts superficially in relation to matters in which the spirit is not entirely interested. This is also the case if the spirit is not completely true and persistent in its search. Without this total concentration, the power of thought cannot reach the point where it is able to discern reality, nor can it make a decision; consequently, the spirit remains far from full realisation or witnessing.

In order to let the spirit come to a stage of total realisation in knowing the Creator and Provider and to believe, without any doubt, that there is no god but Al’lah, and for the spirit to know that all control is in the Hands of Al’lah alone, it is necessary to acquaint the spirit with the fact that this lower life – with which it is pleased and content – will end in a relatively short time. Whatever a person collects in this life, and whatever they experience, they will die nonetheless and leave this lower, worldly plane of existence. This is an indisputable fact.

If a person calls to mind their parents, relatives and forefathers who have come before them, but who have now passed on from this worldly life, and then they draw their spirit’s attention to those who, later on, lived in their homes or used their places of business, this person’s spirit is being informed about death and its daunting effect, and about the grave and its loneliness; and such a lesson is repeated on a daily basis. Such a spirit will be afraid and will stop indulging in its love for this world and will refrain from turning to the lower life. It will then seriously seek to know its Provider Who takes care of it. The efforts of the spirit will gather together with those of thought, acting hurriedly and earnestly.

This person will continually compare and contrast, question himself and provide their own answers until they reach a decision about the Existence of the Great Creator Who has created everything. They will continue their research until they come to believe that the Almighty is the Supporter and Provider Who provides for all creatures and supplies their every need within a moment, and without overlooking any one of them. This person will fully realise these facts in their spirit, and it will be based on their heart observations, and beyond all doubt.

Finally, this valid thought moves from knowing the Provider to knowing the Steering God Who directs the entire universe, deciding that the directing of the whole universe is in the Hands of Al’lah, and that there is no god but Al’lah. The spirit then realises these facts and becomes a truly believing spirit. In fact, belief is one of the results of realisation, and anyone who realises nothing has neither belief nor faith. Therefore awareness has the most important status in reaching true belief and it is achieved only after thinking profoundly. Thinking cannot be accomplished until a person is honest in their desire to seek knowledge (or seek knowledge of Al’lah), and nor is the process set in motion without this point being reached. This truth is only attained by fearing death and its consequences. That is why Mohammad (cpth) frequently lay on his right side and turned his face toward

al-Ka’ba

while he was in the mosque, between the prayer of sunna and the one which takes place at dawn. He was imitating our position in the tomb, thinking and teaching us how to be true so that we will achieve true belief. He (cpth) said, ‘

Mention that which ends the pleasures [death] frequently.

’ ﴿178﴾

He also cautions people through his noble saying, ‘

Live as much as you like, for you shall certainly die; love whoever you like, for you shall truly leave them; do whatever you like, for you shall indeed be recompensed for it.

’ ﴿179﴾

This is so that a person may be guided and follow the way of belief, and death should be the only lesson and reminder we need. This is a brief statement which must be emphasised frequently to anyone who wants to learn a lesson, or to be encouraged to reach true belief, and subsequently to understand the Qur’an, the Words of the Great Provider.

Returning to the research we began while talking about our master Adam (pth), his eating from the tree, and how he forgot Al’lah’s Advice, we say, in our earlier research about the human being, concerning such points as the spirit, soul, thought, mind etc., we clarified that in this world people have a mind and the power of thought, but in Paradise, they are free from thought and only have a mind. That is because the activity of thought depends on the functioning of the brain and the flow of blood through it. You could also say that thought helps the spirit to achieve awareness of the facts and the realisation of them. This is the case for as long as such a spirit is confined within its mortal body and as long as this body has control over it. However, if the spirit escapes from the body and surrounds it, thus becoming its ruler, then all of the bodily systems – including the process of thought – will stop functioning. In this case, these mechanisms and this power of thought would have no function, and the spirit would understand reality by itself, without the need for thought or feeling.

In this lower life, a person remembers the incidents that happened to them and the deeds that they did by means of thought, the process of which was explained previously. However, in the life to come, ﴿180﴾

the ability to think will cease to function, so this person will not remember anything through thinking; instead, what they see will go directly into their mind. Therefore, when the deeds a person has performed in this life are shown to them, the spirit will be fully aware of them; that is to say, it will realise what was imprinted on itself by its own actions.

That was the state of our master Adam (pth). His spirit surrounded his body and understood what it saw. Then the devil came to him and said, ‘

Oh Adam! Shall I guide you to the tree of eternity [to continually see the Face of God], and to an immortal sublime property?

’ ﴿181﴾

– That is, ‘May I guide you to a tree? If you eat from this tree, your spirit will remain in the sublime state of constant entrance into Al’lah’s Beauty, and you will have perpetual access to that beautiful and exalted state.’ Then when he swore by God to our master Adam (pth) that he was giving him advice, Adam (pth) forgot that God had forbidden him to eat from the tree, just as he forgot that the Almighty had warned him about the devil. It was quite normal that our master Adam (pth) should forget all of this, since on that day he had no power of thought and therefore was unable to remember. He was in a completely spiritual state where control belonged entirely to the spirit, inside which the body was inoperative and its systems, including memory, were not functioning. Consequently, there was no escape from the oblivion which was normal in this state.

God says, ‘

We have covenanted to Adam before but he forgot and We found no intention of his.

’ ﴿182﴾

– That is, God found that Adam had no intention to disobey Him.

The forgetfulness of our master Adam (pth) and his wife was imposed on them by the spiritual state which they were in at that time and, in this case, it was not a transgression. Anyone who was in the same spiritual state as Adam (pth) at that time would have done as he (pth) did, for this was before he went into the physical state in which we now exist. His status inevitably dictated his actions and reactions, and this cannot be regarded as an infringement of God’s Orders or a breach of His Advice. Almighty God let our master Adam (pth) experience this event, and made him and his wife the two focal points. God’s only Purpose in this was to ensure that their offspring would be acquainted with the devil’s enmity and deception when they would be in the physical state by presenting them with an actual example. In this way their children were warned against the devil and his malevolence. The noble verse refers to this when God says, ‘

Sons of Adam! Let Satan not deceive you, as he got your parents out of Paradise.

’ ﴿183﴾

One may ask that if the matter was as has been explained, then what is the correct interpretation of the noble verse which mentions this incident, when God says, ‘

And Adam disobeyed his Provider [with no intention to contravene God’s Advice, for his purpose was sublime: to perpetuate his entering into God’s Presence]; then he has gone astray ﴿184﴾

[diverted, in bewilderment, from that lofty condition].

’ ﴿185﴾

We have already revealed that Adam’s (pth) spiritual state had its own particularities and specific characteristics which do not apply to the physical state in which we now exist. Adam had not then reached this physical state. When he forgot the Advice, this was an outcome of his spiritual state at that time due to the absence of thought. Therefore Adam’s eating from the tree can never be regarded as an infringement within the meaning that we now understand by the term in our worldly state, no matter what strikes the minds of those who did not know the rank of God’s Envoy (cpth).

To understand this verse, we have to understand the noble verses that come before and after it, and which are mentioned in the course of this account when God says, ‘

We have covenanted to Adam before but he forgot and We found no intention of his. When We said to the angels, “Prostrate yourselves before Adam”, they prostrated themselves, except for Lucifer who rejected this. Then We said, “Oh Adam, this is an enemy for you and for your wife also, so do not let him get you to leave Paradise lest you become tired; you neither feel hungry nor naked therein, and you do not feel thirsty, nor does heat of the sun injure you.” The devil whispered to him saying, “Oh Adam! Shall I guide you to the tree of eternity [to continually see the Face of God], and to an immortal sublime property?” They both ate from it, so their shameful deeds [that displeased them] appeared to them and they started to place the leaves of Paradise over themselves. And Adam disobeyed his Provider [with no intention to contravene God’s Advice, for his purpose was sublime: to perpetuate his entering into God’s Presence]; then he has gone astray [diverted, in bewilderment, from that lofty condition]. His Provider then chose him [brought him closer to Himself], forgave him, and gave him guidance.

’ ﴿186﴾

These honourable verses clarified to us that our master Adam (pth) simply forgot the Advice of God and had no intention to disobey Him. He (pth) ate from the tree only because he wanted to perpetuate his existence in Paradise, which is (as previously mentioned) the ecstasy of entering into God’s Presence and enjoying observing His Beauty. The only motive that drove him to eat from the tree was his love for Al’lah and his wish to continue to remain in the bliss of entering into His Presence. As for the statement ‘

Adam disobeyed his Provider[with no intention to contravene God’s Advice, for his purpose was sublime: to perpetuate his entering into God’s Presence]; then he has gone astray [diverted, in bewilderment, from that lofty condition]

’, its meaning becomes clear if we join it to the statement ‘

They both ate from it, so their shameful deeds [that displeased them] appeared to them and they started to place the leaves of Paradise over themselves.

’ – That is, as soon as our master Adam (pth) and his wife ate from the tree they were able to observe their physical states (their bodies appeared), and due to the emergence of that state, our master Adam (pth) remembered Al’lah’s Advice. This occurred because the bodily state is associated with the existence of thought, which in turn results in memory being activated. At that time, he (pth) knew that the state in which he found himself was the result of forgetting God’s Advice and thereby infringing His Order.

As a result, the statement ‘

And Adam disobeyed his Provider [with no intention to contravene God’s Advice, for his purpose was sublime: to perpetuate his entering into God’s Presence]

’ means that no sooner had the bodily state come over our master Adam (pth) than he realised in his spirit that he had forgotten what Al’lah the Almighty had advised him, and that he had acted contrary to that Advice. So, too, this same statement is not confirmation of Adam’s disobedience, nor is it a confirmation of infringement. Instead, it describes the state of our master Adam, and reveals his sense and his spiritual perception of his inadvertent disobedience because he forgot God’s Advice.

Referring to the words ‘

Then he has gone astray [diverted, in bewilderment, from that lofty condition]

’, the word ‘

astray

’ is derived from ‘straying’, which means ‘to be converted’ or ‘to turn away from a high state, including happiness and goodness, to a lower one, thereby causing discomfort and wretchedness’. God says, ‘

But there came after them generations who neglected communication with Al’lah and succumbed to desires; these shall assuredly go astray

’ ﴿187﴾

– That is, the following generations will be degraded according to the position of their forefathers because they neglected to communicate with Al’lah but followed their own desires instead, and so they will face troubles and distress.

Mohammad (cpth) often introduced his sermons with his august saying, ‘

He who obeys Al’lah and His Envoy is on the right path, but he who disobeys Al’lah and His Envoy goes astray, until he returns to God’s Order.

’ ﴿188﴾

As a result, when our master Adam (pth) eventually saw his bodily state, and remembered that he had acted against his Provider’s Advice, his spirit became ashamed and was veiled off from that high state of entering into God’s Presence.

One can understand from the statement, ‘

Adam disobeyed his Provider [with no intention to contravene God’s Advice, for his purpose was sublime: to perpetuate his entering into God’s Presence]; then he has gone astray [diverted, in bewilderment, from that lofty condition]

’ that Adam (pth) realised, in his spirit, that he had disregarded his Provider’s Advice, and that his spirit was ashamed and thereby veiled off from continuing its high entering into God’s Presence. This resulted in Adam turning away from the elevated state in which he had been. Also, the words ‘

then he has gone astray [diverted, in bewilderment, from that lofty condition]

’ mean that Adam had mistaken the way that would lead him to his true intention. He (pth) ate the fruit, physically, wanting only the continuity of his witnessing Godly Manifestation and to remain in the state of seeing Godly Perfection. Yet this act did not help him to fulfil his goal; on the contrary, it caused his spirit to break off from that expansive witnessing.

The verse ‘

Adam disobeyed his Provider [with no intention to contravene God’s Advice, for his purpose was sublime: to perpetuate his entering into God’s Presence], then he has gone astray [diverted, in bewilderment, from that lofty condition]

’ teaches us that anyone who breaks the Godly Commandments will inevitably suffer distress and anguish and results contrary to what they expect. However, at the moment when Adam (pth) sensed the reticence in his spirit and turned away from his ascending witnessing, his Provider called him and revealed that his eating from the tree actually had happened because of his honourable intention. As we have learned already, Adam’s intention was that his state of being constantly in the Presence of God’s Beauty should continue forever. Such a lofty intention is not considered to be disobedience, nor does it entail any shame or diffidence, especially when associated with that original spiritual state which ensures forgetting due to the absence of the ability to think. Through acquainting our master Adam (pth) with these facts the Almighty brought about Adam’s return to Him and expelled the diffidence which had occupied his spirit. That is what we understand from the words ‘

his Provider then chose him [brought him closer to Himself]

’ ﴿189﴾

– That is, He caused his return to Him with his heart fully committed to Him, the Almighty.

The noble verse ‘

his Provider then chose him [brought him closer to Himself], forgave him and gave him guidance

’ confirms what we have already explained: Adam (pth) and his wife Eve’s eating fruit from the tree occurred simply because they forgot God’s Advice and wanted only to fulfil the lofty purpose of witnessing the Godly Perfection forever. This is because the Almighty would never consider selecting a disobedient man who seeks worldly desires rather than to seek his Creator’s Satisfaction. Certainly, only men who have a superior nature and a lofty purpose, and are fully taken up with perfection will be chosen for such distinction.

But how did Al’lah select Adam, that is, cause him to turn back wholeheartedly and come closer to Him after Adam (pth) ate from the tree? The Almighty clarified that for us in His Saying, ‘

Then Adam received Words from His Provider.

’ – That is, Words that revealed to him his noble intention and elevated purpose. This was in order to dispel the shyness from his spirit. With that, he knew that Al’lah, the Almighty, did not blame him for his forgetfulness and did not consider his action on an external basis, instead He looked inside at the reality and the intention that was folded within this action for, truly, all deeds are evaluated according to intentions.

When Adam (pth) turned to God with humility, the Almighty inspired his spirit, ‘Oh, Adam! Your intention is noble and high. We never blame you for what came out of you.’ In the same way, whoever lapses unintentionally can easily return to God, but those who persist in their failings with no intention of giving them up, have no way back to Him. Adam then realised that he had not disobeyed his Provider, nor had he purposely broken His Rules; he realised also that Al’lah is Omniscient and considers only our intentions.
