With that, his spirit was at peace and reassured of God’s Satisfaction once again. He returned to approach his Provider and directed himself entirely to Him. His Provider then accepted his repentance and lifted the veil of diffidence from his spirit, restoring him to his original state of increasingly observing Godly Beauty and Perfection. This is indicated in the noble verse when God says, ‘

And He made him repent [He accepted his repentance].

’ – This refers to Al’lah’s Care which surrounded our master Adam (pth), maintained him, and is clearly indicated in this account. That is how the Almighty treats all of His servants. He sends them what they need to make their wandering spirits return to Him to enjoy the eternal bliss that He has prepared for them. That is what we understand by the statement ‘

He is the Re-granter, the All- Merciful,

’ ﴿190﴾

– which means that He initiates the kind of therapy that will allow us to return to Him.

One should observe, then, God’s Sympathy and Compassion and think about His great Grace for His servants. He decided to make our master Adam (pth) His successor on earth when he was still in a spiritual state, before He brought him into this earthly world, and before He brought his offspring out from his back. Then He caused his transition from the spiritual state to the bodily one to take place in a way in which He showed the eminence of this Envoy (pth) and his great love for his Creator; besides which, with the tale of this first man, the Almighty gave lasting examples and lessons to his children by making him, Adam, the first tutor of his own offspring. He fulfilled His Will in a way that would acquaint people with the rules of the spirit which are the basis for entry into God’s Presence. He let them know how the spirit can return to the field of sacredness so that if their spirits become reticent and withdraw from their Provider, they will be able to return if they only do what will revive their confidence and shake off their shame.

As we have previously mentioned, the Almighty also wanted to acquaint us with the enmity of the devil, so we would be aware of his cunning and trickery. In addition He wanted us to consider that love for Him, and truthfulness and sincerity with Him should be within the bounds of certain law and order. Given the above explanation can anyone remain unconvinced, object to and disparage this worthy Envoy (pth) or accuse Al’lah of cruelty towards humanity? The truth is that He, the Almighty, always tries to turn His servants back to the right way, ‘

Yet the unbelievers wrangle about Al’lah, though He tries a lot with them.

’ ﴿191﴾

This is just some of what we have learnt from this account and, in fact, so many other examples and lessons have also been included! ‘

Those examples We give to oblivious people, but none will be mindful of them except the scientists [of Al’lah’s Attributes].

’ ﴿192﴾

We have answered the questions that were raised previously; we have also demonstrated in detail that our master Adam (pth) did not disobey his Provider, and that his original spiritual state made it necessary for him to forget the Advice he had received. This proves to us that what our master Adam (pth) and his wife did when they ate from the tree was based, in fact, on the best of intentions, as the devil swore to them – by God – that they would stay forever in that delightful state of witnessing God and their sublime entry into His Presence if they did what he said and ate from the tree. Since this Prophet (pth) was aware of the Greatness and Majesty of his Creator, he thought that it was beyond belief that anyone would dare to swear falsely by God.

This is why he believed wholeheartedly what the devil was saying and forgot Al’lah’s Advice to him. The noble verse serves, ‘

Our Lord, may You not be angry with us if we forget or lapse into error by mistake.

’ ﴿193﴾

Our master Mohammad (cpth) said, ‘

Punishment was raised off my people for lapses into error by mistake, forgetting, and for what they were impelled to do.

’ ﴿194﴾

Al’lah says, ‘

God chose Adam, Noah, the Abrahams and the ‘Imrans above all the worlds

’ – These families were selected by the Almighty above the people of all other nations in order to guide people to Al’lah. What was this choice based on? The Almighty set this out in ‘The Family of ‘Imran’ Fortress, saying, ‘

They are the offspring of one another.

’ – This means they are all of one origin, they are Adam’s sons, but ‘

Al’lah is All-Hearing, Omniscient

’ ﴿195﴾

– Meaning He did not choose them haphazardly, but can hear everything that they say, and the Omniscient knows everything about their intentions and genuine exalted states. He selected them because of their elevated states and their lofty level of guidance. If your intention is high and your words are too, Al’lah will grant His Favour to you.

So, anyone who wrongs the Prophets (ptt) or mistrusts them is certainly trying to discredit the statement ‘

Al’lah is All-Hearing, Omniscient

’; in other words, such a person thinks that Al’lah, the Almighty, chose Adam in a haphazard way, without knowing anything about him. As we already know, this is untrue. The Almighty God chose these people for their perfect exalted spirits, as a guide should be a perfect person. Anyone, then, who talks against the Prophets (ptt), and offends them, has no faith. If a person really believes that Al’lah hears all and knows all, they will not talk about Al’lah’s Envoys in an evil way, for Al’lah hears every creature and scientifically knows their state: He chose His Envoys (ptt) because of their pure spirits and noble intentions.

Returning to the hadith of God’s Envoy (cpth),who never speaks simply on impulse, we find that his illustrious saying tells us, ‘

Without pride, I am the master of Adam’s sons on the Day of Resurrection, and - without pride - the banner of praising Al’lah is in my hand. On that Day, there is no Prophet - Adam and all who are below him - who does not join me [and is under my banner], and - without pride - I am the first intercessor.

’ ﴿196﴾

Here we understand that Adam (pth) is in second position from the point of sublimity and hierarchy. He is above all other Envoys and Prophets (ptt) but is below the master of Creation, our master Mohammad (cpth). Just like all the devout Prophet masters (ptt) below him, he is unblemished by any error or the committing of any sin, either great or small, and is incapable of disobeying Al’lah or contravening His Command, for He, the Almighty, says of all the Prophets, ‘

But they are purified and strictly true servants. They do not speak before Him, and by His Order they act.

’ ﴿197﴾

He was the first Prophet and Envoy (cpth) to be created, and the Almighty addressed him in His noble Saying about the angels, ‘

Tell them about their Names.

’ ﴿198﴾ ﴿199﴾

He is a Prophet and an Envoy (pth) sent forth by Al’lah to the responsible jinn (that is, those who accepted bearing the Trust in al- Azal world) and to all the virtuous angels, as well as to mankind, beginning with his worthy offspring. The purpose behind this account is to warn people against the devil’s cunning and scheming ways, and that is purely because of the Almighty’s Sympathy, Compassion and Clemency.

chapters.title: Did the Devil Cause Adam (pth) and Eve to Be Deceived?
chapters.html:
We have to understand two points arising from the discussion of the questions mentioned above. If we grasp these points correctly we will automatically forget all other matters that many people misunderstand. The first one is about the meaning of the noble verse which is found in this account in the Words of the Almighty, ‘

So, he [the devil] let them down with deception.

’ ﴿200﴾

Could the devil have caused our master Adam (pth) and his wife to be deceived? Alternatively, could this verse have a subtle meaning that is appropriate only to the position and perfection of this noble Envoy (pth)?

Replying to this, we say that the words ‘

So, he let them down

’ are taken from ‘to let down’, that is, you can say that someone let down the branch, meaning that they brought it closer to themselves. So when the devil saw our master Adam’s (pth) delight and his lofty position close to God he swore to him that eating from the tree would lead to his residing eternally in the Presence of Al’lah; and he then made him (pth) approach the tree and eat from it with his wife. As for the words ‘

with deception

’ they do not refer to our master Adam but to the devil himself, as it was the devil’s spirit that was engaged in deception, and not the spirit of our master Adam (pth).

To clarify the details we say that deception is a spiritual state that prevails over a person’s spirit, making them assume that a certain thing is true, but this is not the reality. For example, a person may be deceived by the moonlight at night, for if they wake up and see the moon rising they may think that the dawn is about to break although it is still the middle of the night. A person may also be deceiving themself if they think that they are powerful and knowledgeable, although in fact they have no knowledge except what Al’lah has taught them, and they have no power except through Al’lah.

It is clear then that the devil was deceiving himself also; he thought that by swearing by Al’lah and claiming that eating from the tree would ensure that our master Adam’s sojourn with Al’lah would last forever, he would be able to make Adam (pth) disobey his Provider, causing him to become reticent and distant from Al’lah. However, the subsequent events conflicted with the devil’s aim and supposition for Adam’s (pth) noble intention was a steady foundation on which he depended, and this allowed him to return and resort to Al’lah. On the other hand, the devil came out of this trial humiliated, and was expelled. This made it clear to us that the devil was unable to deceive our master Adam (pth) or cause him to distance himself from Al’lah. The meaning of the words ‘

with deception

’ describes the state of the devil when he imagined that he could be successful. However, events did not match his expectation, and he was turned away in failure and disappointment.

Concerning the second point, one might ask, how could the devil direct his whispering at our master Adam (pth) even though Adam constantly entered into Al’lah’s Presence? Can we regard this incident as proof that Satan can enter into the spirits of the Prophets (ptt)?

This matter becomes absolutely clear if we return to the original state of humanity when Adam’s spirit was surrounding his body, and compare this spiritual state to the physical body in which we now exist. When our master Adam (pth) was in the Paradise of entering into Al’lah’s Presence, his body was enclosed within his spirit, that is, the spirit was surrounding it. Because of this there was no screen to veil his spirit from the spirit of the devil for Adam’s spirit was visible and uncovered. However, since our master Adam (pth) was constantly entering into Al’lah’s Presence and witnessing Him, the devil could do no more than project whispered suggestions to Adam, and talk to him from a distance without approaching him. For example, if I were walking along the street and heard a word whispered from a distance, or a word that someone wanted me to hear, intending it to affect my spirit, surely this would not be regarded as this person entering into me; nor would their speech and whispering be considered as the domination of their spirit over mine. It would be merely the sound waves of some uttered words originating from one spirit and hitting the surface of a second spirit, despite the considerable distance between them.

Similarly, wireless radio stations may broadcast from a particular area and the sound waves will be received by other sets situated far away. In fact, this is the perfect example to clarify the point we are making; it also demonstrates how the devil did not need to approach our master Adam (pth) or enter into his spirit in order to give him a message. He was unable to approach him because he (pth) was continuously tending towards Al’lah. Being of a sublime nature, our master Adam (pth) never knew any kind of evil but thought that all people were goodhearted. Even if he had been informed otherwise he would not have remembered this because he was in a spiritual state in which his capacity for thought was dormant, and therefore had no memory. He also possessed a genuine innocence which made him unaware of people for he still had no actual experience of any person except his wife at that time. Since his spirit contained nothing but goodness and perfection, he was unable to anticipate the existence of any animosity from anything in God’s Creation; nor did he know that there was such a thing as a lie, for he (pth) was still behaving in accordance with the perfection with which Al’lah created humanity.

The idea of being untruthful had never once occurred to him, especially when Satan swore a false oath by Al’lah. But afterwards, he became aware of the existence of enmity, the shunning of Al’lah, slyness and treachery. He also recognised Satan’s hostility towards him. Had he previously known Satan and his capacity for deception he would have responded to him with a ray of God’s Light, which would surely have burnt him as punishment for his deviousness and his shunning of Al’lah. However, since he had not yet started to think he was unable to remember his instructions from God.

Subsequently Satan realised that he could not approach the Prophets (ptt) once he had been unmasked and his evil intentions had been revealed, as referred to by the verses, ‘

“Truly, I shall seduce them all [humankind], except Your pure selected servants from among them.”

’ ﴿201﴾

In fact the devil only whispered to Adam from a distance which is clear in God’s Words, ‘

The devil whispered to him.

’ ﴿202﴾

God did not say that the devil whispered into his chest or his spirit as, for example, when He says, ‘

He who whispers evil in the chests of oblivious humankind,

’ ﴿203﴾

– That is, in the chests of those who are disconnected from Al’lah, the Almighty. It is clear that the preposition ‘to’ indicates separation while ‘in’ indicates a position of inclusiveness. This whispering from a distance could never be mistaken as the devil drawing near to our master Adam (pth) or entering his spirit. Furthermore, this account can never be regarded as proof of the devil’s ability to enter into any of the Prophets (ptt).

Finally, the following illustrates how the devil can never approach the Prophets (ptt) in their bodily state. They are like the rest of humankind in terms of how their bodies surround and control their spirits. They are born just like anyone else, and their bodies are exposed to the same conditions that affect others, such as good health or disease, youth and old age, weakness, senility and death. As for their spirits (ptt), they have a constant tendency to Al’lah, and they have become devoted to that Lofty Presence due to their knowledge of the Tenderness and Mercy that Al’lah has for everything in His Creation, and their witnessing of His Perfection and His unlimited Beauty. Consequently they are always overwhelmed with the Godly Revelation, and eternally covered with that Light. In this bodily state, since the spirit is surrounded by the body the devil’s whispering can never reach it from a distance. He has to penetrate the spirit by first passing through the chest. However, the bodies of the Prophets (ptt) are protected by always being engulfed in the Godly Light that comes to their spirits, due to their unswerving honesty before Al’lah and their great love for Him. So, because the devil is unable to penetrate this Godly Light he can never approach them. Through this Revelation they (ptt) are safe in an inaccessible fortress which provides them with a forbidding shelter from the devil.

We have shown that Satan has no possible way to enter into the Prophets (ptt), equally he cannot reach any believer as long as their spirit is entering into Al’lah’s Presence, tending towards Him or being joined with His honourable and loyal Prophets (ptt). Al’lah guides a person to this means by which they can be rid of the devil. He says, ‘

When Satan inspires evil to you, seek refuge in God; He hears all and knows all. When those who seek piety [see by Al’lah’s Light] are touched by a passing satanic temptation, they remember [Al’lah] and then they become enlightened.

’ ﴿204﴾

He also says, ‘

No power has he [Satan] over believers who put their trust in their Provider. He has power only over those who befriend him and those who obey other gods besides Him [Al’lah].

’ ﴿205﴾

Having answered these sensitive questions, we shall address a new point which can be summarised by the following question:

chapters.title: Was the Coming of Adam (pth) and All That Ensued, the Best Course?
chapters.html:
Was the coming of our master Adam (pth) to this lower life, followed by the rest of humanity, for the best? Would it have been better for him to stay in Paradise, and for the rest of humanity to have been created there without allowing them to enter into the lower, earthly life? Which of the two states would have brought about more happiness and goodness for humankind?

This point can be clarified if we return to the words about Paradise and its reality, and take into consideration the fact that a person’s level in Paradise will be in proportion to their deeds. For example: let us suppose that a man was travelling on a train that was passing through an area of beautiful scenery; from the windows he was gazing at amazing wonders created by Al’lah. He could see flowers and trees, rivers and lakes, charming scenes and various beautiful towns and cities, the like of which people had never seen or even imagined before. As long as this train kept moving this traveller would crane his neck towards these sights, not wanting to turn away because of their constant, incomparable appeal. However, if the train stopped for any length of time, you would find that the traveller would turn away from the window, no matter how beautiful and pleasant the sight before him. This is because the spirit which God the Almighty has created and made of infinite capacity begins to feel tired if it is kept in the same state, for the human spirit is disposed to curiosity. If a person remains in the same state they will become bored, because however beautiful or delightful something may be, it will become monotonous and even loathsome if it does not alter.

In line with this, we say that a person’s ascension in the overwhelming joy of their entrance into God’s Presence depends, as previously mentioned, on the good deeds they have done in their worldly life. This means that if human beings had been created in Paradise and had never come into this lower world, we would not have carried out any deeds by which we could approach our Creator; nor could we have risen from one state to a higher one, and from one Paradise to another that is more expansive and loftier than the one before. To put it simply, the human race would have remained at one level. Almighty God created the human spirit and granted it the greatest of all gifts. He gave it the ability to advance gradually in its witnessing of Godly Perfection, and to enjoy it increasingly, with no limit or end. The Envoy (cpth) clarified this in a holy saying when God said, ‘

Not My earth or My heaven could bear My Revelations, but the heart of My believing servant could.

’ ﴿206﴾

Then, He, the Almighty, brought this human spirit to this world and gave it a wide scope of action in order for it to qualify for this endless witnessing and this rising through the successive levels. He created our yearning to be a motive for the action that gives it a certain value. Thereby Almighty God has made humankind fit to attain the greatest share of Godly Favour and eternal bliss, which no other being can ever attain. Such being the case, surely you believe that our exodus to this world was a Favour and a Grace of God. Is it not better than keeping us in a single Paradise? Instead of one lofty Paradise with obtainable fruits, God has given us endless elevated Paradises of increasing and ascending sublime pleasure, in which the spirit immerses itself eagerly due to their wonderful variety and ascendancy, one above another, in their majesty and dignity. Whoever tastes them will have their heart filled with joy and delight, and love for the great Merciful God Who continues to overwhelm them with ever increasing bliss. There will be no boredom and no fatigue; on the contrary, there will be pleasure mixed with joy, as well as increasing ascension and closeness to the Benefactor, the Merciful One, moving from one Paradise to endless others. The steps by which this believer will ascend from one level to another are their own deeds combined with their humane intentions.

In the noble verse, God reveals that bringing the human race into the lower world was better for them than if they had remained in the state in which our master Adam (pth) began. God says, ‘

Children of Adam! We have given you garments [God’s Manifestations through Prophets] to cover your bad deeds [that disgrace and displease you] and as adornment for you [good deeds that raise you up]; the garment of piety [seeing by God’s Light] is the best of all garments – this is one of God’s Signs, so that people may take heed [and remember Satan’s enmity].

’ ﴿207﴾

The garment of piety which Adam (pth) had is better than his original state. Similarly, taking a child out of their comfortable home and sending them to school where there are restrictions and pressures, is better for them than keeping the child at home where they are free and boisterous. That is because their progress is accomplished by education. If they do not go to school they will never achieve any advancement. Worldly life is like a school that leads to elevation, both in this life and in the life to come.

Our master Adam (pth) started off enjoying only a single Paradise, but after his worldly life he gained access to many levels of Paradise, rising increasingly towards better and more perfect levels with desirable and attractive continuity; that is to say, he gained endless Paradises instead of just a single Paradise.

chapters.title: The Wise Will Learn from This Account
chapters.html:
We now know how man came to this lower life where favourable and charitable deeds can be carried out. On this earth you can do many good deeds that will be displayed to you in the Hereafter, and through which you are promoted from one state to a higher one, and from one Paradise to another that is even higher. If you pursue the path of righteousness you will be a true believer, and if you go to school and exert yourself you will be elevated, but if you do not go to school you will remain at a lower level. Al’lah the Almighty has mentioned His Command and Adam’s forgetfulness (pth), as related in this account, only in your own interest, to bring you happiness through your understanding of it, to allow you to avoid Satan’s deception by your thinking strictly and acting positively. This is how you will rise and enjoy Godly Gifts. Al’lah the Almighty was Omniscient of Adam and his wife (ptt). He knew precisely that Adam had no power of thought at that time, in addition to knowing that he would surely forget His Command. But the Almighty used this approach of giving Adam an order, knowing that Adam would forget the order, only to remind us of Satan’s enmity; this was also to make us aware of Satan, as well as to tell us that anyone who stumbles through no intention of their own can easily return to their place in Al’lah’s Presence. However, whoever is purposely unmindful can never return until they repent. Satan has no access to the true believer for Al’lah the Almighty is the Protector of those who believe, whereas Satan is able to get near to those who have no true faith. So, one learns that it is important to seek to achieve true faith. In the Holy Qur’an, God says, ‘

No power has he [Satan] over believers who put their trust in their Provider. He has power only over those who befriend him and those who obey other gods besides Him [Al’lah].

’ ﴿208﴾

Mankind should seek to achieve true faith, for anyone who does not believe truly in Al’lah will certainly be destroyed. Faith is not achieved merely through speaking, but also through being mindful and witnessing that the Almighty is the All-Hearing and the Omniscient Force Who directs every motion. If you endeavour to reach that level of faith, then you must consider this universe, think carefully, and you will believe that there is no god but Al’lah. Only then will this account act as an instructive lesson and a reminder for you.

chapters.title: Chapter Three, TRUE FAITH
chapters.html:
The Way of Belief and True Faith

This universe contains so many wonders: the sun and the moon, the planets and stars, rain and ice, clouds and winds, animals and plants, the heavens and even the earth in its circular orbit, the four seasons with their changes and sequences, and night and day with their differences and alternation. That is to say, the universe contains this abundant world filled with all its wondrous creatures and beings. This includes your body and the fascinating composition of its systems and organs, and the constant dissolution and composition that happen within it, ensuring that it has all that it requires for survival. The universe is filled with everything that you know and everything that you do not know, and runs according to firm rules and strict discipline.

Therefore, if the Great Creator has laid down a law for this universe with all its creatures, and a system to be followed and never broken, and if this Great Creator has taken that same universe and controlled it for humans, the most noble of all creatures, is it then possible that He did not provide them with the appropriate law or statute to guide them? Has the Great Creator arranged the entire universe, only to leave humankind to live this life without guidance or order? Has the Great Creator put this entire universe in order and then neglected mankind and let them wander in spiritual darkness, unable to distinguish between that which is beneficial to them and that which is damaging? It is undoubtedly true that positive thought, sound logic, and intelligent understanding confess to the undeniable existence of a law which has been planned for humankind. The question then, is, where is that law and order?

Let us consider what all the noble Envoys (ptt) brought from God. Let us pay attention to the first verses with which the Almighty Al’lah inspired the Envoy (cpth), so that he (cpth) could inform people. God says, ‘

Read in the Name of your Provider, Who has created; He has created man from clots! Read, and your Provider is the Noblest One, Who has taught by printing, ﴿209﴾

He has taught man what he did not know.

’ ﴿210﴾

Let us think deeply about these words which the Envoy (cpth) disseminated to all the Arabs and people of all other nations. Let us ponder upon that guidance to which the Envoy (cpth) led his noble companions, and let us study the Qur’anic verses sent from Al’lah which he (cpth) recited to the people in Mecca during the first days of his mission. Let us look as someone who is thirsty for the truth might look, rather than as someone who is clinging to the habits and beliefs that their forefathers followed blindly. Let us leave behind the ignorance which has come about through the mere whims and misguidedness of some people. Let us return to righteousness, for the way of righteousness is the only way that should be followed. Rather, let us choose to be guided by the noble Envoys (ptt) and adopt the straight path that they all adopted before us. When you do that you will discover the order and the law that is laid down in the Qur’an for humanity to follow. It was this same law which the Envoy (cpth) applied for himself and his people, and which he called upon all his noble companions to apply. In this way they achieved high rank and became known all over the world. This was how they gained great happiness and much favour.

To apply this law and order is to consider your origin and to think of your beginning, because those who recognise themselves will recognise Who their Provider is. Once they recognise Him, they will be guided to the way of happiness and protected from anguish and loss. Therefore, those whom God guides are those who have adopted the straight path, but those who stray from God will find no other lord than Him.

Think of your origin, for thinking of your origin and your beginning is the first article of this law and order which Al’lah has put in place for you. Think! Why do you not think, since your Provider has granted you such a precious gift to help you to think, to lead you to know your Creator and Provider? Think! Why do you not think, when He has given you the great signs and the amazing discipline of this universe with its wide fields and great scope in which your thoughts can roam and become absorbed? Think! Why do you not think, since the universe is like an open book before you? You can read even if there is no teacher to teach you or no one to guide you, because Almighty Al’lah is the best Teacher and Guide for you, as long as you are truthful. Think of your origin when you were a speck of semen in your father’s back. Consider this minute speck, how was it formed? Of what is it composed? Consider too, where was it first placed, and where did it settle? Think of yourself when you were in that safe haven, the deep darkness of your mother’s womb. Think of those stages through which you have passed: from semen to a clot, from a clot to a lump of flesh, from a lump of flesh to bones. Consider how these bones have been arranged in consistent good order; the muscles have been fixed upon the bones, and openings have been made in those bones for the brain, the eyes, the ears and the mouth; there is a cage for the heart and the lungs; there are vessels for the intestines, and centres for the veins and for the sinews.

Think and think again! We shall not develop this in greater detail but leave it for you to ponder upon and see how semen, ultimately made from an extract of various fruits and vegetables grown in the soil and consumed by man, has turned into a balanced human being, a noble creature.

Think of, and appreciate, the Greatness of the Hand Which created and formed you. It created your organs for you, the main systems of the body; It created your bone structure and all of the other various components, and then placed them within a safe place as though within a protected stronghold. Think of that Hand Which nourished you when you were just coming into this world, alone and helpless. You were unable to provide for yourself and, indeed, nobody could provide for you except the Hand Which watched over your Creation. It is that same Hand Which provided for you, delivering food to you and supplying each of your organs with its necessary sustenance. Think of that Hand, Which was Able to turn you from semen into a perfect person within just a few months, so that Its Creation would neither be delayed nor premature in forming a human being within the appointed term. Then, when the time of birth and entry into this world approached, It turned you upside down in your mother’s womb, placing your head facedown, thus preparing the easiest way for your entry into this world. God says, ‘

Man has been destroyed. What makes him ungrateful? [Does he never consider] from what thing did He create him? From semen He created and proportioned him. Thereafter He lets him easily pass along the path, then causes him to die and stows him in a grave. Then, when He pleases, He will resurrect him. No! Indeed he has not yet fulfilled what He has bidden him.

’ ﴿211﴾

Having come into this new world and this new land, think how He endowed you with your mother’s sympathy and kindness, and filled her heart with love and tenderness for you. He prepared your food in her breasts, ensuring that it was pleasant and delicious to drink, and that it contained all the nourishment needed and required by your body. Think of those meals and nutriments which that Merciful Hand made for you. It increased their nutritional proportions moment by moment and meal after meal, in a way that was appropriate to your growth as time passed. Then, when your body required even greater nourishment and your stomach became able to digest solid foods, He caused your milk teeth to grow, one tooth after another, as it became necessary. Later, when you were seven years old, in order to build a body that would be ready for serious situations and great deeds, and to create a thought process that could manage important matters, He replaced your milk teeth with adult ones to process the food that would be necessary for this human body as it grew to maturity.

Think of that Hand Which is still providing for you until now. It directs the warm rays of the sun into the sea in order to vaporise the water and form it into clouds. It then impels the winds to rouse the clouds and drive them from the places where they lurk in readiness, gathering them and piling them up in towering masses through which drops of water pour down, expressing God’s Cordiality towards His creatures. Once the dry earth is irrigated and revived from its thirst, It then dispels the clouds and reveals the clear blue sky and the radiant sun. This allows plants to begin their growth cycle again, and it is then that the land grants us God’s lavish Blessings. He says, ‘

Have you considered the fact that you cultivate? Is it you that give it growth, or We? If We pleased, We could turn it into chaff. Would you then keep enjoying yourselves [or would you say], “We have incurred a loss. Indeed, we are deprived”? Have you considered the water which you drink? Was it you that poured it from the well-measured clouds, or We? If We pleased, We could turn it saline; so why do you not give thanks?

’ ﴿212﴾

Consider all the types of foods and their various kinds, and the myriad flowers and their beautiful shapes and perfumes, and the numerous varieties of fruit and their colours and flavours. Consider the four seasons and their rotation. Consider sleep and how God the Almighty has made it a period of rest when we cease to feel. Consider the day and how He made it a means for survival. Think of the air which helps you to breathe and which, by the very act of breathing regularly provides the oxygen needed to burn materials within the body. Think of the sun which supplies you with heat and light. Think of the seas and rivers, plains and mountains, animals and plants, clothes and the fabrics of which they are made: wool, cotton, flax and silk. Think of this Hand, Which fulfils all your requirements and continues to rear you, showering you with Its Blessing, overwhelming you with Its Favour, and supplying you with every necessary provision. And It does this, moment after moment, without end.

Ponder all this, and think of this Providence, for it was through such thought and reflection that our master Abraham (pth) took his first step in the way of belief. Through such thinking, our master Adam (pth) and our master Mohammad (cpth), and all the noble Envoys (ptt) who came through the ages, started on their individual path to belief. Think! If you followed their example you would be guided and would know that there is a Great Provider Who looks after you and never neglects you even for the twinkling of an eye. This Provider has continued to provide for you from the time that you were an embryo until you became an infant, and then a young child, and then an adult. Therefore His Sustenance to you is permanent and His Charity continues to flow over you without end. If these things settle inside your spirit so that it becomes mindful of them and you are certain of their reality, a different way of thinking will open before you.

If this were to happen, you would see that your body will not remain either strong or resistant, and that you will not live forever.

This is how it was for your relatives who have left this life.

And it is the same with your neighbour who has met his death and parted from his spouse and children, after enjoying the worldly life for only a few years. Furthermore, your friends were not able to take pleasure in their stores or in the houses which they built. They died at the time appointed to them, so death also brought an end to all their hopes in this life. There are those who have died after illness, others after troubles, and others suddenly and unexpectedly. You might remember this one and that one, the kings and princes, the supreme commanders, the rich and the poor, and even the noble Envoys (ptt), and you find that death has not left one of them untouched. Then you will be sure that death is your inevitable end also, despite all your efforts to stave it off; just as it was the end of everyone who came before you. There is no escape from it. At that time you will find no hope in this life and you will fully realise that this is nothing more than a temporary world.

Thinking of death produces fear and awe in your spirit, and generates a serious desire to attain knowledge of the Provider, making you truly rush to seek Him. You ask yourself Who this Provider is, Who created you from semen – though you were nothing worth mentioning before that time – and then made you into a child and eventually a perfect adult. You contemplate the universe once again, but you look deeper than before. There you will find that It is this Provider Who guides the sun and the moon and directs the entire universe and all that it contains in order to provide for you and to fulfil all your demands and meet all your needs. There is no hand and no act of anyone besides His.

He alone is Al’lah, and there is no god but Him.

And so you will move from believing in the Provider to a new level, which is believing that this Provider is the Steering God. You will see the heavenly bodies floating within their orbits, and witness the sun sending down its warming rays. Moreover, you will see the clouds moving, stirred from their hidden sites, and the winds blowing gently or gusting violently according to their direction and the season. You will see the waters of the great seas churning and their waves chopping, the rivers rising from their sources, and flowing down to their estuaries where they enter the seas. As for the terrestrial globe, you will see it orbiting within its designated space and spinning on its own axis, carrying all creatures on its surface. You will see all of this moving and churning and spinning, but all is only through the Power and Command of God. You will think more and more deeply until you realise that no creature can take a single step or raise a hand or move a single inch except by God’s Leave, Will and Power.

Thereafter you will advance further in your thinking, ascending until you reach a degree of understanding where you realise that the entire universe is a single unit of interconnected parts and bonded atoms. Furthermore, you will recognise that it all works in harmony and uniformity, and that it is the Godly Will that watches over it and supports it.

You will know that the Provider is the Steering God of the whole universe and there is no director or god other than Him. You will know that your Provider is Al’lah, and therefore, once your spirit has witnessed this in the universe and you have ascertained it within your own depths, you will say the words: there is no god but Al’lah. You will speak these words because they will have become lodged in your mind; you will accept no false imitation or what you have heard from others. Your belief in this will be similar to that of the goodly ancestors and the noble companions rather than the random belief of old men, which is based on legends and myths. Thus, you will truly believe in this statement and will say with heart and soul: there is no god but Al’lah. That is some of what we understand from God’s Saying, ‘

Know that there is no god but Al’lah.

’ ﴿213﴾

In the hadith, the Envoy (cpth) says, ‘

He who says, “There is no god but Al’lah”, faithfully and loyally, will enter Paradise. It was said, “What is the sign of its loyalty?” He said, “To keep him away from what is forbidden by Al’lah.”

’ ﴿214﴾

Surely, this will prevent anyone from doing anything that is forbidden by God, because they will see that Al’lah the Almighty is with them, watching and observing them wherever they go and whatever they do.

chapters.title: The Fruits of Certain Belief
chapters.html:
Having arrived at this stage – the belief that there is no god but Al’lah, and that He is the Provider – we shall make rapid progress, as you are now able to follow our account with greater ease. We shall now reveal to you the effects of believing that there is no god but Al’lah, and lead you to the love for the Envoy of God (cpth). When you believe that there is no god but Al’lah you become one of those who see that God’s Hand controls the movement of the universe. When your spirit is immersed in this view of God’s Controlling of the universe you will see that no winds blow, no clouds cover the sky, no rain falls, no lightning flashes, no thunder resounds, no sea runs high or low with restless waves, no river flows in constant flux, no volcano erupts angrily, no flood streams forth with force or intensity, no earthquake shakes the land causing forgetful and heedless hearts to tremble in fear, no earth rotates, causing night and day and the four seasons, no shining stars float within their galaxies, except as directed by the Hand of the Wise and Peerless One. It is only by your own efforts and daily contemplation that you will observe that the universe – with all its creatures – is a single marvellous system controlled and guided by the Will of the Cognisant and Omniscient One.

What is more, without Him your physical body does not function: your hand does not move; your eye does not blink; your ear hears no sound; your heart does not beat; your stomach does not break down the foods inside it; your liver does not store certain substances or secrete others according to its set standards; your lungs do not expand and contract between inhalation and exhalation; your blood does not flow in arteries and veins; the red corpuscles do not carry what they should carry to and fro; the white corpuscles do not fight and struggle with microbes; and germs do not attack the body.

Furthermore, if you become sure of all this by your ability to think and by spiritual witnessing, rather than by listening to specialists or reading various books and other printed material, you will see that everything is controlled by God’s Hand and that all people, everywhere, be they dignitaries or commoners, be they near or far, strong or weak, and even all of the creatures of the earth – none of these can be of any benefit to you, nor protect you from any evil, nor hurt you, nor cause any change in your situation, except by Al’lah’s Leave. Thus you will enter the stronghold of righteousness and you will never exceed God’s Bounds. Since the spirit cannot remain motionless, you will find that once it has rejected all bad deeds and turned completely towards Al’lah, it will spare no effort in doing charitable and beneficial deeds. It will become absorbed in helping everyone in need because it will wish to approach Al’lah by means of this activity.

At this stage – the stage of integrity according to God’s Order – the spirit will be confident of its benevolence and of God’s Satisfaction with it. As a result of this confidence, it will draw nearer to its Creator and turn entirely towards Him, so that a link will be established. Then its communication with God will be correct. It will see that it lives in a state of closeness rather than distance, feeling love and purity rather than coolness or reluctance. It will consequently enjoy a happy life of tranquillity and bliss. At this time, the spirit will gain two fruits that it would never have gained without this link to the Creator and the entrance into His Presence, and it will gain them only by virtue of this link, this direction, and this pleasurable communication with God.

The first fruit to be gained is that by turning towards its Creator, all sins will fall away from the spirit; the word ‘sins’ here refers to the base desires that are attached to the spirit and the defects that are rooted in it. By communicating with God these lowly yearnings will be eroded and fall away, so that the spirit will be purified of disease. It will emerge from this communication having been purified; it will be free of the lust that once intruded on it, and the dirt that once soiled it. It will no longer hold any base desires such as stinginess; there will be no cowardice, no attachment to this worldly life, no miserliness, no rudeness, no grossness, no hard-heartedness, no desire to do damage, no cowering, no subservience, no inclination to oppression or aggression, and no wish for worldly glory or authority.

Thus, there will be none of the bad qualities that degrade humanity’s esteem or standing among people or with God. All of these negative qualities will be wiped out by the link with Al’lah and the entrance into His Presence. The Envoy (cpth) explained the effect that communication with God has on the spirit of humanity in a noble saying, where he (cpth) says, ‘

“Suppose there is a river flowing beside the doorway of one of you, and that this person washes himself there, five times a day. What do you say about this? Will any of his dirt remain?” They said that no dirt would remain. He told them that this example explains the five prayers. Al’lah effaces misdeeds through them.

’ ﴿215﴾

That is the first fruit that results from entering into God’s Presence and performing the correct communication with Al’lah.

As for the second fruit, you will be overjoyed if you acquire it, and we explain it as follows: When your spirit attains the link with your Creator, you will feel life flowing in its depths, just as one feels the reviving warmth of the sun on days that are bitterly cold. You will feel life spreading in your spirit, as one feels a gentle breeze of fresh air while sitting in the shade of a tree on a hot midsummer’s day. You will feel life entering your spirit, just as a thirsty man feels cool water flowing into their body, quenching their thirst and refreshing them, body and soul. For the true believer there is no feeling more beautiful than what they feel in their times of closeness to their Creator and Provider. Moreover, while you are absorbed in this state of exaltation and sublimity, great impressions of perfection will be imprinted on the surface of your spirit. That is the second fruit that the spirit gains through true communication and nearness to Al’lah.

This perfection which colours the spirit as it enters into God’s Presence, will be manifested in the spirit of the believer in the form of so many wonderful qualities: mercy, tenderness, generosity, bounty, chivalry, helping the needy, telling the truth, openness of speech, kindness, gentleness, politeness, patience, deliberateness, modesty, bravery, justice, equity, self-esteem, a sense of honour, resistance to falseness, and so forth. Whatever attributes and indications of perfection one may mention, you will find that the spirit acquires them and is stained by them when it is near to Al’lah, for God says, ‘

It is the Stain of Al’lah. And who gives a better stain than Al’lah when we are worshipping Him?

’ ﴿216﴾

When the spirit reaches such a stage and ascends to such a rank through its perfection and good conduct, you will find that it loves all other people of perfection and high merit. It will love those people because of the perfection it has achieved itself, for no one appreciates a virtue except those who possess it, and only people of perfection can recognise perfection in others. In this way, if the spirit sees people who are generous and unstinting, it appreciates their superiority in those attributes, and if it meets people who are compassionate and affectionate, it will value their superiority over itself in those attributes also. And so it is with all the other supreme qualities and morals. The spirit will naturally appreciate any who surpass and exceed it, and therefore it will love perfect believers when it encounters them; equally, if it meets truthful leaders it will revere them and accompany them. The Envoy of God (cpth) is the master of the people of perfection, and supersedes all the worlds in this domain. Moreover, because of his closeness to his Creator he (cpth) attained the greatest share of perfection from that Godly Presence, so that no angel or human could even approach his rank. Consequently, you will find that a believer is devoted to God’s Envoy (cpth).

In the view of a true believer there is no being greater than the Envoy (cpth), and nobody has a rank higher than his (cpth). When believers hear any words spoken about him (cpth) their hearts long for him; if his name or his merits or his deeds are mentioned, their spirits travel over great distances across the eras and generations that separate them in order to accompany that revered spirit, and maintain a firm unbreakable link with it. By way of this spiritual flowing and through this moral connection to that spirit – the pure and virtuous spirit of the Envoy (cpth) – and by becoming one of those who attain such a level, your spirit will ascend gently and unconsciously in the company of the Envoy’s spirit which constantly enters into the Presence of Al’lah. Thus your spirit will be together with that of the Envoy (cpth) in the Presence of God.

At that moment, the light of the Envoy (cpth) – whom Almighty Al’lah has called ‘the Shining Lamp’– will illuminate an aspect of God’s Perfection for you. This will allow you to witness all that you deserve of God’s Compassion, Tenderness, Sympathy, Kindness, Clemency, Charity, Justice, Might, Knowledge, Wisdom, abundant Favour, Provision, comprehensive Steering, Boons for every being that has life and a soul, and all the other Godly Attributes, which will enthral all who witness them. Out of its passion and love for Godly Perfection that arises from seeing the Supreme Attributes, the spirit attains a high link with its Creator. This link is achieved through the love produced when one witnesses the Godly Attributes and Perfection. This is the way that leads to the acquisition of a mind that is illuminated by Godly Light and is the way one should adopt by accompanying and following the great master Mohammad (cpth). This is the way by which a believer realises a part of the Godly Perfections in their spirit, after they have thought about them, believed in them and understood them fully. They also realise the secret that lies behind Godly Legislation and the benefits that are concealed behind the Orders which the Almighty sent down to His Envoy (cpth) in the Holy Qur’an. With any verse they hear, they

under stand

the meanings that it contains on a level that is in proportion to their link with, and their nearness to, their Creator.

Through this link the spirit will acquire a light from Al’lah the Almighty that allows it to see goodness, and understand that it really is good. Consequently, the spirit likes this goodness and will become inclined towards it. Similarly, the spirit comes to see evil and understand that it really is evil, and so it will disdain and loathe it. Truly, this is the level of piety (seeing by Al’lah’s Light) to which the Almighty Al’lah urged His faithful servants and with which He charged them, ‘

You who believe, seek piety [see by Al’lah’s Light], and be with the truthful.

’ ﴿217﴾

God says, ‘

You who believe: seek piety [see by Al’lah’s Light] and believe in His Envoy. He will grant you two portions of His Compassion and make a light for you by which you can go, and He will forgive you. Al’lah is All-Forgiving and All-Merciful.

’ ﴿218﴾

In another Fortress He says, ‘

You who believe, if you become pious [illuminated by Al’lah’s Light], He will grant you the power of discrimination and veil your sins from you and forgive you. Al’lah is of great bounty.

’ ﴿219﴾

He also says, ‘

You who believe, seek piety [see by Al’lah’s Light] and speak apposite speech. He will make your deeds right and forgive you your sins. Those who obey Al’lah and His Envoy will achieve a great success.

’ ﴿220﴾

Without doubt, that is true piety. In Arabic, the word ‘piety’ means ‘avoidance.’ Therefore we understand that ‘piety’ means avoiding evil by means of Al’lah’s Light. This is the avoidance of danger once you have witnessed the causes of corruption in this worldly life by means of the Godly Light – the Light to which you would never have gained access if your spirit had not connected with that of the Envoy (cpth). And so, belief in the Envoy (cpth) comes after belief in God, and loving the Envoy (cpth) is always connected with real faith and associated with true communication with God.

The noble saying denotes, ‘

He that has no love has no faith. He that has no love has no faith. He that has no love has no faith.

’ ﴿221﴾

Indeed, the favour of the Envoy (cpth) is so boundless that no one can express it.

Once a human being has gained piety they will treat all creatures with kindness as they will have truly understood the meaning of God’s Justice. They will start to draw people’s attention to the well-arranged universe in the heavens as well as on earth, and the wisdom behind all things. They will show to others God’s Good Names and the wisdom in His Actions, all of which refer to mercy, wisdom and justice. For this reason, it is very important to illustrate the principle of God’s Justice, otherwise it may be perceived as a vague ideal from the general point of view.

chapters.title: God’s Justice
chapters.html:
The reality of Godly Justice was still denied by huge masses of ignorant people, though this undeniable fact is as clear as daylight for those who think carefully and reflect deeply on this universe, and if they are truly sincere in their search for the truth. Contemplating the sky with its huge celestial bodies, its wonderful stars and planets, and the outstanding accuracy of their perfect creation and movement will lead the observer to the decision that there must be a Great Creator and an Almighty Steering God Who directs and organises all these with meticulous regulation. But when looking at the earth and seeing the rich and the poor, the black and the white, the oppressors and the oppressed, the tall and the short, the beautiful and the ugly, the healthy and the ill, the happy and the sad, this encroaching on that, and that stealing from this, the strong killing the weak, and states annexing states, such a thinker may decide that there is no God, and no Creator or Arranger. For if God is there in the sky and He is the Organiser and Controller, why does He not maintain the earth? When this person’s thoughts turn to injustice on this earth, they deny the Existence of God: a God Who is Supervising, Controlling, Omniscient, and Who oversees everyone and is Omnipresent surely cannot allow this. Either there is injustice and no God, or there is God and no injustice. This is the quandary: what is the reply?

God Does Exist and There Is No Injustice

The Almighty Creator, the Great Director exists in the sky and on earth. He is in and beyond the sky with His Beauty, and on earth with His Compassion. Every single movement comes from His Omniscience, Direction, perfect Motion and Precision in the sky and on earth. There is no creator except God, Who has created and directed all that was created in the heavens and on earth, so there is no injustice at all. God the Almighty says, ‘

It is He Who is God in heaven and God on earth. And He is the All- Wise and Omniscient.’ ﴿222﴾

Mankind came to this world after promising their Provider that they would recognise Him, follow His Light and never turn away from Him. They would carry out good deeds and be charitable to all His Creation and servants. When man came to this world and God covered their spirit with a physical body as its garment and gave them the power of choice, they forgot their promise to God, and deviated from humanity and the straight path which they had promised to follow. But God’s Mercy did not leave this human being in such a plight; He provided them with the ability to think and distinguished them above all His other creatures. He also provided them with all the senses such as hearing and vision. He presented them with cosmic miracles such as the stars, the planets, the sun and the moon, the rain, and many other bounties to direct them. If they consider all that surrounds them, in the heavens and on earth, they will find that these wonders will guide them to Almighty God, as they did with Abraham and his brothers, the Envoys (ptt). Through death, which takes away their relatives and loved ones, God intended to waken them from their satisfaction with this fleeting world and unfounded arrogance in order to help them ascend to the rank of humanity, achieve perfection and gain access to Paradises. God also sent the noble Envoys (ptt) to mankind to remind them, and He sent the angels to rouse their thought. He made laws and regulations to organise all aspects of man’s life.

Despite the mercy, love and kindness that God has shown to man, man has deviated from the path that leads to happiness and real eternal life. They became absorbed in their detestable lusts: hurting, killing, and stealing from Al’lah’s servants, yet they wouldn’t be able to kill, steal or hurt anyone except those who had previously killed, stolen and harmed others who were weaker than them. Therefore, God gives a free hand to one oppressor against another, but they, in fact, wrong only themselves. God says, ‘

Thus We let some of the wrong-doers have power over others because of what they are wont to earn.

’ ﴿223﴾

At the same time the oppressor has no authority to harm anyone who is strictly following the straight path of righteousness and humanity: according to the Orders of Almighty God. He (Glory to Him) says, ‘

What does Al’lah gain by your punishment if you are grateful [in offering good acts], and yet you believe? Al’lah is Worthy of thanks and Omniscient.

’ ﴿224﴾

– Why does He punish you? He created happiness for you in this life and in the Hereafter. But because there is evil in your spirit, He inflicts these hardships upon you. Out of the Mercy of the All-Merciful and the Wisdom of the All-Wise, the oppressor is not left to do what would cause them to live in a hellish state. God inflicts hardship, disease, poverty, and other deprivations upon them. God says, ‘

We shall test you with something of fear and hunger.

’ – Meaning that if the believer inadvertently falls into wrongful ways, Al’lah reminds them by sending them afflictions. Out of His Sympathy and Compassion, He wants to purify you from all filth, for man cannot enter Paradise if their spirit is not pure.

So, times of hardship and distress are to remind you of God in order to cleanse your spirit. When you are afraid, you turn to Al’lah to seek refuge and the impurity will disappear from your spirit. This hardship can be compared to a surgical operation, but one which removes evil. ‘

Some loss in wealth, lives and the fruits [of your toil], but give glad tidings to those who patiently preserve

’ – Meaning that if someone has done something wrong, Al’lah will punish them in order to cure them. So they must be patient, for Al’lah cures the believer in order to make them pure and once this is achieved Al’lah will take them into Paradise. But if they persist in remaining impure, their disease will be serious and momentous. ‘

Who say when afflicted with calamity.

’ – This is when the person is cured: the hardship comes and hits the points of the spiritual illness and pain, and then they are purified. ‘

To God we belong

’ – therefore surrendering to Al’lah; ‘

and to Him we repent and return

’ – Meaning, they repent and turn back to Him. ‘

They are those on whom communications and mercy descend from their Provider.

’ – The meaning of this verse is that their patience and confession of God’s Mercy cause their spirits to become purified. Thus the Godly Revelation descends upon them. ‘

And those who are guided

’ ﴿225﴾

– to righteousness. The result of this is that they receive a light from Al’lah and they enter Paradise. And His Saying (Glory to His Names), ‘

And indeed We will make them taste of the lightest chastisement before the greatest chastisement in order that they may [repent and] return

’ ﴿226﴾

– This states that God lets these oppressors experience suffering in this world so that they may repent and return to their Provider and thereby stop the injustice they bring upon themselves.

God will only empower one oppressor over another so that they may become aware of their negligent behaviour and stop their acts of aggression. All this is done through the Omniscience and Wisdom of the Almighty God and on a similar level to the oppressor’s heedless behaviour. These adversities are sufficiently difficult to cause the oppressor to awaken from their negligence, so they are not evil to themselves, but they are merciful and good. God says, ‘

And if Al’lah did not keep a check on one set of people by means of another, the earth would indeed be full of mischief. But Al’lah is Full of bounty to all Creation.

’ ﴿227﴾

The situation is similar to that of the teacher who puts pressure on his lazy pupils or the father on his careless sons.

All this chastisement is simply a form of mercy, kindness and love, and not oppression or punishment. God the Almighty says, ‘

Say, “Oh God of all! Possessor of all the possessions [Creator of power and rule]. You give possession and power to whom You please, and remove possession and power from whom You will. You endow with honour those whom You please and You debase whom You will. In Your Hand is nothing but goodness. Truly, over all things [You have], You are Omnipotent.”

’ ﴿228﴾

That is, there is only goodness in the Hands of God; because whether He gives or deprives, cherishes or humiliates, the result for the recipient is that they are receiving what is appropriate for their own good. The doctor who may be obliged to cut open the abdomen of his patient and possibly remove what ails him is similar to this. This necessary surgical procedure may, however, deprive his patient of many pleasures. The behaviour of the father, the teacher or the doctor might be seen from two different points of view:

The first is a feeling that the pain or discipline is unjust and cruel when we do not know why it is being inflicted.

The second is a feeling of relief and a blessing if we know that what they did was for the benefit of the person affected.

The hard-working student, the obedient son and the wise man do not need such aggravation, stress or pain. God’s Purpose in instigating disasters is part of His Mercy and a mark of His Love for His Creation, therefore, all the pain, suffering and evil which one sees in this world are simply remedies for these people who are sick in their spirit. The treatment differs according to the spirit’s illness. Some are greedy for money: they need to learn self-denial, so God impoverishes them because money cannot make them good. Some like to be unjustly arrogant and they use their might to oppress others and to encroach on their freedom, even though these others deserve it. God deprives them of this and then inflicts a series of treatments on them, such as hardship, disaster and disease which distract them from the exhausting spiritual illnesses which arise from their malicious lusts and desires. Thus they will forget their lusts because of these disasters. This kind of treatment and adversity will continue until they die, and God will not deprive them of this treatment in the Hereafter.

All of the Qur’anic verses show that the cause of hardship and disaster is what has already been done at the hands of this person, along with all that is sent to them by God. God says, ‘

Evil has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, that Al’lah may make them taste a part of that which they have done, in order that they may return.

’ ﴿229﴾

And another of His Sayings is, ‘

And the Jews and the Christians say, “We are the sons of Al’lah and His loved ones.” Say, “Why then does He punish you for your sins?”

’ ﴿230﴾

Another of His Sayings (Glory to His Names) is as follows, ‘

So We punished each for his sin, of them were some on whom We sent a violent wind, others were overtaken by an awful cry, others whom We caused the earth to swallow, and others whom We drowned. It was not Al’lah Who wronged them, but they wronged themselves.

’ ﴿231﴾

These hardships are never inflicted on true believers; and they are always dealt with correctly. If anyone wants to hurt them, Al’lah will defend them. God says, ‘

Truly, Al’lah defends those who believe. Truly, Al’lah does not love any treacherous ingrate to Al’lah.

’ ﴿232﴾

If these mean-spirited people go too far in their infidelity without being able to return to God, and the disasters have no positive effect, Al’lah opens the gates of this world to them and then He suddenly takes them; then they discover that they were misled.

There are a group of people who gain no benefit from treatment because they want only to enjoy this life. So God gives them what they want from this world: He fulfils their worldly desires and they become completely engrossed in them. However, they do not encroach on the freedom of those who differ with them, and they do not oppress others. These people are masters of this world and they are granted their demands and desires here, but they have no share in the Hereafter because their greatest aim was to enjoy this world and they rejected the life to come. In the Holy Qur’an, God says, ‘

But when they forgot the warning they were reminded with, We opened to them the gates of all [good] things until in the midst of their enjoyment of Our Gifts, of a sudden, We called them to account, when lo! They discovered that they had mistaken the path of Paradise for that of Hell.

’ ﴿233﴾

And He says, ‘

Of the Bounties of your Provider; We bestow freely on all these as well as those; the Bounties of your Provider, none are deprived of.

’ ﴿234﴾

The believer may suffer from some adversities but the aim is their atonement and advancement in order that they do not turn toward the lower world. They must have done something wrong, and the evil of this misdeed has recourse against them. All people are susceptible to temptation, except God’s Prophets. If they have done nothing wrong they will suffer no harm. God wants this human being to wish for guidance and to accept it voluntarily, because there is no benefit to the human being if they are forced to do what they hate. True guidance is achieved when the human being voluntarily turns towards God, for then they see the Goodness and Justice of God and feel mercy and love flooding throughout all of existence. God says, ‘

We shall test you with something of fear and hunger, some loss in wealth, lives and the fruits [of your toil], but give glad tidings to those who patiently preserve who say when afflicted with calamity, “To God we belong and to Him we repent and return.”

’ ﴿235﴾

Kinds of Humanity

A disaster may hit the target, for these calamities are inflicted on a human being so that they will return to their Provider. They will wonder, ‘Why did God send this trouble to me?’ They will then reflect upon their actions in order to acknowledge their sins and wrongdoings; they then decide to stop doing evil, and repent. However, there is no injustice in the universe. If someone has their money stolen they must have gained this money illegitimately by fraud and cheating, or they have not followed God’s Command to give alms (

al-zakat

) and help those who are in need. If someone is killed they must also have killed someone previously, or committed evil deeds that have caused them to die in this way. And so the adulterer is driven to the adulteress, and the oppressor is driven to the oppressor. God says, ‘

The adulterer is only [fit] to marry an adulteress or an idolatress; and the adulteress is only [fit] to marry an adulterer or idolater; such behaviour is forbidden to believers.

’ ﴿236﴾

No one has control over someone who is pure and good. God says, ‘

What does Al’lah gain by your punishment, if you are grateful [in offering good acts] and yet you believe?

’ ﴿237﴾

And He says, ‘

Women of purity are for men of purity, and men of purity are for women of purity.

’ ﴿238﴾

By deeds, mankind is divided into three kinds:

The humane.

Those who do wrong to themselves and to others – ‘oppressors’ – and who act like animals to achieve their whims.

Those who do wrong to themselves and to others – worse ‘oppressors’ – and who act in a devilish manner to achieve their low and mean purposes.

Nowadays, the humane person is very rare, and there remain two types of oppressor as stated above. God alone has Good for the good man and the sinful man alike, and whoever does not realise this fact in this world will witness it in the Hereafter.

So, in fact, there is no injustice among people and since there is no injustice, there is no evil. What we consider to be evil is nothing but God’s Goodness directed towards the afflicted one, because this lesser evil will save them from an even greater evil; and this would not have happened to them if they had not done something bad. To explain it further, slicing open the abdomen of a healthy person may be a villainous act but it is beneficial for someone who suffers from a particular ailment which needs to be healed.

Seeming injustice is directed only to someone who deserves it, and the oppressor directs their oppression only to someone like them. God says, ‘

Thus We let some of the wrongdoers have power over others because of what they are wont to earn.

’ ﴿239﴾

Through that disaster, they might remember their sin, then abandon their oppressive habits and totally repent to God. Then this affliction will be drawn off from them and God the Almighty might let them have power over those who oppressed them.

This behaviour is not only limited to individuals but also applies to entire nations and peoples. Any nation which has a greater capability for faith than another one will suffer from the injustice of a more oppressive nation by God’s Order, so that it might plead to God and stop its evils, and thus return to God. God the Almighty says, ‘

Say, “He is Able to send punishment upon you from above you or from beneath your feet, or to bewilder you with dissension and make you taste the tyranny of one another.” See how We display the Revelations so that they may understand the truth.

’ ﴿240﴾

So, God changes their sins into good deeds and gives power to the oppressed over their oppressors, not for them to take revenge and attack in turn, but to make them return to the path of integrity and goodness. God says, ‘

And was it so, when a disaster smote you, though you had smitten [with a disaster] twice [as great] that you said, “How is this?” Say [unto them, Oh Mohammad], “It is from yourselves. Lo! Al’lah is Omnipotent.”

’ ﴿241﴾

God’s Ways are slow but sure. When man is disobedient punishment is apportioned to them. If they repent and change the evil inside them, God stops this chastisement. If they do not repent but choose to continue their aggression, God will send them an even greater punishment so that they might stop their evil ways and return to the path of goodness.

Here are some examples:

If a student is hard-working and performs his duties in the best possible way, does his teacher punish him? Of course not! He must be rewarded with love and generosity. Another student is lazy and does not study; he won’t succeed as he is incompetent.

The teacher might neglect him as there is no purpose in making him study. It is better to expel him as he may then develop a profession. A third is negligent sometimes and hardworking at other times. The teacher’s mercy might require punishment so as to make him work hard in order to be successful.

Let us suppose that a patient has a dangerous chronic disease and there is no hope of his recovery. Does the doctor take care of him or does he tell his family to take him away and let him eat and drink whatever he wants because he will die soon? Another question, does a doctor give medicine to a person who is strapping and healthy? Does he carry out a surgical operation on him or deprive him of delicious food and drink? Of course not! Another sick person who has a reasonable hope of recovery will be treated appropriately and given bitter medicine, and also deprived of tasty food.

These are actual examples from life to make the reality clear. In the holy words (

hadith qudsi

), God says, ‘

Oh My servants, seek Me and you shall find Me. If you find Me, you will find everything, and if you miss Me, you have missed everything; and to you, I am the most beloved of everything.

’ ﴿242﴾

And in another holy saying, ‘

Oh My servant, be for Me as I wish and I will be for you as you wish.

’ ﴿243﴾

God the Almighty wants us to act according to His Orders and so He protects us from every evil. He will always be with the person who is straight in order to support, help and protect him. God says, ‘

And Al’lah will not give the disbelievers any way [of success] against the believers.

’ ﴿244﴾

And in another verse God says, ‘

What does Al’lah gain by your punishment if you are grateful [in offering good acts] and yet you believe [in Him]?

’ ﴿245﴾

He also says, ‘

If you [do good acts] thanking Me, I will give you more [of My graceful Gifts].

’ ﴿246﴾

– In this verse, thanking means performing good deeds, as when God says, ‘

Give good deeds to thank Me, Oh House of David!

’ ﴿247﴾

If man remains distant from their Provider and denies the Graces of God, they will undoubtedly be deprived of His Bounties on the Day of Resurrection. Al’lah wants only good things for mankind, and has prepared Paradises for them. By remaining distant from their Provider, mankind deprives themself of such gifts and is unjust to themself. In addition it also appears that they wish to fulfil their lusts and vices, so God provides these too and then expels those people from this world in disgrace. Whoever chooses this lower world is granted this outcome, but they will have nothing on the Day of Resurrection. The one who mixes a good act with an evil one, whose faith is weak and who has done very few good deeds, will go to Hell, which is a wretched home.

On this earth God’s Mercy is present when these people are afflicted with disasters and trouble or are oppressed by others, in order to make them repent and return to God, since they have the ability to be good. God then stops their misery and other disasters that may overcome them when they repent and return to Him, and so they become happy during this life and in the Hereafter. God says, ‘

If only there had been a community [of all those that were destroyed of old] that believed and profited by its belief as did the folk of Jonah! When they believed, We drew off from them the torment of shame in the life of this world and gave them comfort for a while.

’ ﴿248﴾

God does not change the condition of people until they themselves change. If they change, they will find a Forgiving and Merciful God, Who will inevitably make them enjoy life in this world and in the Hereafter. God has great Compassion for mankind, although most of them fail to realise it.

Does Distress Purify the Spirit?

However, it is not the hardships which the Almighty imposes upon people that purify the spirit or perfect its noble manners, but approaching Al’lah and truly and whole-heartedly facing Him are the only ways to purify the spirit. If a person enters into their Provider’s Presence and totally directs themself towards Him, and if the Godly Light then permeates this spirit – especially when it is communicating with Al’lah – then this spirit will be purified, freed from all the contamination of immoral cravings and traces of sin. If those people who fail to remember their Provider had thought carefully, and had then sought refuge in their Creator, their spirits would have become pure. There would have been no need for distress and misfortune to overcome them – for this is what drives people to resort to Al’lah. If they had chosen to follow the straight path and willingly communicated with Him, their spirits would have been easily and gently purified, and the remedy would have been pleasant and agreeable: all this comes through communicating with their Provider and entering into His Presence. The Almighty has revealed to us the importance and value of real communication with Him and its influence on the spirit, saying, ‘

Truly, communicating with God interdicts [humanity] from committing indecency and evil.

’ ﴿249﴾

Eliminating the spores of lust from the spirit and purifying it comes about through a link that exists between the servant and their Creator, and which is expressed by the word ‘communication’.

The Almighty acquaints us with His Supreme Self, saying, ‘Al’lah’ – The Owner of the most beautiful Attributes; ‘

There is no god but He

’ – Everything is attributed to Him, the Almighty. So consider your position: if you are not happy, correct your course and Al’lah will improve your affairs. Everything is in the Hands of Al’lah and there is not even the smallest action anywhere in Creation except through Him: for example, a man’s hand cannot move nor can they speak unless He wills it. The Almighty is Just: both the powerful and the powerless are in the Hands of Al’lah and He controls everything, but He does not change people’s circumstances until they themselves change. So, change what is in your spirit and Al’lah will change your condition and make it pleasant for you. ‘

The All-Living, the All- Subsisting

’ – The Source of life and all motions. If you know for certain that your life and movements are brought into being by Al’lah you will not feel pain from anyone, instead you will understand that you have brought about your own problems.

Things happen according to your condition. The father puts pressure on his son if he misbehaves; similarly, the Provider of the worlds chastises the man in order to lead them to happiness. All that exists in the universe subsists and moves by the Hands of God, the Almighty. He manifests His Glory in the universe and ‘

No slumber nor sleep can seize Him.

’ ﴿250﴾

Seeking Refuge in God Alone Will Certainly Avail

The

Quraysh

people (from Mecca) asked the Envoy Mohammad (cpth) a similar question, for they were very surprised when this great man presented this glorious guideline about the fact that there is no god but Al’lah. He had never studied at a school or university, so where did he acquire this knowledge and wisdom which, since then, have spread all over the world and made him the spiritual father, great tutor and genius leader, who has formed the minds of the leaders and masters of this world?
