He is the man of so many wonderful attributes: the doctor who heals; the perfect social reformer; the intelligent politician; the refiner of spirits, manners and morals; the genuine sage. This man had been a simple, uneducated orphan grazing sheep in Mecca’s mountain passes but became the one who filled this worldly existence and the Afterlife with human perfection and noble acts.

Therefore, in Fortress

al-Nas

(Oblivious Mankind, Oblivious jinn-kind) his God instructed him, ‘Oh Mohammad, tell them, ‘

I proudly seek refuge in the Provider of mankind

’ – He (cpth) said to them, ‘I seek refuge in the Provider of mankind, whereas you seek refuge in Creation, and what a great difference it is! I sought refuge in Him, therefore He taught me, supported me, guided me and inspired me with something of momentous importance to be passed on to you. If the jinns and mankind united to do something similar they would fail. I take refuge in your Lord, the Provider of the oblivious (mankind), who created you and gave you the senses of hearing, vision, taste and touch, gave you the treasures and fruits of this world, took care of you while you were embryos in your mothers’ wombs, gave you every luxury and raised you perfectly.’

Then they asked him why God created one man short and another one tall, one rich and another poor, this one white and that one black, one handsome and another one ugly. God told the Envoy (cpth), ‘Say to them,

“He is The King of mankind”

’ – They are all entirely in His Hands, and He gives to each what suits them. They then asked, ‘Since God is Merciful and He is our Possessor, why does He not make us enter Paradise; and what is the purpose of Fire?’ God told him, ‘Say to them,

“He is The guiding Lord of mankind.”

’ ﴿251﴾

– He is the One Who directs them according to their own free choice, and He guides them always to what is most beneficial for them. God gives you the power to achieve your deeds which are based on your free will.

If you take heed and follow His Orders, you will be happy both here and in the Hereafter; you will receive blessings kept in store for you, far greater than those given to all other creatures. However, if you disobey, continue to do whatever you want and commit sins, He will guide you according to your personal choice and then you will be responsible for the outcome. You risk losing everything both here and in the Hereafter, and you will have chosen to taste Fire. Only then will you fully realise your spiritual torture and the pain of your eternal loss! Then how difficult the hopeless life of the Hereafter will be ….. in Hell!

In fact, people confuse Hell with Fire: they do not understand the significance of each of them, they also fail to distinguish the one from the other and therefore, they adopt false and unfair concepts about them. In turn this will lead them to accuse Almighty Al’lah of injustice and hard-heartedness. They believe wrongly that Almighty God will force disbelievers into the Fire; and worse still, that this Merciful God will put disobedient servants into Fire simply to punish them for their wrongdoings and for disobeying Him. Some of them support their claims with evidence that they claim is irrefutable, and that it is Almighty Al’lah Who has created the Fire and the angels of torment. For this reason, we consider it our duty to throw light on this topic by giving an appropriate explanation along with logical, general and Qur’anic evidence in the hope of convincing our dear readers.

chapters.title: Chapter Four, AN APPROACH TO FIRE & PARADISE
chapters.html:
The All-Merciful God Is the Creator of Fire

Most people suppose that Almighty God punishes disbelievers by putting them in His Fire according to their disobedience and for shunning Him, but the facts do not support this assumption. And so, it is far from Almighty God to treat them like that, since He is the Creator, the Grand, the All-Merciful and the Gracious One Who created man and has utilised everything in the universe to serve them. However, a creature is not equal to the Creator, the All-Merciful and the Generous, so He does not treat His Creation as One treats His equal, for His Perfection is far superior and His Mercy is far greater and far above such behaviour. To summarise: Almighty God created man and placed the love of perfection in their spirit, and gave them the ability to be superior to all other creatures. Finally, when the disbeliever dies they will see how their spirit was plunged into bitterness and detestable deeds by shunning their Creator and not performing the good deeds that they were created to do. Additionally, they will see that if they had acquired true belief in God and done these good deeds, they would have been drawn to them in order to attain nearness to Almighty God and to witness His unlimited, wondrous Beauty.

We say, if the human being sees their condition as being full of malice, error and lowliness and they realise what they have forfeited by neglecting God and how they negatively recompensed the Godly Goodness, Bounties, Benevolence and Mercifulness with meanness and ingratitude and by shunning God the Almighty, then at that moment their spirit will be full of regret, shame, misery and sadness, and the fire of regret and unspeakable shame will burn their heart. They will remain in such a sorry state until the Day of Judgement comes; then they will find no dwelling for themselves except the Fire. This is indicated by the word ‘

companions

’ in the verse, ‘

But those who disbelieve and deny Our Signs shall be the companions of the Fire, and there they will abide.

’ ﴿252﴾

They will throw themselves into the Fire and remain in painful torment in order to forget their spiritual suffering. Almighty God describes the condition of those disobedient servants and disbelievers with His Words, ‘

Lost indeed are those who deny the meeting with God until, when the Hour suddenly comes, they say, ‘Alas for us that we disregarded this!’ They will bear their burdens on their backs. How terrible those burdens will be!

’ ﴿253﴾

This loser will be overcome by terrible regret for what they have forfeited and their descent from the Paradises: facing and approaching Almighty Al’lah. All this is the result of their own previous stubbornness and poor choice in the worldly life, and makes them accept the treatment of the Fire in order to quell their terrible spiritual pains and shame.

The Almighty God created human beings, sent them to this worldly life and assigned them a great mission which they accepted freely and willingly; no other creatures accepted to fulfil this undertaking. As mentioned previously, Almighty God also offered this Trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains but, unlike mankind, they refused to accept it, but mankind held it voluntarily to their complete satisfaction. Actually, therein lies the possibility of great danger and everlasting misery if man misuses it. On the other hand it has a great aspiration and wonderful eternal happiness if man accepts to fulfil the mission.

So it is true to say that the human being may be either the best of all creatures or the very worst: they will have Paradise with all its lasting blessings and great joy or the Fire with its terrible torment as treatment for their diseased spirit and the relief of their most painful spiritual fire.

On the other hand, most creatures refused to bear the Trust, unlike humankind and the jinns, and were satisfied with a little pleasure instead of the unlimited pleasure they might have had. Instead they were content with this limited pleasure in exchange for their services to those who bore the Trust: the human being. Humans saw the appeal and attraction contained in the offer so they attached no importance to its possible failure. They chose to bear the Trust and agreed voluntarily to worship Almighty God and go forth in this life according to God’s Will and Orders. But, one wonders, is it true that they were unjust and ignorant?!

In fact they will be ignorant and unjust only to themselves if they fail to fulfil the pledge. The Trust is not there for them to separate themselves from Almighty God but to maintain a link with Him through the Prophet (cpth), and to voluntarily give Him the reins of their spirit in this world; for only then they can willingly submit to what God bids, or forbids, them to do.

Conclusion

God the Almighty gave us the freedom of choice so that all creatures will carry out every deed both voluntarily and willingly; in fact no deed will take a creature even one step closer to their Creator unless that deed is undertaken willingly through their own freedom of choice. Originally, the will of all creatures is in the possession of their Creator and is subject to His Power. Therefore, they have no volition or choice in any matter. As God wanted to give the most precious gift to the spirits, He showed them the means to acquire this gift .

He offered to make the ‘will’ – which is His – as a trust to the spirits, and made them free to follow the path leading to the achievement of the deeds resulting from their yearning. The giving of this will and freedom of choice is meant by the word ‘Trust’. In the world of

al-Azal

, the pre-material world, God offered the ‘Trust’ to all the spirits without discrimination and showed them that the shouldering of the Trust, that is to say, the freedom of choice concerning the deeds, can be a very dangerous thing. As mentioned previously, if, by their deeds, a human being can ascend to the highest rank, equally the quality of their deed might be so poor that it takes them to the lowest rank.

So, out of God’s Mercifulness for His creatures He clarified that if they accepted to bear the ‘Trust’ and come into this worldly existence, He would send them a book to serve as a light and guidance for their every act. If they become illuminated by His Light when they initiate the act due to their own yearning, if they seek His Guidance and ask Him for inspiration to be right in their action, their way will be straight, their move safe, and their act will comply with the true path shown to them in His Book. Thus, they will be protected from committing any wrongdoing and from straying from the proper path: their deeds will be the cause of their elevation. When they come to God after their death, their distinguished humanitarian acts will be the basis they rely on in their approach to God, where they gain greater closeness to Him, rising successively and persistently in the Paradises of eternal delight.

If they carry the Trust and come into existence without being guided by His Light or seeking His Guidance when they start their deeds, they will undoubtedly miss the path of righteousness which leads them to happiness and all their work will be harmful and cause damage to all creatures. When they eventually leave this world, they will face their Creator ashamed of their wrongful acts: despised because of their shameful deeds, humiliated by their ungratefulness and depravity which will force them to throw themselves into Fire. They will hope to forget the great pain of their spiritual torture which is alleviated by the pain of Fire and the torture of burning, namely: the escape from Hell to the Fire. In a prophetic saying, the Prophet (cpth) says, ‘

Man will be restricted by the sweat of shame on Doomsday that he says, “My Provider; relieve me even to Fire.”

’ And in another saying he says, ‘

Shame will adhere to man on Doomsday until he says, “Oh My Provider, your sending me to Fire is easier than what I am suffering”, although he knows the great torture in it.

’

chapters.title: Dealing with Spirits that Refused to Bear the Trust
chapters.html:
The rest of the creatures who did not have the freedom of choice, as they had refused to shoulder the Trust, act according to their instinct and perform their function in this worldly life. However if they carried out actions beyond the limits of their ‘duties’ they would be duly punished in this life but not in the Hereafter, because on Doomsday they will be rewarded with various pleasures, but at a level inferior to the various Paradises of man.

For example: it is forbidden to kill a snake in its natural habitat in the mountains or deserts, or by pulling it up from its hiding place underground, because it has several functions serving the human in this life, for example: it kills the mice which destroy the farmers’ crops, and in digging to build its underground shelter it enables fresh air and water to get to the roots of the plants. The Qur’an says, ‘

And do not kill any spirit which Al’lah has forbidden, except for a just cause.

’ ﴿254﴾

If someone killed a snake in its habitat or on uncultivated land, he would suffer great punishment from the Almighty God either in this worldly life through having various diseases and torments, or in the Hereafter where the snake will meet its killer face to face before the Almighty God, the Envoys (ptt), the angels and all people to ask him reproachfully, why did you kill it? Is it right that you should kill a creature which was created to serve you? Will the reward for good deeds be anything but good? With this he will feel instant shame and disgrace in front of all creatures. As he promised to communicate with Almighty God when he comes to this worldly life and to take a liking to Him, every creature will like his company, and that is the meaning of the truly humane man.

But if the snake exceeds the limits that were laid down for it and deviates from its function by entering a human’s house or facing him with the aim of hurting him, then the human being must kill it; if he kills it he will receive a great reward from God.

The Almighty Al’lah likes the bravery of His faithful servant even when it is a matter of killing a snake that goes beyond the bounds of its duty in this universe. The rules mentioned above apply to all animals, for example lions, wolves and hyenas. It is forbidden to follow them into the forests or wild bush in order to kill them because they have certain functions within nature in the service of the noble one: the human being.

The lions and hyenas clean the land of the stinking, germridden, decaying carcasses and should be left unhindered to carry out this task, but if they cross a human’s path then he has the right to kill them and he will be thanked and rewarded for his deed. As has been mentioned previously the aggressive animal has its punishment on earth, therefore it will not receive punishment or the Fire in the Hereafter as it had never accepted to bear the Trust. The noble Prophet (cpth) said, ‘

Whoever killed a bird in vainness, it will complain to the Almighty God on Doomsday, saying, “Oh God that person killed me in vainness, not for a beneficial thing.”

’ In another saying, ‘

A bird complained around the throne with a sound like thunder, saying, “Oh my God, ask that man why he killed me in vainness, not to be eaten.”

’ ﴿255﴾

Our freedom of choice is controlled by the power of thought. If a human being has a defect in their ability to think they will not be held responsible for their freedom of choice, nor will they be held accountable or be questioned on Doomsday. As for all the creatures that do not have the freedom of choice and the power of thought, if any one of them makes a mistake and exceeds the limits of its designated function it will be punished in this worldly life and will have a pleasurable and happy life in the Hereafter. Voluntary work can never be compared to any compulsory work whatever it may be, and so its value equals many times that of a deed carried out under obligation or for payment. It also generates more self-confidence in the spirit of the doer than any other action, especially if they seek only to satisfy Almighty God through their work and expect no reward or thanks from anyone.

If a man offers help voluntarily to their fellow human beings without asking for reward, their action will be of far greater benefit to their spirit than any paid or conditional favour. However, freedom is priceless. So when man transfers this freedom voluntarily to the One Who bestowed it upon them because they recognise His Sympathy and Mercy to them, that is to say, when they offer themselves voluntarily to be His true servants, submit to His Commands, and abandon forbidden things, their spirit then becomes confident of God’s Satisfaction with them.

So they will draw nearer to Him and their heart will drink from the flood of His Delight. In turn, this provides them with endless recompense, far greater than all that they sacrificed in the Cause of God. This is because Almighty God appreciates and thanks man for their deeds, their surrender and their adherence to His Command and Legislation, and for relinquishing their freedom of choice to choose only what Al’lah wants, in order to grant them what is good. The Almighty Al’lah said, ‘

Surely Al’lah gives the best rewards, and knows everything.

’ ﴿256﴾

When man carries out the charitable and humane deeds that Al’lah wants them to do, their spirit will become very confident of God’s Satisfaction with them. For example, when they willingly give up all those things that are forbidden, such as gazing at foreign women ﴿257﴾

or collecting money without giving alms (

zakat

), or bragging about it or spending it extravagantly on other people, and when they give up worldly pleasures or amusements in order to seek God’s Satisfaction, they will definitely attain Paradise.

Actually, the Trust means that we must be faithful to the promise we made to Almighty God before we came into this worldly life. So it is not a mystery that we are unable to remember but a promise we made to ourselves not to be separated from God, and to keep our spirits linked to Him and communicating with Him if we come into this worldly life, and to be illuminated and enlightened by His Light during our lifetime. Only then will we be able to put His Commands into effect. However, we would not be able to remember that promise if we are overly occupied with a materialistic life or with cheap yearnings. The wise person is the one who remembers and keeps that promise in mind. Prophets and Envoys (ptt) have kept their pledge, driven by misty feelings they sense but do not know their source. Yet soon they find out the reality of such feelings of the link of God when they seriously and earnestly seek to recognise something they feel but do not understand. This is the reason they become guides to all humankind. God said describing them, ‘

They are those whom Al’lah had guided, so follow their guidance.

’ ﴿258﴾

Man cannot fulfil their promise without the Prophets and Envoys (ptt) because they cut the link with Almighty God but those noble men do not; they keep their insight (third eye) facing His Beauty and Grandness, with great affection, so truthful people will support the Prophets wherever they are from or whatever nation they belong to. Almighty God says, ‘

So those who believe in him, honour him, help him and follow the light which has been sent down with him, it is they who will be successful.

’ ﴿259﴾

But, those who enclose themselves within limited borders and do not look at the truth unless it is to their own benefit, or through bigotry or blind fanaticism, are fake guides because the truth cannot be limited by place or time and man must support the truth even if it is not in their own best interest to do so.

chapters.title: What Is the Reason for Fire? How Will Sinners Enter It?
chapters.html:
We shall continue to talk about the unfamiliar subject concerning the reason why the disobedient go into the Fire on Doomsday. We shall also continue to mention the Trust which we accepted; and how we promised Almighty God before coming to this worldly life that we would keep it and shoulder it faithfully. We promised to be kind and humane with what Almighty Al’lah created and exploited for our benefit. We must not treat these creatures with prejudice, oppression, or the burden of excessive exertion, nor exceed the limits of our rights and duties with any creature even if they cause us harm or abuse us. We have the right to treat them as they treat us but it is much better to forgive them. We even have the right to get rid of harmful and dangerous insects but it is forbidden to attack them in their own habitats unless they exceed the limits of their designated functions and try to hurt us. Every creature has a function in this universe for none was created in vain, and all of them are utilised for us directly or indirectly, as we have mentioned previously.

But we surely realise that we cannot keep the Trust without God’s Help in order to attain the Godly Light which enables us to walk the straight path; otherwise we shall stumble in the darkness, turn away from the truth and follow our own desires while thinking that we are doing good work. Actually, if we do not fulfil and keep the Trust in our words and actions we cannot draw nearer to Almighty God. However, a human being might lie to or cheat others, but not themselves. God the Almighty said, ‘

Yet, a human is an eye-witness against himself, even though he puts forth his excuses.

’ ﴿260﴾

The spirit would not be able to attain the link with the Almighty God or draw nearer to Him unless it was confident of its deeds, but its bad deed would become like a veil between them and Him. God said, ‘

No indeed! Their hearts are encrusted with what they have acquired.

’ ﴿261﴾

A human can hide their errors and sins from all creatures except Almighty God because He is the All-Knowing. Therefore, how will they face the One who treats them with all kinds of Charity and Benevolence when no secrets will remain hidden from Al’lah? Whatever level of moral courage or spiritual ability a human being has, they would not be able to come face to face with the one who did good deeds for them while they had previously done bad deeds to them. The same thing applies to the situation on Doomsday, when man will witness how Almighty Al’lah has never failed to overwhelm them with His Kindness, Benevolence and Bounty and how they have reacted wrongly to that and repaid charity and favour with ingratitude and abuse. They will certainly lower their head in shame and disgrace. ‘

[Prophet], if only you could see the wrongdoers hang their heads before their Provider, “Our Provider, now that we have seen and heard, send us back and we shall do good. [Now] we are convinced [believe with certainty].”

’ ﴿262﴾

On Doomsday they will become certain that entering Paradise requires honourable deeds, and their deeds in the worldly life were full of cheating, lies, malice, deception, and whatever deeds appeared to be good and charitable were simply for gaining worldly benefits rather than attaining God’s Satisfaction. God said, when revealing their situation on the Other Day, that is, Doomsday, ‘

You [Prophet] will see them exposed to it [Fire], abject in humiliation, glancing furtively, while those who believed exclaim, “The losers are the ones who have lost themselves and their people on the Day of Resurrection.” Truly, the evil-doers will remain in lasting torment.

’ ﴿263﴾

Almighty God granted us nourishment in our mothers’ wombs. Then He provided us with nutritious milk through their breasts. Moreover, He put mercy in their hearts when they became too tired to take care of us so that we would enjoy the pleasure of life. They had sleepless nights when we were ill, and made sure that their children were fed before they were. In fact that mercy which they shower upon us is not their own mercy but it is the Mercy of the Almighty God Who has placed it within their hearts. For the times we are tired He has prepared a quiet and peaceful night for us that we may feel rested and tranquil, and He removes our freedom of choice (by sleeping) to rest our bodies from the exertion of the day. Then He gives it back to us in the morning so that we may have His Benevolence and Graces by doing good deeds. He utilises everything in the universe such as animals, plants and all sorts of materials to serve us. Is that treatment not clear evidence of His Mercy, Love and Sympathy toward us? And after all that Divine Kindness, how could we meet the Provider of the worlds if we repaid His Charity and Favour with denial and abuse, and good with bad?!

Then, what is our pretext if we think that He is oppressive, unjust and unmerciful even though Al’lah is far beyond all that? How could we draw nearer to Him if we wronged His creatures that He loves and utilises to serve us for our benefit? How could people deny all these bounties with which He overwhelms them at every moment?! How can they fail to believe despite His clear and evident Signs? And would they forget all His Benevolence if something repulsive happened to them?! But if only they knew that even that misfortune is actually a kindness for them, because it comes to awaken them from their negligence and drive away their shunning of God, though it is, above all, a result of their bad actions; moreover by means of it God the Almighty distracts them from many of their mean desires.

On Judgement Day, when the human sees that they have forfeited Paradise with all its benefits of seeing the beautiful Face of Almighty God and lost the lofty rank that they were nominated to have, they will join the lowest ranked of all creatures: it will be an immeasurable loss, far worse than one might imagine, for they will have forfeited their ‘lofty rank’ for meagre pleasure during their relatively short time spent in this worldly life. Therefore they will be burdened by great regret and sorrow for wasting that time and will come to meet Almighty God with a dirty cloth holding snakes and scorpions, that is, bad deeds instead of valuable gifts such as helping His servants, or leading them out from darkness to the Godly Light and the straight path. This would have made their face pure and blameless and caused them to draw nearer to Almighty God. And by means of their closeness to Him they would attain real lasting delight, happiness and lofty Paradises. They would see instead that they lost all that, see how they took the shells and discarded the pearls and kept the waste instead of the jewels. Then they may well gnash their teeth but it will be too late, the results of the test have been issued and everything is over. It is indeed a time of extreme sadness and regret, when their heart will be eaten up with remorse. It is all over and they have no-one to blame but themselves; there is no hope for them, how difficult it is to live without hope!

The disbelievers lost their families and friends. They would be withdrawn from their companions and other people around them as they tried to hide their depravities and their mantle of vice. They lost their spirits and deprived themselves of the delights kept in store for them and the attainment of their elevated rank. As the noble verse stated in God’s Words, ‘

So worship what you like beside Him. Say, “The losers are those who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Verily, that will be a manifest loss!”

’ ﴿264﴾

These are the people who lose everything, even their hope, and what can make them forget the terrible condition they suffer except the Fire? Therefore, through His Mercy and in order not to leave them suffering this misery, pain and disgrace, God will apply the Fire in accordance with what will make them forget their severe spiritual pain. However, every human will suffer torment to a degree equivalent to their level of disbelief and denial of God, in order to relieve them and alleviate their inner spiritual torment. God mentioned these two kinds of suffering in the Qur’an several times. He said, ‘

For those who tempt the believing men and the believing women and then do not repent, there will be the torment of Hell [inner regret fire] and then the torment of burning [in God’s Fire].

’ ﴿265﴾

chapters.title: Hell and Fire
chapters.html:
Therefore, in order for them to escape from the torture of Hell, that is, the horrible spiritual pain of regret and remorse that will assail them when they realise their total and deadly loss and the betrayal of their pledge, Al’lah the Almighty will soon divert them to another type of suffering, the burning of Fire, which will be less and lighter than their unspeakable and infernal pain. This is indicated in the holy verse when God said, ‘

On a Day when they will be captivated by the Fire, “Taste your captivation! This is what you used to ask to be hastened.”

’ ﴿266﴾

They will be obsessed with the Fire just as a patient is absorbed by the medicines that relieve his illness and pain. Our Prophet, Mohammad (cpth) said in his tradition, ‘

Shame will adhere to man on Doomsday until they say, “Oh! My Provider, your sending me to Fire is easier than what I am suffering,” although they know the great torture in it.

’ The Almighty God says, ‘

These are the ones who buy error in place of guidance, and torment in place of forgiveness. Ah, what makes them patient in the face of the Fire?

’ ﴿267﴾

In another verse God said describing their approval of treatment in Fire, ‘

The close of their request [the two parties; the people of Paradise and the people of Fire] will be, “All praise is to God, the Provider of the worlds.”

’ ﴿268﴾

They will say this because this treatment is the most suitable cure for the terrible spiritual condition of the disbelievers.

According to what Al’lah’s Envoy has revealed in his noble saying, mentioned previously, Fire can be compared to a hospital for the suffering wrongdoers who request it voluntarily in order to alleviate their severe spiritual pain: for the Merciful God will never force them to dwell in it. The Almighty Al’lah says, ‘

They will say, “Ah, would that I had put forward [goodness] for my life [that was to come]!” However, on that Day their torture will not be inflicted upon them by anyone [other than themselves]; nor will any bind their bonds upon them.

’ ﴿269﴾

The following is a more detailed explanation of the verses mentioned above, ‘

They will say, “Ah, would that I had put forward [goodness] for my life [that was to come]!”

’ – The poor man saying these words has lost the chance of their life, wasted their valuable years and gained nothing. Their time for gaining blessings, drawing nearer to the Creator of all beings and acquiring honour and high rank is over. There will be nothing to be gained from sorrow and regret. They will then feel great remorse and will repent: they will suffer such grief that their heart will break with sorrow. They will understand that the only real life is the life of the Other World. Alas they will have lost their opportunity, and done nothing to allow themselves to enjoy it. ‘

However, on that Day their torture will not be inflicted upon them by anyone [other than themselves].

’ – That is, on that Day noone will inflict this torture on them, it is they who will inflict it upon themselves. They have only themselves to blame for whatever happens to them. Their self-reproach and shame and their evil deeds which will appear before their eyes will strike them hard in the depths of their spirit and cause them unbearable agony; therefore they will rush to Fire and throw themselves into it, wanting the pain of its torturous burning to help them to conceal and forget their spiritual pains.

The situation of this human on that Day is like that of a child whose father warned it against touching a sharp blade. The child did not follow its father’s guidance but tried to sharpen its pencil with the sharp blade, thinking that it would be better than the pencil sharpener which its father had advised it to use. Needless to say, the child cut its finger and began to cry and call its father for help, asking him to bandage the wound and relieve the pain. This example leads us to wonder, was anyone else responsible for this child’s suffering at that moment? Of course not! Nobody caused that pain but the child itself. Sterilising the wound and dressing it would also cause pain to the child, but this was only done for the purpose of cure and healing.

This simple example clarifies the truth in our minds, although the truth is far deeper than this. Anyone who disobeys God and His Envoy (cpth) strays far away indeed and thus incurs a great loss. The Almighty wanted to describe the state of such a wretched and miserable man in some detail. He says, ‘

Nor will any bind their bonds upon them

’ – That is, on that Day no-one will confine that poor, unfortunate human to the Fire for they will remain there voluntarily. They will put up with the pain of burning and force themselves to bear their torment in order to escape and forget their internal spiritual suffering.

This is a clear description of the state of the disobedient when they are in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. So the only way for man to be saved from this infernal situation is their instant repentance and returning to walk the straight path before it is too late. Otherwise they will be absorbed and beguiled by the Fire due to its alleviation of the suffering caused by their intolerable spiritual pains. This can be compared to the patient who is keen to take a bitter medicine for the relief it brings, and the same is true for sedatives or surgical operations in the hope of relief from their great pain and illness. God said in this respect, ‘

On a Day when they will be captivated by the Fire.

’ ﴿270﴾

They will certainly know that the Fire is the most suitable thing for their situation and so they have to dwell in it. Almighty God confirmed that they will go to the Fire of their own volition. He said, ‘

They are the companions of the Fire, they themselves will abide therein forever.

’ ﴿271﴾

They will submit to the cure and furthermore they will remain in the Fire for the benefits it brings by relieving them. The word ‘

companions

’ confirms that sense. However, we seek refuge in Almighty God from the evils of our spirits, so that we shall not have the urgent need of the company of the Fire.

So, the terrible spiritual fire of the disbelievers’ inner regret, shame and disgrace will burn their hearts, and then they will find no better treatment than the Fire to treat their spiritual illness and relieve their severe spiritual fire. Moreover, they themselves will dwell in it seeking its relief, and God certainly does no wrong to them, but they themselves do wrong and bring injustice to their spirits. This sense will become clear and obvious to us if we take a look at the condition of a human being now in their worldly life. If they develop a painful condition in one of their organs and realise that there is no cure except by surgical intervention, they will surely go to a doctor and place themself in his hands, asking for help and relief even if a limb requires surgical amputation and they know that it will be extremely painful after the operation.

If that is their state in the worldly life, what will their condition be in the Hereafter when their spirit will be free from its yearnings? Their spirit will return to its pure nature of perfection and awaken as though from a deep sleep. They will immediately remember their pledge and how they have broken it. They will soon realise how God has treated them fairly and with endless benevolence throughout every moment of their life. And then they will see their great forfeiture of the Paradises and how low they became after losing their high rank in accepting the Trust, while the mountains, earth and heavens were afraid to accept it. Indeed, initially they accepted to bear it so as to rise above all creatures and become superior to them but they changed their mind, turned to their yearnings and so fell to the lowest level whereby they lost every iota of hope to recompense or repair their loss. No one can live without hope, for what a hard and miserable life it would be to become hopeless and helpless! Moreover, due to their disgrace and shame, they missed their opportunity to witness the beautiful Face of Almighty God Who is the Spring of Favour, Goodness, Beauty and Perfection. They will then be overcome by regret and burnt by their low and disgraceful deeds. Finally they will be overwhelmed by shame, self-reproach and sorrow.

Doubtless, this human being will throw themself into the Fire which will burn away their skin and scald their face, and they will be given boiling water to drink that tears at their guts. Nevertheless, they will still prefer to suffer all this rather than their unbearable spiritual pains.

Oh God of all: all praise is given to You in good times and bad, and all praise is to You in times of good fortune and misfortune. You created the human being for them to bask in happiness and the delight of witnessing the Grandeur of Your Noble Face and to rise up through the Paradises of bliss; but they shunned that and distracted themselves by deviating to the low worldly life to arrive at the worst position. However, if they return to You in the Hereafter wearing a disgraceful garment stained with base evil deeds, You will not abandon them to burn within themselves, nor will You deliver them to their spiritual pain and sorrow. But rather You will have mercy upon them and guide them to the Fire to make them forget their disgrace, shame and the flame of their interior spiritual fire which is infinitely worse than the flame of burning Fire. It is true that all praise is to You in the first life and the Last Life, and in every circumstance. God depicted, in a few words, the condition of the two parties in Paradise and in Fire, ‘

The close of their request [the two parties; the people of Paradise and the people of Fire] will be, “All praise is to God, the Provider of the worlds.”

’ ﴿272﴾

chapters.title: The Reality of Paradise
chapters.html:
We now know the state of the evildoer on Doomsday, the reality of how they will seek out Fire and throw themselves into it, and the fact that Fire is like a hospital where those suffering from spiritual diseases and bad deeds will receive proper treatment for their severe spiritual pains. Therefore we must move on from this topic to another important subject: ‘Paradise’.

What is this Paradise which the Compassionate God has promised to His servants?

The Concept of Paradise

The word ‘Paradise’ does not only indicate materialistic pleasure, nor is a human’s joy confined to enjoyment of that wonderful place that contains so much natural beauty such as an abundance of exquisite flowers, verdant trees full of delicate blossom providing restful shade, gently flowing rivers and fruits of every variety. However, these things and other similar physical things will not make any place into a paradise unless a human being also enjoys a level of spiritual happiness and profound delight. And so, even if a man lives in a charming place with various kinds of tangible pleasures, they will never be really happy unless they experience spiritual happiness within their heart; only then will they feel that they are truly happy and they will understand that they are in a real paradise.

To clarify further we give the following example: let us suppose that there are two students living in a most appealing place, the like of which the eye has never seen before. While they are sitting there, one of them is given the good news of his success in his last exam and being granted a decree that will lead to a high position in a new job. On the other hand, it is also the day of the other student’s exam, and the transport which will take him to the exam venue is late. I wonder! Is his inner state like that of the first student? Certainly not! For the first student will feel as though he is in paradise because of his intense inner happiness and pleasure, whereas for the second student it will be like hell because of the waves of worry and confusion attacking his heart.

The Real Sense of Paradise

The word ‘Paradise’ in Arabic means

jan’nah

which is derived from the word

jan’na

, meaning to cover and conceal something. Accordingly

jan’nah

expresses the status of graceful inner feelings of spiritual happiness and pleasure concealed from other people; it is only the owner of these pleasing sensations who feels and enjoys them, and no one else can be aware of them. This is referred to in the noble prophetic saying, ‘

If you pass by the gardens of Paradise then stay and enjoy them.’ His companions asked the Prophet, “What are the gardens of Paradise?” He replied, ‘The assemblies in which the Almighty Al’lah is truly mentioned [knowledge about God].

’ And in another prophetic saying he (cpth) said, ‘

The space between my tomb and my pulpit transmits one of the gardens of Paradise, and my pulpit is on my basin [cistern].

’ ﴿273﴾

You see, the Prophet (cpth) indicated the place between his holy tomb and pulpit as one of the gardens of Paradise. This is due to the inner Divine sublime pleasure that the believer finds in their heart as a result of the established link attaching the spirit of the believer who sits there to the spirit of the noble Prophet (cpth). So, through this noble company with the Prophet they draw closer to Almighty Al’lah and experience that high spiritual pleasure and real heart life near to Him. It is the same state that a human will experience when attending the assemblies wherein knowledge about God is given. Therefore, in the Hereafter, you will find the believer in Paradise because of the great spiritual delight they enjoy by drawing closer to their Creator. They will be found moving endlessly in the ranks of Godly closeness and Paradises from one state of bliss to another that is even higher and more wonderful, according to their nearness to Almighty God. As Godly Perfection is unlimited and without end, so Paradise and the joy of those who dwell therein also have no limit or end. In addition, the spiritual enjoyment is accompanied by the material pleasure of whatever the spirits desire and are attracted to: such as exotic fruits and foods, and beautiful gardens, and flowing rivers full of blessings. This physical pleasure will increase endlessly according to the inner spiritual pleasure: one by one and moment by moment. This is referred to in God’s holy Saying, ‘

Whenever they are given a provision from a fruit in these Gardens, they say, “This is what we were provided with before,” for they will be given this provision in resemblance [to what was given to them in the world].

’ ﴿274﴾

As mentioned above, although the fruits still have the same shape and colour and flavour, the believer will find

ever increasing

enjoyment through their pleasing appearance and delicious taste; and God’s Favour is limitless and endless. How happy the people of Paradise will be! Glory to Him the Almighty! What a Generous Granter He is!

Having introduced the subject of ‘Paradise’, we shall relate the following from the story of our Master, Adam (cpth): Almighty God ordered our Master, Adam (cpth) to live with his wife in Paradise, enjoying being close to God and witnessing His Perfection and Beauty; and, what is more, He ordered them to eat whatever they wanted from there. But what is the reality of this eating? And how do the dwellers of Paradise eat from it? It is necessary to shed light upon the state of people in Paradise and how they enjoy themselves there. This is important in order to acquaint humanity with the limitless Favour of Al’lah the Almighty, so they will recognise His great Graces.

chapters.title: Man’s Components – A Further Statement
chapters.html:
As previously mentioned every person is composed of a spirit, a soul and a physical body. We have explained that the spirit is the main element of a person for it is the subtle consciousness of man. It is a Godly Light and its centre is in the chest. Its rays spread to all parts of the body through the nerves. This spirit, confined to the body, is aware of its surroundings through the five senses. It sees with the eye, hears with the ear, smells with the nose, feels and touches with the skin and tastes flavours with the tongue, which is also used for speaking in order to express ideas and thoughts. To emphasise this we say that if one stands by the sea shore, through contemplating the endless motion of the sea, their awareness will lead them to revere and glorify it. This submission and glorification come from the ‘spirit’. If we see someone dear to us whose hand is bleeding because it is wounded, we feel sorry for them and sympathise with them. This pain and grief also come from the ‘spirit’. If we hear that we have passed an exam or achieved something important to us, we feel pleased and happy to know this. These feelings of pleasure and happiness are possible because of the ‘spirit’. Thus, the spirit is the essential component of man. It glorifies and submits, grieves, annoys, delights, rejoices, feels contentment and anger, tastes, enjoys and suffers. It is the centre of our existence.

The soul is a Godly Light whose rays flow through the body carried by the blood in order to supply it with heat and life and help it grow. The soul ensures the movements of the body and the continuity of its existence and life. If this supply with Godly Light is stopped the body will become motionless and die. We see, therefore, that the soul and the spirit differ from each other, but the body and the soul work as servants to the spirit to help it perform its deeds. However, in this earthly world the spirit is confined within, and surrounded by, the body. It perceives only pictures or ‘images’, and enjoys pleasure by means of the physical senses, so the spirit does not enjoy things directly but from behind the veil of the body. This is not the situation in the life to come. In the other abode the spirit will envelop the body and surround it on all sides, as the flame of a candle completely surrounds its wick.

If we suppose that the wick of a candle is a body, then its flame and its light would be the spirit, however, after death we will experience the same state we did when we were only spirits before our existence in this life, we will go back to the same situation which our father Adam (pth) was in before his physical eating, as Almighty God says, ‘

As He brought you in the beginning, so shall you be brought into being.

’ ﴿275﴾

In the Afterlife, the state of man’s spirit will differ from the one in the worldly life: it will not see with the physical eye or hear with the physical ear. The entire spirit will be eyes and ears, and it will taste, smell and speak with its entire self, without using any organ: its taste will be intense, its witnessing vast and its bliss perfect. That will be the state of the spirit on that Day. It will get far more pleasure there than it does here for its earthly enjoyment is only partial because it is veiled. However on that Day it will be complete and direct. Just as a human feels hungry in the worldly life then derives pleasure in eating food and feels satisfied after eating a limited quantity, in Paradise, however, they will not need to allay their physical hunger pangs and will be able to constantly eat and drink as much as they want through the limitless ability of the spirit. Every pleasure and delight are without limits and endless in Paradise which is indicated through this holy verse where Almighty God says, ‘

In the Garden you will never go hungry, feel naked, be thirsty, or suffer the heat of the sun.

’ ﴿276﴾

In the life to come when the spirit wants to look at something, it will not need eyes, just as it will not need a mouth or teeth to eat food. Its rays will flow to food and allow it to taste it and enjoy its flavours with no need to chew or swallow it. In such a case, one might consider that the entire spirit consists of tongues, so, it is able to taste continuously and enjoy increasing bliss without feeling heavy or uncomfortable or bored. Thus, its enjoyment is constantly increasing without being aggravated by anything; its joy there will be completely different and far greater than in this world. In this world people soon satisfy their appetites, whereas in the life to come nothing will restrict the spirit from enjoying and taking continuous pleasure in anything it wishes. God says, ‘

This is a picture of the Garden which the pious [who see by God’s Light] have been promised: the rivers [of blessings] are running underneath it: eternal are its fruits, and so is its Shade [the Godly Manifestation].

’ ﴿277﴾

As mentioned previously, the spirits are confined to the bodies in the worldly life therefore we see and feel everything around us through the five senses: the eyes, the ears, the nose, the mouth and touch. However the spirit does not feel, see and taste directly but from behind a veil, that is, the body. But in the Hereafter it will be the opposite for the spirit will be outside the body and surrounding it. The believer’s spirit will become beautiful as it is overwhelmed by the Godly Light according to its good deeds and high rank; as the beauty appears in its reality, it is the beauty of the spirit itself and not of that physical body. As the spirit in Paradise becomes free from the obstructions of its body which was confining it in the worldly life it does not become confined by time or place in the Hereafter. God said, ‘

And their garments therein [in Paradise] will be of silk.

’ ﴿278﴾ ﴿279﴾

When a human being sleeps at night their spirit becomes free from that recumbent body: it comes and goes, loves or hates, may be afraid, or possibly speaks. While they are sleeping they may see themself in one place and then in another without any link between them, even in time or place. This happens because their spirit is free from the control of the process of thought because this stops functioning during sleep, so they are aware only of what their spirit sees and the place where it is. In the Hereafter there is no need to think so this process will be disabled, but the mind will remain since it is one of the features of the spirit, as the spirit is the conscious, undying essence of the human being: so whatever it gives its full attention to in the worldly life, whether good or bad, will be stained with it forever.

Therefore, the spirit will be in one of two states: either a state of great happiness through what it has realised and paid attention to in this life and thereby has an enlightened face and continuous Divine Lights with unlimited Graces; or it will be ashamed because of its realisation and therefore its face will be dark and it will be unable to receive the blissful Divine Manifestation which helps in seeing the truth and realities. The heart of this sceptical human being will be blind because in the Hereafter there are no material appearances, but only realities which can be seen only through Godly Light. Almighty God says, ‘

And whosoever is blind in this world, he will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray from the path.

’ ﴿280﴾

However all creatures will leave their material functions and return to their abstract spirits; the Almighty God says, ‘

On the Day when the earth will be changed to another earth and so will be the heavens, and they [all the Creations] will appear before Al’lah, the One, the Irresistible.

’ ﴿281﴾

In Paradise everything, such as those things mentioned in the Holy Qur’an, will differ from the things that we see in this life: they will have the same realities but they will be more beautiful, more appealing and more sublime. It would be no wonder if the human being becomes blind in the Hereafter because in their mortal life their heart was blind and they could not see the realities of things through the Godly Light. Their spirit did not understand or pay proper attention to any reality, and they saw nothing but the images of things. Furthermore they could not realise the essence of their realities, and in the Hereafter all things will return to their realities. But at that time they will no longer be able to see them because they were not illuminated by a Godly Light in the worldly life and they were veiled by their yearnings. The Almighty Al’lah says, ‘

And he for whom Al’lah has not appointed light, for him there is no light.

’ ﴿282﴾

This light would have guided them in the worldly life if they had acquired it, but as they have lost it they are truly blind because they see nothing in this life except the passing pleasure of their yearnings and the frippery of this temporal worldly life, and have failed to be illuminated by the company of the Prophet (cpth). Almighty God said, ‘

Verily, it is not the eyes that grow blind, but it is the hearts that are in the chests that grow blind.

’ ﴿283﴾

chapters.title: Chapter Five, A GLIMPSE AND A DEFINITION
chapters.html:
You may wonder, as do I, and as do people everywhere: how could this great scholar have gained access to such truth, when all of the earlier scholars and the great guides and imams failed to do the like? I would reply to you: a person has nothing except what they strive for. Indeed, people are differentiated through their actions.

This is true even for the Envoys and noble Prophets... and there will be a different level for everyone according to what they do. Our own great scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho was given knowledge by Al’lah, and he was distinguished by his high deeds and his great and humane sacrifices. Al’lah did not grant him anything unless it was in accordance with what he deserved. God says, ‘

And We sent down it deservedly, and with righteousness it came down.

’ ﴿284﴾

chapters.title: A Glimpse into the Life of the Eminent Scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho (His soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) His Honourable Birth
chapters.html:
A splendid full moon appeared over Damascus on a blessed night in 1890 when a baby son was born to a Damascene merchant and his wife… surely a portent of good news! The father loved his son very much because of his admirable and bright companionship, and because, for him, he resembled the full moon in all its heavenly beauty.

All during his young years, the son was an active, clever, and lively child; and his constant cheerfulness and joy radiated out to all those around him, creating a great sense of well-being in them too. Day by day he grew bigger and stronger, and showed an ever increasing level of intelligence and strength of personality, which led his devoted parents to become ever more deeply attached to him. They adored the child and cared for him with great love, affection and understanding. Sadly, however, his loving father died at a young age after suffering an exhausting and painful illness.

The entire family was greatly affected by the death of their husband and father, for he left behind a widow and two sons to grieve his passing. He was also sorely missed by his friends and colleagues for he was a good and honest man. The child, Mohammad Amin was not yet seven years of age when he took on the responsibility of protecting his mother and defending her against the difficulties which surrounded his family after the death of his father, and the departure of his brother

Saleem

to Turkey.

Even as the only child Mohammad Amin was distinguished for his serenity when faced with the many problems of life. Patiently he bore difficulties that powerful men might never have been able to deal with, because he was a member of a small, respectable family that had faced much adversity.

A Distinguished Young Man and a Glimpse at His Deeds

Because of his honourable lineage that is linked directly to the great Envoy ﴿285﴾

(cpth) he had direct access to the hierarchy of the ruling Turkish state of the time, which entitled his family to reside in

Sarouja

Quarter, known as ‘Little Istanbul,’ a residential quarter reserved then for Turkish statesmen. This connection also enabled him to study at

Amber

, the Royal Ottoman Faculty for police officers in Damascus.

Mohammad Amin completed his studies when he was eighteen years old and graduated with the rank of police officer. He was far superior to his colleagues insomuch as he displayed extreme courage, trust and integrity; also his perseverance and dedication to hard work led to distinction. Succesively, he became the commanding officer of many of the police stations in various districts of Damascus, thus eliminating the criminal and political chaos rampant in the city at that time. Thereafter he was appointed as the chief of police in a succession of small towns away from the capital city, where, yet again he established law and order in his unfailing way. In recognition of his professional ability and success he was eventually appointed to the position of director of the citadel of Damascus where the central prison was located. He was a great example to all, for no sooner had he taken up each new position than peace and safety prevailed throughout the entire area under his administration.

By day and by night he was constantly alert and prepared to protect and defend his country.

Whenever the state was confronted by any lawlessness or atrocity, his assistance would be requested. When all manner of evil such as killing, corruption and criminality spread across a region, he was their hope, their saviour, the man they could always rely on to resolve a dangerous situation and liberate people from oppression.

When decay began to nibble at the body of the Turkish state, and the light of Islam was dimmed, corruption and chaos prevailed all over the country to the extent that the level of crime became overwhelming; life became difficult, the daytime was fraught with danger, and the darkness of the night covered many horrific crimes; except in Damascus! Damascus, its suburbs and surrounding countryside, was a haven of calm and safety under the ever watchful eye of the eminent officer Mohammad Amin, whose life was dedicated to peace.

In his work he dauntlessly faced numerous criminals, showing superior courage and audacity, besieging many guerrillas and arresting their leaders. All of the tasks he undertook in the line of duty culminated in success and further support and he was given the nickname Aslan, meaning ‘the Lion,’ for his fearlessness in facing adversity. With the Help of God, he was the only officer possessing the courage to confront injustice and terrorism. Fearing his bravery, criminals would surrender to him, and beg for his mercy and compassion.

He rose through the ranks and was moved from one police station to another until eventually he was appointed director of the citadel of Damascus, which contained the city’s warehouses and prisons. He held this position for many years during which he achieved great distinction and demonstrated a level of bravery, the like of which Damascus had never seen before. He took audacious measures when, during the First World War, he freed thousands of soldiers facing the death sentence because of their flight from fighting in this war and put them in the army front lines to defend the country against the invading enemy. This singular decision was the reason that all gallows throughout the country could be demolished. These gallows had originally been constructed on the orders of

Djemal

Pasha

, the Ottoman governor of Syria, known as ‘the Butcher’ for his brutal acts. They were placed prominently in marketplaces and neighbourhoods across the country and were used, rightly or wrongly, to snuff out the lives of hundreds of young men every day. For that reason he was frequently exposed to the threat of death. Thus, by His Greatness, His Mercy, and His Assistance, Al’lah saved Mohammad Amin by enabling him to have this innovative idea.

During the French mandate of Syria 1920-1946, as he was a trusted civil security officer, he was returned to his former position as the director of a district or the chief of a police station, until the great Syrian revolution took place. At this time, due to his love for God and his noble wish to serve his country, he became the incomparable driving force of the revolutionaries and the life blood of the revolution. In recognition of his sincerity and commitment to their cause the revolutionaries put the seal ring into his trustworthy hands. He unnerved the French forces with the astounding tactics that he employed to turn retreat into victory. The French forces were further infuriated when he showed his sympathy to the revolutionaries and arranged, to the benefit of the revolutionaries, the greatest arms transfer between France and Greater Syria.

At that time the French had appointed him to the prestigious position of director of

Anjar

Castle (in Lebanon) where they had stored a great amount of arms. One dark night, Officer Sheikho handed over these arms to the revolutionaries. General Catroux, the governor of Syria at that time, was totally enraged and ordered that Mohammad Amin be executed, but the Almighty God saved him and his adjutant through His Complete Words, and the French came to trust and respect him again despite their original error of judgement.

Guidance and Invitation to Al’lah

When Mohammad was forty years old, God revealed to him vast knowledge of all things, that is, His Omniscience.

He began to envision and to hear the Prophet’s (cpth) recitation of

al-Fatiha

(the Opening) Fortress ﴿286﴾

while he was praying to God. After that he started to guide his disciples, undertaking this great task with unparalleled strength and great worthiness.

He used to be called ‘

Emin Bey

’ for ‘

Bey’

is a Turkish word meaning ‘the pure’. His salon attracted the flower of the youth of Syria, Lebanon, and Iraq, who came asking to bathe in his Mohammadan well of wisdom. Here they found a rich, dignified and generous spiritual sanctuary.

‘It is sufficient that your noble deeds are mentioned,

For us to know that you are the shining example to all of us.’

A Glimpse of Mohammad Amin’s Invitation to Al’lah - His Revelation

Mohammad Amin’s blessed gatherings were distinguished by his captivating and unique revelations which he explained perfectly with plain and realistic meanings. His words flew like an arrow that always hit the target and fell peacefully on the hearts of the listeners, and was like a light that charmed them into allowing their spirits to soar higher and higher.

He drove away darkness, ripped apart all contradiction, and finally obliterated the schools of intrigue and empty debate which created a mental chasm between the people and their God. He made them aware of the Reality of God, and the consummation of His Qualities: a Merciful God, Compassionate, Wise, Fair, Conferrer of benefit, Giver, and that He deserved to be worshipped for Himself for He is the Owner of Beauty and Consummation. He should be praised even if a man suffers something harmful because this harm results in a cure and assistance from God. Al’lah has no need of any part of creation nor of man’s allegiance and obedience, because He is Rich and we are poor; our obedience to Him is solely for our own good and benefit. We need to enter His Presence through prayer and good deeds in order to enter the shining stronghold of faith, and to be protected from misfortune and adversity.

The history of Mohammad Amin’s acclaimed life is full of meaning and is a perfect structure for the wonderful revelation that he brought: a revelation which contained facts at which heads bowed in great respect. The reality of his life was like a light: his own behaviour was proof and his true practical application of God’s Word was a guide. His revelation was without equal in world civilisations and the positive laws of contemporary life.

Why are we created?

What is this universe for?

What is the use of religious rituals?

What is the reason for fasting, followed by eating in Ramadan?

What does prayer achieve? And what are its benefits?

Why go on pilgrimage to a dry and barren desert?

Why were we brought into existence?

Where were we before coming to this earth?

What is death for? And what really comes after it?

What is the spirit? What is the soul?

What is the mind?

What is Paradise?

What is Hell?

What about the question of fate?

What is the pre-material world (the world of spirits)?

People have not allowed themselves to ask these questions because they were taken up with the temptations and deceptions of this human world, and they forgot to search in the files of existence to discover the secrets it holds.

In one of his meetings with other Western scientists, the famous English scientist, Sir John Bennett, a contemporary of Mohammad Amin, said, ‘Indeed, all the scientific knowledge that we have obtained do not equal the sea of scientific understanding of that great scholar in the Orient.’

His invitation to follow God’s Path is based on a course of action that never fails, ‘

Say, “This is my way: I, and whoever follows me, invite you to Al’lah with certainty, for Al’lah is Glorified and Exalted. And I am not one of those who worship many gods.

”’ ﴿287﴾

After Mohammad Amin received such a message through this honorable ayah (verse), he began to ask for God’s Guidance for all mankind and continued to do so for a period lasting more than thirty years, concentrating on the following points:

Acquainting people with the absolute Perfection of the Almighty God, and demonstrating His Mercy to His obedient and disobedient people; and His Justice towards His creation.

He discredited all the bad thoughts about God that remained in the minds of humans, and whatever else that acted against Godly Justice, Clemency, Mercy, and all Godly Perfection.

In this point Mohammad Amin Sheikho was guided by the Word of God, ‘

And all the most Beautiful Names [Attributes] belong to Al’lah, so call on Him by these Names, and do not keep company with those who deny His Names. They will be paid back for what they have done.

’ ﴿288﴾

Revealing the perfection of the Envoys (ptt), whose purity and flawless spirits God guaranteed in His Glorious Book (the Qur’an), and He made them the ultimate role models and guides for all the worlds ﴿289﴾

as mentioned in Mohammad Amin’s book,

Impeccability of Prophets

, the like of which could only have come through God and could never have been written by his predecessors. He refuted all falsehood or interpretation that disagreed with the Envoys’ (ptt) high spiritual worth and their flawless adherence to the Word of God, ‘

They are the ones who are guided by Al’lah, so follow their guidance.

’ ﴿290﴾

Calling people to strictly adhere to the high principles and directions of the Godly Statute and to attain the true devotion to God (as witnessed by Al’lah’s Light), besides warning people not to let their spirits follow their capricious whims, nor to depend upon worthless wishes but turn to the Word of God, ‘

It will not be as you hope nor as the people of Scripture do [Jews, Christians]: whoever does wrong will be held accountable for it and will find no guardian or helper for himself besides Al’lah.

’ ﴿291﴾

And also calling on the tradition of the Envoy (cpth), ‘

The discerning person is one who knows his own faults and works towards what comes after death; and the disabled person is one who follows his own whims and asks God to grant whatever he wishes for.

’ ﴿292﴾

Guiding people to the steps of true faith that the Envoy (cpth) showed to his noble companions: steps which were derived from the Book of God. When a person’s heart begins to sense the joy of faith they will definitely follow God’s Order and be self-disciplined so as not to commit sins. God mentioned this in His noble Saying, ‘

And whoever believes in God, will have his heart guided by Him.

’ ﴿293﴾

Revering God’s Envoy (cpth), glorifying him, and demonstrating the eminent position in which Al’lah holds him; then guiding people towards the way of his love (cpth) and revealing what benefits come from loving that pure, virtuous spirit, are twofold: man will enter into Al’lah’s Presence through him; and if a man’s spirit is joined to the Envoy (cpth) through the perfection which comes to him from God, he will be the one to benefit, according to the Almighty’s Saying, ‘

So those who believe in him, honour him, help him, and follow the light sent down through him, will be the ones to gain.

’ ﴿294﴾

The years that this pure man spent striving and seeking closeness to Al’lah were of the greatest benefit. And through this closeness to God he achieved great prominence and fulfillment; he brought about wonderful things, undertook work that was full of bitter conflict, and made great humane sacrifices. So his life was the greatest example of perfect behaviour, in that he supported what is right through the unequalled heroic deeds that he did to defeat and destroy all falsehood.

Mohammad Amin devoted his valuable life to the service of mankind. He fought against the passing of time and radiated light as did the sun in the sky. At his hands, the dark, shadowy Damascus nights seemed as bright as day because of the glittering light of his works and the blessed grace brought by his sacrifices. He worked tirelessly, by night and by day, taking little time to rest. He rarely closed his eyes except to take short naps as his over-riding driving force was to save his human brethren who were mired in spiritual sorrow and pain. He gave no thought to the risks and dangers he faced, knowing that he might be punished or even put to death for his humane actions and deeds. He made many concessions and paid much money in the service of God, and despite his previous wealth, many times he became penniless. Due to Mohammad Amin’s unique virtue it is no wonder that God chose to reveal to him that clear revelation one divine night so that he could witness the Realm of God and his spirit could rise to the sacred lofty worlds of Mohammad (cpth) which were prepared for him because of his truthfulness, endeavours and great sacrifice undertaken to bring the Word of God to mankind. Similarly, anyone who does their utmost to follow this example and is honest in their love and their quest for God and the Envoy (cpth), will find the door open for them along with all their comrades, if they too choose to follow this path.

Joining the Highest Comrade – the Death of Mohammad Amin

In this wonderful way, Mohammad Amin spent a beneficial life, brimming with the knowledge of God, that makes the heart feel secure, and without which humankind will never achieve true happiness. He was like a lamp that lit generations on their path towards achieving bliss through the Book of God (the Qur’an), and the light that guided mankind to great joy, fulfillment, integrity, and the virtuous life that comes only from knowing God. He carried out this unique work until he left this world to join Al’lah, man’s Highest Comrade, during the first days of

Rabi’ al-Thani

in the year 1384 A.H. (1964 A.D.). He was buried in the cemetery of God’s Prophet,

Dhi al-Kifl

, in

the al- Salhiyeh

district of Damascus.

God says, ‘

Who speaks better than someone who calls people to God, does good deeds, and says, “I am of the Muslims [who submitted to God].

” ’ ﴿295﴾

chapters.title: A Glimpse into the Life of the Researcher & Islamic Scholar
chapters.html:
Prof. A. K. Yahya Alias Al-Dayrani

Verifier & Publisher of Books of the Humane Scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho (His soul has been sanctified by Al’lah)

The birth of Abdul-Kadir al-Dayrani took place on 24 July 1934, and he was most fortunate that this momentous occasion occurred in the Damascus house of his father, a great scholar, Sheikh Mohammad al-Dayrani (God has mercy upon him), a disciple of the great Sheikh Badrud-Deen al-Hassani al-Hussaini (God has mercy upon him), who was one of the great scholars of Hadith in Damascus. It was at his hands, too, that Professor Abdul-Kadir received an ethical education during which he gained a great amount of knowledge and learning.

He was so eager in his acquisition for knowledge that during his youth he assiduously read every one of his father’s books. Before completing his secondary education, he met the scholar, Mohammad Amin Sheikho (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah), and was astonished at the scholar’s knowledge of the greatest Godly Sciences. He then followed him like his shadow for nine years, throughout which he too was educated as a scholar. These were years abundant with information and a time when great scientific discoveries came to the fore.

He finished his secondary education and started university where he gained ten university diplomas.

Prof. Abdul-Kadir said, ‘I gained no real knowledge whilst acquiring these diplomas; rather, I learnt everything from my guide, the great scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho. I have a diploma in Arabic literature, but it has never been of any benefit to me in philology or in understanding the meanings of language. I know the language and its meanings directly from the words of the scholar, and the same can be said of my learning of other sciences. ‘All the information contained in the books that I have published is derived solely from the scholar’s scientific studies, and includes facts which have astonished every philosopher and scientist.

I have received certain great discoveries and proven facts directly from the great scholar himself; I have published them literally, as they are Godly Revelations that could not be acquired through the usual teaching of human science, even if the whole of humanity came together to collaborate to assist one another. They form a tangible and actual challenge which has diminished the sciences as known to humankind.

‘Some of these facts came to light and then brought enlightenment to many; for example, the operation of cupping ﴿296﴾

which far surpassed accepted medical practice when results showed that it cured diseases that had been considered incurable by Arabic, Roman and Greek medicine for thousands of years. This practice has since come to the notice of millions of people who have applied cupping, and therefore, it is considered a miracle of the present age.

‘Equal to this in importance is the previously unknown secret of mentioning Al’lah’s Name aloud over animal carcasses while they are being slaughtered. This was discovered by the great humane scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho, and since then has been a blessing for both the cattle slaughtered in this way and the people who consume the meat.

‘In addition, there is all that he revealed in the field of physics, such as his discovery of the true sources of spring water, an issue which no-one had been aware of in earlier times.

‘Besides this are the great Qur’anic sciences, such as the revelation of the significance of the letters with which some Fortresses begin, his remarkable explanation of the Introduction al- Fatiha and of the meanings enclosed within the verse, ‘

Praise is to God, the Provider of the worlds

’, and further, the meanings of each verse of the Holy Qur’an (Al’lah’s Saying). There are, too, other sciences instituted by the scholar which contain facts not brought to light by anyone before him, or indeed, after him. ‘I welcome any discussion about these sciences: an impartial, scientific, open and pragmatic discussion, devoid of emotion, in search of the absolute truth untainted by any dispute, fraudulent practice or error.’

Professor Abdul-Kadir compiled numerous collections of works through the Qur’anic lessons of his guide, the humane scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho, and he imbibed much knowledge from the wellspring of his scientific teaching. The renown of the scholar had spread far and wide and he had heard of the scholar’s deeds from those who had witnessed them, just as he had observed many of them for himself.

When he devoted himself to guidance and the call to Al’lah, he collected, checked and examined the information and knowledge he had received from his scholar, and published these collections so that their benefits might spread all over the world, at a time when mankind is in great need of such knowledge.

Prof. Abdul-Kadir al-Dayrani has checked and verified more than fifty-five books, and his name has become widely known as being associated with the name of the great humane scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah).

He undertook unique modern scientific research on the medical procedure of cupping which the scholar had taught to his disciples who followed the holy prophetic tradition. Furthermore, he became the head of the Syrian medical team which carried out a modern scientific study of the process of cupping, wherein all the essential requirements of research and the application of the rules of cupping were fulfilled under his authority and with his guidance and consultation at every step.

The method and results of this study have been spread widely around the world so that many Eastern and Western hospitals have acknowledged its efficacy and adopted it as part of their medical practice. Since then it has become discussed extensively because of the astonishing cures that have been achieved by virtue of its application.

Prof. al-Dayrani also carried out further scientific research to prove the wisdom behind uttering the words, ‘In the Name of God, Al’lah is Greater’ over cattle when slaughtering them.

This was an astounding modern medical method based on the tests of great medical scholars and through which it was confirmed that mentioning the Name of Al’lah results in purifying the cattle’s meat from microbes, saving it from the pain of slaughter, and curing it from certain previously incurable dangerous diseases such as mad cow disease and bird flu, which would be harmful to the consumer. This was a subject which had been elucidated by the scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) through his Qur’anic teaching to his disciples.

Damascus, 4 September 2007

chapters.title: Excerpts from the Sciences of the Humane Scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho (His soul has been sanctified by Al’lah)
chapters.html:
The research and fields of thinking of the scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho cannot be written down in any specific sequence for the purposes of study; indeed, this document is simply to draw attention to the knowledge of the Holy Qur’an that he offered and revealed to humanity.

Many venerable scholars have discussed him at length and praised his knowledge, his deep insight into the Holy Qur’an and his great understanding of it.

They found truth and faithfulness in his mission, and found that it gathers all humankind under the banner of the Holy Qur’an and the sacred Sun’na of God’s noble Envoy (cpth), so that all the hateful sectarian disputes destroying the religion of our master Mohammad (cpth) will be driven away by this guidance.

This sectarianism is no longer a faithful adherence to the words and meaning implicit in the Holy Qur’an but has been diminished by many who are merely following in the footsteps of their forefathers and their misguided beliefs.

Excerpts from the Sciences of the Humane Scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho (His soul has been sanctified by Al’lah)

The scope of endless knowledge of the venerable humane scholar Mohammad Amin Sheikho (his soul has been sanctified by Al’lah) was such that he filled all the heavens with boundless Quranic scientific learning: a level of learning which has inspired awe in man, prompting him to bow in homage, and to glorify and revere the meanings of the Holy Qur’an.
